# Module 13: Redis with Node.js & NestJS

Module 1 (section 1.12) gave you a minimal `RedisModule` with a single `REDIS_CLIENT`. This module turns it into something you would be comfortable shipping: validated configuration, several named clients (cache, queue, subscriber), explicit connection lifecycle, sane timeouts, graceful shutdown, health checks, and a real test strategy. Names stay consistent with Module 1: `REDIS_CLIENT`, `redis.constants.ts`, `RedisKeys`.

---

## 13.1 Definition and why this matters

**Definition.** A Redis client library is the code that opens TCP (optionally TLS) connections to Redis, encodes commands into RESP, decodes replies, and manages connection state: reconnects, offline queueing, pipelining, pub/sub mode, and so on. In NestJS you additionally wrap the client in a provider so it can be injected, configured, started, health-checked, and stopped by the framework.

**Why a "production-grade" module is needed.** The three-line `new Redis(url)` works until:

| Failure scenario | What happens with a naive client |
|---|---|
| Redis restarts during a deploy | Commands queue in memory unboundedly, or throw `MaxRetriesPerRequestError` at random places |
| Redis is unreachable at boot | App starts "healthy", every request fails; or the app never starts |
| `SIGTERM` from Docker/PM2 | Process exits with in-flight commands lost, sockets leaked, BullMQ jobs stalled |
| Wrong `REDIS_URL` typo in prod | Discovered at 3 AM when the first request hits |
| One client used for cache **and** BullMQ **and** pub/sub | A blocking `BRPOPLPUSH`/subscriber mode starves or breaks everything else |
| Unit tests | Need a running Redis, so they are slow and flaky |

---

## 13.2 Installing Redis locally

### Windows

Redis does not officially support native Windows. Use one of:

| Option | Command / steps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Docker Desktop** (recommended if you already use Docker) | `docker run -d --name redis -p 6379:6379 redis:8.2` | Uses WSL2 backend. Simple, matches production image. |
| **WSL2 + Ubuntu** | `wsl --install -d Ubuntu`, then follow the Ubuntu steps below inside the distro | Port 6379 inside WSL2 is reachable from Windows as `localhost:6379` with default mirrored/localhost forwarding. |
| Memurai / unofficial ports | Not recommended | Different codebase, version lag, behaviour differences. |

### macOS

```bash
brew install redis          # installs the current Homebrew redis formula
brew services start redis   # runs as a launchd service
redis-cli ping              # PONG
```

### Ubuntu (quick dev install)

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y redis-server   # distro version may be older than 8.x
redis-server --version
```

For the current 8.x release on Ubuntu use the official `packages.redis.io` repository (full steps in Module 15, section 15.2). For local development, Docker gives you an exact version pin and is usually the better choice.

### Docker run (any OS)

```bash
docker run -d --name redis-dev \
  -p 127.0.0.1:6379:6379 \
  -v redis-dev-data:/data \
  redis:8.2 \
  redis-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy noeviction

docker exec -it redis-dev redis-cli ping
# PONG
docker logs redis-dev --tail 5
# ... Ready to accept connections tcp
```

Binding to `127.0.0.1` on the host matters: Docker-published ports bypass UFW on Linux, so `-p 6379:6379` on a VPS exposes Redis to the internet.

---

## 13.3 Connecting with ioredis

```bash
npm i ioredis
```

```ts
// connect-ioredis.ts — run: npx tsx connect-ioredis.ts
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const redis = new Redis({
    host: '127.0.0.1',
    port: 6379,
    // username/password only when ACLs are enabled
    connectionName: 'demo-script',       // shows up in CLIENT LIST name=
    connectTimeout: 5_000,               // TCP connect timeout in ms
    commandTimeout: 2_000,               // per-command timeout in ms
    maxRetriesPerRequest: 3,
    lazyConnect: false,                  // connect immediately (default)
  });

  redis.on('error', (e) => console.error('redis error:', e.message));

  console.log(await redis.set('hello', 'world', 'EX', 60)); // OK
  console.log(await redis.get('hello'));                    // world

  // Pipeline: one round trip, results are [error, value] tuples
  const results = await redis.pipeline().incr('c').incr('c').get('c').exec();
  console.log(results); // [[null,1],[null,2],[null,'2']]

  // Transaction (MULTI/EXEC)
  const tx = await redis.multi().set('a', '1').incr('a').exec();
  console.log(tx);      // [[null,'OK'],[null,2]]

  await redis.quit();   // graceful close
}
main().catch((e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });
```

Key ioredis facts:

- It **auto-connects** in the constructor. With `lazyConnect: true` it connects on the first command (or an explicit `connect()`).
- Commands issued while disconnected go into the **offline queue** (`enableOfflineQueue: true` by default).
- Pipelines and `multi()` return `[error, result]` pairs; a failed command inside does not throw from `exec()`. You must inspect each tuple.
- `redis.duplicate()` creates a new connection with the same options. You need it for subscribers and blocking commands.

## 13.4 Connecting with node-redis (v5)

```bash
npm i redis
```

```ts
// connect-node-redis.ts
import { createClient } from 'redis';

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const client = createClient({
    url: 'redis://127.0.0.1:6379',
    name: 'demo-script',                 // CLIENT SETNAME
    socket: {
      connectTimeout: 5_000,
      // Return a number (ms) to retry, or an Error to stop retrying
      reconnectStrategy: (retries: number) => Math.min(retries * 200, 5_000),
    },
  });

  // MANDATORY: without an 'error' listener, an error event crashes the process
  client.on('error', (err) => console.error('redis error:', err.message));
  client.on('ready', () => console.log('ready'));

  await client.connect();                // explicit; ioredis does not need this

  await client.set('hello', 'world', { EX: 60 });
  console.log(await client.get('hello')); // world

  // Multi-command
  const res = await client.multi().incr('c').get('c').exec();
  console.log(res); // [1, '1']

  await client.close();                  // v5: graceful close (quit() is deprecated)
}
main().catch(console.error);
```

Notes for v5:

- Graceful shutdown is `close()`, forced shutdown is `destroy()`. The older `quit()` and `disconnect()` are deprecated aliases in v5.
- Commands issued in the same event-loop tick are automatically pipelined.
- Redis modules (JSON, Search, Bloom, TimeSeries) have typed APIs, for example `client.json.set(...)`.
- RESP3 and client-side caching are opt-in (`RESP: 3`, `clientSideCache`); treat these as advanced features and test them before adopting.
- Use `client.duplicate()` for a dedicated subscriber connection.

## 13.5 Choosing between ioredis and node-redis

| Criterion | ioredis | node-redis v5 |
|---|---|---|
| BullMQ compatibility | **Required** (BullMQ is built on ioredis) | Cannot be passed to BullMQ |
| API style | Positional args: `set(k, v, 'EX', 60)` | Options object: `set(k, v, { EX: 60 })` |
| Connect model | Auto-connect, offline queue on | Explicit `connect()`; offline queue configurable |
| Sentinel / Cluster | Mature, battle-tested | Supported |
| Module commands (JSON, Search) | Via `call()` or third-party typings | First-class typed |
| Per-command timeout | `commandTimeout` | Use `AbortSignal` / `commandOptions` (verify against your installed minor version) |
| Maintenance model | Maintained, slower feature pace | Primary client of Redis Inc., gets new features first |

**Decision rule for your stack (NestJS + BullMQ):** use **ioredis everywhere**. One library, one set of reconnection semantics, one mock strategy. Pick node-redis only for a service that does not use BullMQ and leans on Redis 8 JSON/Search or client-side caching. Mixing both in one codebase is allowed but doubles the operational surface; do it deliberately.

---

## 13.6 Environment-based configuration with validation

Fail at boot, not at 3 AM. Validate environment variables before any provider is constructed. Zod gives typed output with minimal ceremony.

```bash
npm i @nestjs/config zod
```

```ts
// src/config/env.schema.ts
import { z } from 'zod';

const bool = z
  .enum(['true', 'false', '1', '0'])
  .transform((v) => v === 'true' || v === '1');

export const envSchema = z.object({
  NODE_ENV: z.enum(['development', 'test', 'production']).default('development'),
  APP_NAME: z.string().min(1).default('api'),

  // One URL per logical client. rediss:// means TLS.
  REDIS_URL: z.string().url().refine((u) => /^rediss?:\/\//.test(u), 'must start with redis:// or rediss://'),
  REDIS_QUEUE_URL: z.string().url().optional(),   // falls back to REDIS_URL

  REDIS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS: z.coerce.number().int().positive().default(5_000),
  REDIS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS: z.coerce.number().int().positive().default(2_000),
  REDIS_MAX_RETRIES_PER_REQUEST: z.coerce.number().int().min(0).default(3),
  REDIS_RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS: z.coerce.number().int().positive().default(5_000),
  REDIS_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED: bool.default('true'),
  REDIS_KEY_PREFIX: z.string().default(''),
});

export type Env = z.infer<typeof envSchema>;

export function validateEnv(raw: Record<string, unknown>): Env {
  const parsed = envSchema.safeParse(raw);
  if (!parsed.success) {
    const msg = parsed.error.issues
      .map((i) => `${i.path.join('.')}: ${i.message}`)
      .join('; ');
    throw new Error(`Invalid environment: ${msg}`);
  }
  return parsed.data;
}
```

```ts
// src/app.module.ts (excerpt)
import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ConfigModule } from '@nestjs/config';
import { validateEnv } from './config/env.schema';
import { AppRedisModule } from './redis/app-redis.module';

@Module({
  imports: [
    ConfigModule.forRoot({
      isGlobal: true,
      cache: true,
      validate: validateEnv, // runs once at bootstrap; throws -> process exits
    }),
    AppRedisModule,
  ],
})
export class AppModule {}
```

Alternatives: `class-validator` with `plainToInstance` + `validateSync` (idiomatic if you already use DTOs), or Joi via `validationSchema` (the original Nest docs example). All three do the same job: the important part is that **validation happens in `ConfigModule.forRoot` and aborts startup**.

Example `.env`:

```bash
NODE_ENV=production
REDIS_URL=rediss://app:s3cret@redis.internal:6379/0
REDIS_QUEUE_URL=rediss://queue:s3cret2@redis.internal:6379/1
REDIS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS=1500
```

Terminal when invalid:

```text
$ node dist/main.js
Error: Invalid environment: REDIS_URL: Required
```

---

## 13.7 Production NestJS RedisModule

### Design goals

1. **Dynamic module** with `forRootAsync` so options come from `ConfigService`.
2. **Named clients** declared up front (`default`, `cache`, `queue`, `subscriber`). Nest providers must be known when the module is built, so names are static; connection options are resolved asynchronously.
3. Backwards compatible with Module 1: `REDIS_CLIENT` is still the default client token.
4. One place that owns lifecycle: logging, events, shutdown.

### Why separate clients?

```text
                    +-------------------------+
 Nest providers --> | cache client            |  fail fast, short timeouts, maybe eviction-tolerant
                    +-------------------------+
                    +-------------------------+
 BullMQ ----------> | queue client            |  maxRetriesPerRequest: null, noeviction DB
                    +-------------------------+
                    +-------------------------+
 Pub/Sub ---------> | subscriber client       |  in subscriber mode: only (P|S)SUBSCRIBE-family commands allowed
                    +-------------------------+
```

A connection in subscriber mode cannot run `GET`/`SET`. BullMQ workers require `maxRetriesPerRequest: null` on blocking connections, but you want the opposite (fail fast) for cache reads in an HTTP request path. Separate clients let each have its own policy and also make `CLIENT LIST` readable (`name=api:cache`, `name=api:queue`).

### File: `redis.constants.ts` (extends Module 1)

```ts
// src/redis/redis.constants.ts
export const REDIS_CLIENT = Symbol('REDIS_CLIENT');        // default client (unchanged from Module 1)
export const REDIS_MODULE_OPTIONS = Symbol('REDIS_MODULE_OPTIONS');
export const REDIS_REGISTRY = Symbol('REDIS_REGISTRY');

export const DEFAULT_CLIENT_NAME = 'default';

/** Deterministic token per client name; Symbol.for gives the same symbol everywhere. */
export function getRedisToken(name: string = DEFAULT_CLIENT_NAME): symbol {
  return name === DEFAULT_CLIENT_NAME ? REDIS_CLIENT : Symbol.for(`REDIS_CLIENT:${name}`);
}
```

### File: `redis.interfaces.ts`

```ts
// src/redis/redis.interfaces.ts
import { ModuleMetadata } from '@nestjs/common';
import type { Redis, RedisOptions } from 'ioredis';

export interface NamedRedisOptions {
  url: string;
  /** Extra ioredis options; these win over module defaults. */
  options?: RedisOptions;
}

export interface RedisModuleOptions {
  clients: Record<string, NamedRedisOptions>;
}

export interface RedisModuleAsyncOptions extends Pick<ModuleMetadata, 'imports'> {
  /** The client names you will inject. Must be static. */
  names: string[];
  inject?: any[];
  useFactory: (...args: any[]) => RedisModuleOptions | Promise<RedisModuleOptions>;
}

export type RedisRegistry = Map<string, Redis>;
```

### File: `redis.decorators.ts`

```ts
// src/redis/redis.decorators.ts
import { Inject } from '@nestjs/common';
import { getRedisToken } from './redis.constants';

/** @InjectRedis() -> default client, @InjectRedis('cache') -> named client */
export const InjectRedis = (name?: string): ParameterDecorator => Inject(getRedisToken(name));
```

### File: `redis.module.ts`

```ts
// src/redis/redis.module.ts
import {
  DynamicModule, Global, Inject, Logger, Module, OnApplicationShutdown, Provider,
} from '@nestjs/common';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import {
  REDIS_MODULE_OPTIONS, REDIS_REGISTRY, getRedisToken,
} from './redis.constants';
import {
  RedisModuleAsyncOptions, RedisModuleOptions, RedisRegistry,
} from './redis.interfaces';

@Global()
@Module({})
export class RedisModule implements OnApplicationShutdown {
  private static readonly logger = new Logger('Redis');

  constructor(@Inject(REDIS_REGISTRY) private readonly registry: RedisRegistry) {}

  static forRootAsync(opts: RedisModuleAsyncOptions): DynamicModule {
    const optionsProvider: Provider = {
      provide: REDIS_MODULE_OPTIONS,
      inject: opts.inject ?? [],
      useFactory: opts.useFactory,
    };

    const registryProvider: Provider = {
      provide: REDIS_REGISTRY,
      useValue: new Map<string, Redis>() as RedisRegistry,
    };

    const clientProviders: Provider[] = opts.names.map((name) => ({
      provide: getRedisToken(name),
      inject: [REDIS_MODULE_OPTIONS, REDIS_REGISTRY],
      useFactory: (cfg: RedisModuleOptions, registry: RedisRegistry): Redis => {
        const entry = cfg.clients[name];
        if (!entry) {
          throw new Error(`Redis client "${name}" is declared but has no configuration`);
        }
        const client = new Redis(entry.url, {
          // Defaults that can be overridden per client
          connectionName: name,
          connectTimeout: 5_000,
          commandTimeout: 2_000,
          maxRetriesPerRequest: 3,
          enableOfflineQueue: true,
          enableReadyCheck: true,
          retryStrategy: (times: number) => Math.min(100 * 2 ** Math.min(times, 6), 5_000),
          ...entry.options,
        });
        RedisModule.attachListeners(name, client);
        registry.set(name, client);
        return client;
      },
    }));

    return {
      module: RedisModule,
      imports: opts.imports ?? [],
      providers: [optionsProvider, registryProvider, ...clientProviders],
      exports: [REDIS_REGISTRY, ...opts.names.map(getRedisToken)],
    };
  }

  private static attachListeners(name: string, client: Redis): void {
    const log = RedisModule.logger;
    client.on('connect', () => log.log(`[${name}] TCP connected`));
    client.on('ready', () => log.log(`[${name}] ready`));
    client.on('error', (err) => log.error(`[${name}] ${err.message}`));
    client.on('close', () => log.warn(`[${name}] connection closed`));
    client.on('reconnecting', (ms: number) => log.warn(`[${name}] reconnecting in ${ms}ms`));
    client.on('end', () => log.warn(`[${name}] ended (no more reconnects)`));
  }

  /** Called after SIGTERM/SIGINT once app.enableShutdownHooks() is active. */
  async onApplicationShutdown(signal?: string): Promise<void> {
    RedisModule.logger.log(`Shutting down Redis clients (signal=${signal ?? 'none'})`);
    await Promise.all(
      [...this.registry.entries()].map(async ([name, client]) => {
        if (client.status === 'end') return;
        try {
          await Promise.race([
            client.quit(),                                  // graceful: flush pending, send QUIT
            new Promise((_, rej) => setTimeout(() => rej(new Error('quit timeout')), 5_000)),
          ]);
        } catch (err) {
          RedisModule.logger.warn(`[${name}] quit failed (${(err as Error).message}), forcing disconnect`);
          client.disconnect();                               // hard close, drops pending commands
        }
      }),
    );
  }
}
```

### File: `app-redis.module.ts` — wiring from validated config

```ts
// src/redis/app-redis.module.ts
import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
import { RedisModule } from './redis.module';
import type { Env } from '../config/env.schema';

@Module({
  imports: [
    RedisModule.forRootAsync({
      names: ['default', 'cache', 'queue', 'subscriber'],
      inject: [ConfigService],
      useFactory: (config: ConfigService<Env, true>) => {
        const appName = config.get('APP_NAME', { infer: true });
        const url = config.get('REDIS_URL', { infer: true });
        const queueUrl = config.get('REDIS_QUEUE_URL', { infer: true }) ?? url;
        const commandTimeout = config.get('REDIS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS', { infer: true });
        const connectTimeout = config.get('REDIS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS', { infer: true });
        const maxDelay = config.get('REDIS_RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS', { infer: true });
        const rejectUnauthorized = config.get('REDIS_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED', { infer: true });
        const tls = url.startsWith('rediss://') ? { rejectUnauthorized } : undefined;

        const backoff = (times: number) => Math.min(100 * 2 ** Math.min(times, 6), maxDelay);

        return {
          clients: {
            // General purpose (Module 1 compatibility)
            default: { url, options: { connectionName: `${appName}:default`, connectTimeout, commandTimeout, tls } },

            // HTTP-path cache: fail fast, never block a request for long
            cache: {
              url,
              options: {
                connectionName: `${appName}:cache`,
                connectTimeout,
                commandTimeout,
                maxRetriesPerRequest: 1,
                retryStrategy: backoff,
                tls,
              },
            },

            // BullMQ: blocking commands, must not time out or limit retries
            queue: {
              url: queueUrl,
              options: {
                connectionName: `${appName}:queue`,
                connectTimeout,
                commandTimeout: undefined,
                maxRetriesPerRequest: null,
                enableOfflineQueue: true,
                retryStrategy: backoff,
                tls,
              },
            },

            // Pub/Sub receiver: lazy so it only connects when someone subscribes
            subscriber: {
              url,
              options: {
                connectionName: `${appName}:sub`,
                connectTimeout,
                commandTimeout: undefined,       // idle by design; no replies expected
                lazyConnect: true,
                maxRetriesPerRequest: null,
                autoResubscribe: true,           // re-SUBSCRIBE after reconnect (ioredis default)
                retryStrategy: backoff,
                tls,
              },
            },
          },
        };
      },
    }),
  ],
  exports: [RedisModule],
})
export class AppRedisModule {}
```

### Using the clients (DI)

```ts
// src/cache/product-cache.service.ts
import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import type { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { InjectRedis } from '../redis/redis.decorators';
import { RedisKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

@Injectable()
export class ProductCacheService {
  constructor(@InjectRedis('cache') private readonly redis: Redis) {}

  async get<T>(id: string): Promise<T | null> {
    try {
      const raw = await this.redis.get(RedisKeys.product(id));
      return raw ? (JSON.parse(raw) as T) : null;
    } catch {
      return null; // cache is an optimization: degrade to the database
    }
  }

  async set(id: string, value: unknown, ttlSec = 300): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await this.redis.set(RedisKeys.product(id), JSON.stringify(value), 'EX', ttlSec);
    } catch {
      /* swallow: never fail a request because the cache is down */
    }
  }
}
```

Extend `RedisKeys` from Module 1 (same file, additive):

```ts
// src/redis/redis-keys.ts
const APP = 'shop';
export const RedisKeys = {
  user: (id: string | number) => `${APP}:user:${id}`,
  session: (sid: string) => `${APP}:session:${sid}`,
  pageViews: (path: string) => `${APP}:stats:views:${path}`,
  product: (id: string | number) => `${APP}:product:${id}`,
  rateLimit: (ip: string, route: string) => `${APP}:rl:${route}:${ip}`,
  channel: { events: `${APP}:ch:events` },
} as const;
```

Pub/Sub with a dedicated subscriber and the default client as publisher:

```ts
// src/events/events.service.ts
import { Injectable, OnModuleInit } from '@nestjs/common';
import type { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { InjectRedis } from '../redis/redis.decorators';
import { RedisKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

@Injectable()
export class EventsService implements OnModuleInit {
  constructor(
    @InjectRedis() private readonly publisher: Redis,
    @InjectRedis('subscriber') private readonly subscriber: Redis,
  ) {}

  async onModuleInit(): Promise<void> {
    await this.subscriber.subscribe(RedisKeys.channel.events);
    this.subscriber.on('message', (channel, message) => {
      // handle(JSON.parse(message))
    });
  }

  publish(payload: unknown): Promise<number> {
    // returns the number of subscribers that received it
    return this.publisher.publish(RedisKeys.channel.events, JSON.stringify(payload));
  }
}
```

Pub/Sub is fire-and-forget: a subscriber that is disconnected misses messages. For durable delivery use Streams (Module covering Streams) or BullMQ.

Feeding BullMQ with the queue client's options:

```ts
// src/queues/queues.module.ts
import { BullModule } from '@nestjs/bullmq';
import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';

@Module({
  imports: [
    BullModule.forRootAsync({
      inject: [ConfigService],
      useFactory: (config: ConfigService) => {
        const u = new URL(config.getOrThrow<string>('REDIS_QUEUE_URL'));
        return {
          connection: {
            host: u.hostname,
            port: Number(u.port || 6379),
            username: u.username ? decodeURIComponent(u.username) : undefined,
            password: u.password ? decodeURIComponent(u.password) : undefined,
            maxRetriesPerRequest: null,        // required for Workers
            ...(u.protocol === 'rediss:' ? { tls: {} } : {}),
          },
        };
      },
    }),
    BullModule.registerQueue({ name: 'emails' }),
  ],
})
export class QueuesModule {}
```

Passing connection **options** (not a shared instance) lets BullMQ create and own the connections it needs (it duplicates for blocking and event connections). Reusing the `queue` client instance for non-BullMQ work is still fine, but do not hand your HTTP cache client to BullMQ.


---

## 13.8 Connection lifecycle and events

### ioredis connection states

```text
        new Redis()
            |
         "wait" (only if lazyConnect)
            |
        "connecting" --> event: connect  (TCP up)
            |
        "connect"    --> ready check (INFO) / AUTH / SELECT / CLIENT SETNAME
            |
         "ready"     --> event: ready  (offline queue flushed here)
            |
   socket drops -->  event: close
            |
      "reconnecting" --> event: reconnecting(delayMs)  ... loop via retryStrategy
            |
   retryStrategy returns non-number (or quit/disconnect called)
            |
         "end"       --> event: end  (terminal; client unusable)
```

| Event | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `connect` | TCP socket established | Log only. Not usable yet. |
| `ready` | Auth, SELECT, ready-check finished; queued commands sent | Mark healthy, log. |
| `error` | Connection or protocol error. **Without a listener ioredis prints "Unhandled error event" but does not crash; node-redis can throw.** | Log with rate limiting. Do not exit. |
| `close` | Socket closed | Warn. Reconnect follows automatically. |
| `reconnecting` | Waiting `delay` ms before next attempt | Warn. |
| `end` | No more reconnects | Alert: the client is dead; restart pod/process or recreate the client. |

Useful property: `client.status` is one of `wait | connecting | connect | ready | reconnecting | end | close`. Use `status === 'ready'` in health checks.

### node-redis v5 equivalents

`connect`, `ready`, `end`, `error`, `reconnecting`. The `error` listener is mandatory. `client.isReady` and `client.isOpen` are the status flags.

### Hook failures into the Nest lifecycle

Wait for a usable connection **before** accepting traffic:

```ts
// src/redis/redis-ready.provider.ts
import { Provider } from '@nestjs/common';
import type { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { getRedisToken } from './redis.constants';

/** Blocks bootstrap until the client is ready, or fails after timeoutMs. */
export const waitForRedis = (name: string, timeoutMs = 10_000): Provider => ({
  provide: Symbol.for(`REDIS_READY:${name}`),
  inject: [getRedisToken(name)],
  useFactory: async (client: Redis) => {
    if (client.status === 'ready') return true;
    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      const t = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`Redis "${name}" not ready in ${timeoutMs}ms`)), timeoutMs);
      client.once('ready', () => { clearTimeout(t); resolve(); });
    });
    return true;
  },
});
```

Whether to crash at boot when Redis is down is a policy decision. For a hard dependency (BullMQ producer, sessions) fail fast so the orchestrator restarts you and the load balancer never routes to a broken pod. For a soft dependency (cache) start anyway and degrade.

---

## 13.9 Reconnection strategy

ioredis calls `retryStrategy(times)` after every failed connect; the return value is the delay in ms before the next attempt. Returning a non-number stops reconnecting (status becomes `end`).

```ts
const retryStrategy = (times: number): number => {
  const base = Math.min(100 * 2 ** times, 5_000);           // exponential, capped at 5s
  const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random() * base * 0.2);     // 20% jitter
  return base + jitter;
};
```

Why jitter? If Redis restarts and 200 pods retry at identical intervals you create a reconnect storm (thundering herd) at each tick.

Related options:

| Option (ioredis) | Default | Purpose and trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| `retryStrategy` | linear `min(times*50, 2000)` | Delay between reconnect attempts |
| `maxRetriesPerRequest` | `20` | A command fails with `MaxRetriesPerRequestError` after this many reconnect attempts. `null` = retry forever (needed for BullMQ workers). Lower = fail fast for HTTP paths. |
| `enableOfflineQueue` | `true` | Buffer commands while not connected. `false` = commands fail immediately when not ready. Unbounded queue can eat memory during long outages. |
| `reconnectOnError(err)` | none | Return `true`/`1`/`2` to reconnect on a specific error. Classic use: `READONLY` after a failover (replica promoted, old master demoted): `err.message.includes('READONLY')`. |
| `autoResubscribe` | `true` | Re-issue SUBSCRIBE after reconnect |
| `autoResendUnfulfilledCommands` | `true` | Resend commands that were in flight when the socket dropped. **Danger:** non-idempotent commands (`INCR`) can be applied twice if the server executed them but the reply was lost. |
| `enableReadyCheck` | `true` | Wait for the server to finish loading its dataset (`LOADING` state) before `ready` |

node-redis v5: `socket.reconnectStrategy(retries, cause)` returns ms or an `Error` to stop, `disableOfflineQueue: true` fails commands while disconnected, and `commandsQueueMaxLength` bounds the queue.

**Failure scenario:** Redis restarts and loads a 4 GB AOF for 40 s. With `enableReadyCheck: true` the client stays out of `ready` and commands queue (up to `maxRetriesPerRequest` attempts), then fail with a retriable error. With the check off, commands get `-LOADING Redis is loading the dataset in memory`.

---

## 13.10 Connection and command timeouts

| Timeout | Option | Typical value | Protects against |
|---|---|---|---|
| TCP connect | ioredis `connectTimeout`; node-redis `socket.connectTimeout` | 5000 ms | Black-holed network, security group drops |
| Per-command | ioredis `commandTimeout` | 1000–2000 ms for cache | Slow command, Redis blocked by a long Lua script or `KEYS` |
| Socket idle | `socket.timeout` (server-side `timeout`, client `keepAlive`) | keep-alive 10–30 s | Half-open connections behind NAT/LB that silently die |
| Overall HTTP request | NestJS interceptor / `AbortSignal` | 3–10 s | Everything else |

Rules of thumb:

- Cache clients: `commandTimeout` ≈ p99 of your downstream DB query. If Redis cannot answer faster than the database, a cache hit is not a win.
- **Never** set `commandTimeout` on a connection used for blocking commands (`BLPOP`, `BRPOPLPUSH`, `XREAD BLOCK`, BullMQ worker). The command is supposed to wait.
- A timed-out command may **still execute** on the server. Treat timeouts on writes as "unknown outcome", not "failed".
- ioredis `keepAlive` (ms, default `0` meaning the OS default behaviour on initial delay) enables TCP keep-alive; behind AWS NLB/NAT idle timeouts (350 s on NLB, 350 s on NAT gateways) use an explicit value such as `10_000`.

---

## 13.11 Error handling patterns

Common errors and their meaning:

| Error | Cause | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| `ECONNREFUSED` | Redis down, wrong host/port | Retry with backoff; alert if sustained |
| `ETIMEDOUT` / `Command timed out` | Network or slow command | Retry reads; for writes consider idempotency |
| `MaxRetriesPerRequestError` | Offline for more than N attempts | Degrade (cache) or return 503 |
| `NOAUTH Authentication required` / `WRONGPASS` | Missing or wrong credentials | Config bug: fail boot |
| `NOPERM` | ACL forbids the command | Fix ACL, not code |
| `OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'` | `noeviction` and memory full | Alert, free memory, raise limit |
| `LOADING` | Startup dataset load | Retry (ready check handles it) |
| `READONLY You can't write against a read only replica` | Failover happened, you hit a replica | `reconnectOnError` |
| `BUSY Redis is busy running a script` | Long Lua script | Fix script; `SCRIPT KILL` |
| `ERR max number of clients reached` | `maxclients` hit | Fix pool leaks (Module 16, "Too many client connections") |

A small wrapper that separates **optional** (cache) from **required** (queue/session) operations:

```ts
// src/redis/safe-redis.ts
import { Logger } from '@nestjs/common';

const logger = new Logger('SafeRedis');

/** Cache semantics: on any Redis failure return the fallback and log once per call site. */
export async function optional<T>(op: () => Promise<T>, fallback: T, label: string): Promise<T> {
  try {
    return await op();
  } catch (err) {
    logger.warn(`${label} failed, using fallback: ${(err as Error).message}`);
    return fallback;
  }
}
```

For required operations, let the error propagate and map it in an exception filter to `503 Service Unavailable` with `Retry-After`. Do not return 500s with raw Redis messages: they can leak host and key details.

Circuit breaker note: when Redis is hard down and the cache path times out at 2 s on every request, you add 2 s latency to every request. Pair `optional()` with a breaker (for example `opossum`) that short-circuits for 10–30 s after N failures.

---

## 13.12 Graceful shutdown

### Mechanism

```text
 docker stop / pm2 reload / k8s pod termination
        |
     SIGTERM (or SIGINT for PM2)
        |
   Nest (enableShutdownHooks) --> beforeApplicationShutdown -> onModuleDestroy
        |                         -> HTTP server closes (stop accepting, drain)
        |                         -> onApplicationShutdown(signal)  <- RedisModule quits clients here
        v
   process exits 0
        |
   (after grace period: SIGKILL; Docker default 10s, PM2 kill_timeout default 1600ms)
```

```ts
// src/main.ts
import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';

async function bootstrap(): Promise<void> {
  const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule, { bufferLogs: true });
  app.enableShutdownHooks(); // without this, onApplicationShutdown never runs on signals
  await app.listen(process.env.PORT ?? 3000);
}
bootstrap();
```

### `quit()` vs `disconnect()` (ioredis)

| | `quit()` | `disconnect()` |
|---|---|---|
| Sends `QUIT` to server | Yes | No |
| Waits for pending replies | **Yes** (commands already sent get answers) | No, closes socket now |
| Returns | Promise resolving to `'OK'` | `void` |
| Reconnects afterwards | No | No by default (`disconnect(true)` reconnects) |
| Use when | Normal shutdown | Timeout fallback, tests, stuck connections |

node-redis v5: `close()` is graceful, `destroy()` is immediate.

Order of operations matters: stop taking new work (HTTP, BullMQ workers) **first**, then close Redis. For BullMQ call `await worker.close()` in `onModuleDestroy` of the worker class so active jobs finish before the connection disappears. Nest destroys modules in reverse dependency order, but your own `onModuleDestroy` hooks run before `onApplicationShutdown`, which is why Redis is closed in the latter.

Production timing: make `kill_timeout` (PM2) or `stop_grace_period` (Compose) larger than your longest in-flight request or job (for example 30 s).

## 13.13 Health checks with @nestjs/terminus

```bash
npm i @nestjs/terminus
```

Custom indicator (written for `@nestjs/terminus` v11 using `HealthIndicatorService`; on older versions extend `HealthIndicator` instead):

```ts
// src/health/redis.health.ts
import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { HealthIndicatorResult, HealthIndicatorService } from '@nestjs/terminus';
import type { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { InjectRedis } from '../redis/redis.decorators';

@Injectable()
export class RedisHealthIndicator {
  constructor(
    private readonly healthIndicatorService: HealthIndicatorService,
    @InjectRedis('cache') private readonly redis: Redis,
  ) {}

  async isHealthy(key = 'redis', timeoutMs = 1_000): Promise<HealthIndicatorResult> {
    const indicator = this.healthIndicatorService.check(key);

    if (this.redis.status !== 'ready') {
      return indicator.down({ status: this.redis.status });
    }
    try {
      const started = Date.now();
      const reply = await Promise.race([
        this.redis.ping(),
        new Promise<never>((_, rej) => setTimeout(() => rej(new Error('ping timeout')), timeoutMs)),
      ]);
      return indicator.up({ reply, latencyMs: Date.now() - started });
    } catch (err) {
      return indicator.down({ message: (err as Error).message });
    }
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/health/health.controller.ts
import { Controller, Get } from '@nestjs/common';
import { HealthCheck, HealthCheckService } from '@nestjs/terminus';
import { RedisHealthIndicator } from './redis.health';

@Controller('health')
export class HealthController {
  constructor(private readonly health: HealthCheckService, private readonly redis: RedisHealthIndicator) {}

  @Get('ready')               // readiness: should this pod receive traffic?
  @HealthCheck()
  ready() {
    return this.health.check([() => this.redis.isHealthy('redis')]);
  }

  @Get('live')                // liveness: is the process alive? Do NOT include Redis here
  live() {
    return { status: 'ok' };
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/health/health.module.ts
import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { TerminusModule } from '@nestjs/terminus';
import { HealthController } from './health.controller';
import { RedisHealthIndicator } from './redis.health';

@Module({ imports: [TerminusModule], controllers: [HealthController], providers: [RedisHealthIndicator] })
export class HealthModule {}
```

Terminal:

```text
$ curl -s localhost:3000/health/ready
{"status":"ok","info":{"redis":{"status":"up","reply":"PONG","latencyMs":1}},"error":{},"details":{"redis":{"status":"up","reply":"PONG","latencyMs":1}}}

# Redis stopped:
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" localhost:3000/health/ready
503
```

**Do not put Redis in the liveness probe.** If Redis is down and liveness fails, the orchestrator restarts every pod simultaneously, adding a reconnect storm to an incident. Readiness should fail (stop routing traffic) only if Redis is a hard dependency for the endpoint.

## 13.14 Unit testing and mocking Redis

### Strategy

```text
 Test pyramid for Redis code
   many  : unit tests, fake Redis (jest mock) — logic around Redis, key names, error fallback
   some  : integration tests, real Redis (Testcontainers) — Lua scripts, TTL, transactions, BullMQ
   few   : e2e with whole app + container
```

### Jest mock via DI (preferred)

Because the client is injected through `@InjectRedis()`, tests substitute the provider token:

```ts
// src/cache/product-cache.service.spec.ts
import { Test } from '@nestjs/testing';
import { getRedisToken } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { ProductCacheService } from './product-cache.service';

describe('ProductCacheService', () => {
  let service: ProductCacheService;
  const redis = { get: jest.fn(), set: jest.fn() };

  beforeEach(async () => {
    jest.resetAllMocks();
    const moduleRef = await Test.createTestingModule({
      providers: [
        ProductCacheService,
        { provide: getRedisToken('cache'), useValue: redis },
      ],
    }).compile();
    service = moduleRef.get(ProductCacheService);
  });

  it('returns parsed JSON on hit', async () => {
    redis.get.mockResolvedValue(JSON.stringify({ id: '7', name: 'Mug' }));
    await expect(service.get('7')).resolves.toEqual({ id: '7', name: 'Mug' });
    expect(redis.get).toHaveBeenCalledWith('shop:product:7');
  });

  it('returns null on miss', async () => {
    redis.get.mockResolvedValue(null);
    await expect(service.get('7')).resolves.toBeNull();
  });

  it('degrades to null when Redis errors', async () => {
    redis.get.mockRejectedValue(new Error('ECONNREFUSED'));
    await expect(service.get('7')).resolves.toBeNull();
  });

  it('writes with a TTL', async () => {
    redis.set.mockResolvedValue('OK');
    await service.set('7', { id: '7' }, 60);
    expect(redis.set).toHaveBeenCalledWith('shop:product:7', '{"id":"7"}', 'EX', 60);
  });
});
```

### ioredis-mock and its caveats

`ioredis-mock` implements the Redis API in memory, so you can write `new RedisMock()` and run `set/get/hset/zadd` without a server. Useful for quick tests of simple data-structure code, but:

| Caveat | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Not the real server | Behaviour differences in edge cases (error messages, type coercion, ordering) |
| Lua scripting limited | `eval`/`defineCommand` support is partial; scripts using `redis.call` features may behave differently |
| Streams, modules, newer commands | Coverage varies; Redis 7/8 additions (e.g. hash field expiration, JSON, vector sets) are often missing |
| No memory limits or eviction | You cannot test `maxmemory` behaviour |
| Pub/Sub, blocking commands, keyspace notifications | Timing and semantics differ |
| BullMQ | Not supported reliably; BullMQ relies on Lua scripts and blocking commands |

Rule: use jest mocks for "does my service call Redis correctly and handle errors", ioredis-mock only for trivial structures, and a **real Redis** for anything involving Lua, transactions, expiry timing, or BullMQ.

---

## 13.15 Integration testing with Testcontainers

```bash
npm i -D testcontainers @testcontainers/redis
```

```ts
// test/redis.integration.spec.ts
import { RedisContainer, StartedRedisContainer } from '@testcontainers/redis';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';

describe('Redis integration', () => {
  let container: StartedRedisContainer;
  let redis: Redis;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    container = await new RedisContainer('redis:8.2').start();
    redis = new Redis({ host: container.getHost(), port: container.getPort() });
  }, 60_000);

  afterAll(async () => {
    await redis.quit();
    await container.stop();
  });

  beforeEach(() => redis.flushall());

  it('expires keys', async () => {
    await redis.set('k', 'v', 'PX', 100);
    expect(await redis.get('k')).toBe('v');
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 200));
    expect(await redis.get('k')).toBeNull();
  });

  it('runs a Lua rate limiter atomically', async () => {
    const script = `
      local c = redis.call('INCR', KEYS[1])
      if c == 1 then redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]) end
      return c`;
    const results = await Promise.all(
      Array.from({ length: 50 }, () => redis.eval(script, 1, 'rl:test', 60)),
    );
    expect(Math.max(...(results as number[]))).toBe(50);
  });
});
```

Tips:

- One container per test **file** (or per suite using Jest `globalSetup`), `FLUSHALL` between tests. Starting a container per test is too slow.
- In CI, Docker must be available (GitHub Actions runners have it; for GitLab use docker-in-docker or a service container instead).
- Run with `--runInBand` or one container per worker to avoid cross-test interference.
- Use the same image tag as production.

## 13.16 Recommended folder structure

```text
src/
  config/
    env.schema.ts              # zod schema + validateEnv
  redis/
    redis.constants.ts         # REDIS_CLIENT, getRedisToken
    redis.interfaces.ts
    redis.decorators.ts        # @InjectRedis
    redis.module.ts            # dynamic module, lifecycle
    app-redis.module.ts        # app-specific clients wired from config
    redis-keys.ts              # single source of truth for key names
    safe-redis.ts              # optional() helper
  health/
    health.module.ts
    health.controller.ts
    redis.health.ts
  cache/
    cache.module.ts
    product-cache.service.ts   # feature code depends on @InjectRedis('cache')
  queues/
    queues.module.ts           # BullMQ, own connection options
  main.ts
test/
  redis.integration.spec.ts
```

Rule: feature modules never call `new Redis()`. They inject a named client. Keys are only built via `RedisKeys`. This keeps connection policy, key naming, and tests in three predictable places.

---

## 13.17 Real-world use case

An e-commerce API on 4 PM2 instances: product reads cached on the `cache` client (1 s command timeout, failure falls back to PostgreSQL), invoice emails sent through BullMQ on the `queue` client, and cart-updated events broadcast to WebSocket gateways through Pub/Sub on `default` + `subscriber`. When Redis is restarted for an upgrade, the cache path degrades for 10 s with slightly higher DB load, the queue path buffers (offline queue, retry forever), and readiness probes flip to 503 only on the instances where the `cache` client is not `ready`.

## 13.18 Performance and memory

| Aspect | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Connections per process | A handful (one per role). Do not create a client per request or per service. |
| Pool vs single connection | Redis is single-threaded per command stream; one multiplexed connection with pipelining beats a pool for most workloads. A pool only helps for blocking commands or very large payloads. |
| Auto-pipelining | ioredis `enableAutoPipelining: true` batches commands issued in the same tick. Good throughput win; verify latency impact with your payload sizes. |
| Offline queue | Unbounded memory during outages. Consider `enableOfflineQueue: false` on the cache client. |
| `connectionName` | Free observability: `CLIENT LIST` shows who owns each connection. |
| JSON payloads | `JSON.parse/stringify` cost is on your event loop; for big objects consider caching smaller projections. |

## 13.19 Limitations and alternatives

- Pub/Sub has no persistence; use Streams (consumer groups) or BullMQ for durable messaging.
- Client-side caching and RESP3 are node-redis-first features.
- `@nestjs/cache-manager` with a Redis store is a higher-level option; it hides Redis semantics (TTL units, key patterns, serialization), which can bite during incident debugging. Many teams keep an explicit service as above.
- Community wrappers such as `@liaoliaots/nestjs-redis` provide a ready-made module with similar named-client ideas; building your own is about 150 lines and gives full control.

## 13.20 Common mistakes

1. Using one client for cache, BullMQ and subscriptions.
2. No `error` listener (node-redis crashes; ioredis spams logs).
3. Forgetting `app.enableShutdownHooks()`, so `onApplicationShutdown` is never called.
4. `maxRetriesPerRequest: null` on an HTTP-path client, causing requests to hang for the whole outage.
5. `commandTimeout` on a blocking-command connection.
6. Putting Redis in the liveness probe.
7. Calling `redis.disconnect()` on shutdown, losing in-flight replies.
8. Creating `new Redis()` inside a request handler or per-test without closing it (leaks sockets, Jest does not exit).
9. Treating a timed-out write as "not applied".
10. Mocking Redis with ioredis-mock and trusting it for Lua or BullMQ behaviour.

## 13.21 Interview Q&A

**Q1. Why would you create multiple Redis clients in one NestJS app?**
Different connections need different policies and cannot be shared safely. A subscriber connection is restricted to pub/sub commands, a BullMQ worker needs blocking commands and `maxRetriesPerRequest: null`, and an HTTP cache client should fail fast. Separate clients also make `CLIENT LIST` and metrics attributable.

**Q2. `quit()` vs `disconnect()`?**
`quit()` sends `QUIT` and waits for replies to already-sent commands, so it is the graceful choice. `disconnect()` destroys the socket immediately and drops pending commands; use it only as a timeout fallback.

**Q3. What happens to commands while Redis is down?**
With ioredis and `enableOfflineQueue: true` they are queued and flushed when `ready`, subject to `maxRetriesPerRequest`. With the offline queue disabled they fail immediately. The queue is in process memory, so a long outage plus high throughput can exhaust memory.

**Q4. Why validate environment variables at boot?**
A bad `REDIS_URL` otherwise surfaces only on first use, in production, under load. Failing at bootstrap lets the orchestrator refuse to promote the release.

**Q5. How do you test code that uses Redis?**
Jest mocks via DI for logic and fallback paths, real Redis in Testcontainers for Lua, TTL, transactions and BullMQ. ioredis-mock only for trivial cases because of semantic gaps.

**Q6. Why not include Redis in the liveness probe?**
Liveness restarts the process. A Redis outage would restart all pods, which does not fix Redis and adds a reconnect storm. Use readiness to stop traffic instead.

**Q7. A write timed out. What do you do?**
The outcome is unknown; the server may have executed it. Make writes idempotent (`SET` is, `INCR` is not), use a request ID or Lua script with a dedupe key, and avoid blind retry of non-idempotent commands. Note ioredis `autoResendUnfulfilledCommands` can resend commands after a reconnect.

**Q8. Why jitter in reconnect backoff?**
To prevent synchronized reconnect attempts from many clients after an outage.

## 13.22 Senior / Staff discussion

- **Blast radius of Redis as a shared dependency.** Decide per feature whether Redis is a hard or soft dependency and encode that in code (`optional()` vs required), health checks, and runbooks. Document it in each service's README.
- **Separate Redis instances vs separate logical clients.** Named clients on the same server still share CPU, memory, and `maxmemory-policy`. BullMQ needs `noeviction`; a cache wants `allkeys-lru`/`allkeys-lfu`. If both live on one instance you must choose one policy, which is usually wrong for one of them. Run two instances (or two managed clusters) and point `cache` and `queue` at different URLs; this module already supports that via `REDIS_QUEUE_URL`.
- **Observability.** Wrap clients with metrics (command latency histogram, error counts by type) and propagate a trace ID in logs. Redis `connectionName` plus `CLIENT LIST` gives a server-side cross-check.
- **Multi-tenancy and key prefixes.** ioredis supports `keyPrefix`, but it does not apply to `SCAN`/`KEYS` patterns or to Lua `KEYS` arguments in obvious ways, and BullMQ has its own `prefix`. Prefer explicit `RedisKeys` builders over `keyPrefix`.
- **Cluster readiness.** If you may move to Redis Cluster, design keys with hash tags for multi-key operations now (see the Cluster module), because Lua and transactions require same-slot keys.

## 13.23 Practical exercise

**Task.** Add a rate limiter to your NestJS app using the `cache` client:

1. Fixed-window limiter: 100 requests/minute per IP per route, using `RedisKeys.rateLimit`.
2. If Redis is unavailable, **fail open** (allow the request) and log a warning.
3. Write a unit test (mocked) for the fail-open path and an integration test (Testcontainers) proving atomic increments.

**Solution.**

```ts
// src/rate-limit/rate-limit.service.ts
import { Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import type { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { InjectRedis } from '../redis/redis.decorators';
import { RedisKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

const LUA = `
local current = redis.call('INCR', KEYS[1])
if current == 1 then redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]) end
return current
`;

@Injectable()
export class RateLimitService {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(RateLimitService.name);
  constructor(@InjectRedis('cache') private readonly redis: Redis) {}

  async hit(ip: string, route: string, limit = 100, windowSec = 60): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; count: number }> {
    try {
      // Single round trip, INCR and EXPIRE are atomic together
      const count = (await this.redis.eval(LUA, 1, RedisKeys.rateLimit(ip, route), windowSec)) as number;
      return { allowed: count <= limit, count };
    } catch (err) {
      this.logger.warn(`rate limiter failing open: ${(err as Error).message}`);
      return { allowed: true, count: 0 };
    }
  }
}
```

```ts
// unit test: fail-open
it('fails open when Redis errors', async () => {
  const redis = { eval: jest.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('timeout')) };
  const svc = new RateLimitService(redis as any);
  await expect(svc.hit('1.1.1.1', '/login')).resolves.toEqual({ allowed: true, count: 0 });
});
```

The integration test is the 50-parallel-calls case from 13.15: assert max count equals 50 and that `TTL shop:rl:/login:1.1.1.1` is between 1 and 60.

Trade-off to discuss: a fixed window permits a 2x burst at window boundaries; a sliding window (sorted set or token bucket in Lua) fixes that at higher cost.

## 13.24 Key takeaways

- Validate config at bootstrap; one named client per role; each role gets its own timeout and retry policy.
- ioredis for BullMQ stacks; node-redis v5 when you need typed module APIs or client-side caching.
- Attach `error` listeners, back off with jitter, and decide hard vs soft dependency explicitly.
- Shutdown: `enableShutdownHooks()`, stop work first, `quit()` with a `disconnect()` fallback.
- Readiness checks Redis; liveness does not.
- Mock with DI, test real semantics with Testcontainers, distrust ioredis-mock for Lua and BullMQ.

# Module 14: Real-World Projects

This module turns the earlier modules into complete, production-shaped systems. Each project follows the same template: requirements, architecture, data structures, key and TTL design, data flow, NestJS code, failure handling, security, performance, testing and deployment. The goal is not to memorize code. It is to practice the reasoning interviewers expect at senior and staff level: which structure fits, what happens when Redis is slow or down, where the race conditions hide, and what you would monitor.

All projects share the Module 1 foundation (`REDIS_CLIENT` injection token from `RedisModule`, the `RedisKeys` builder with `APP = 'shop'`, and ioredis). Projects 14.1 to 14.7 extend `RedisKeys` as shown below. Baseline is Redis 8.x; version-specific commands are tagged, for example `[6.2+]`.

## 14.1 API response caching system

### Requirements

Functional:

- Cache `GET` responses of selected controller routes, declared with a decorator (`@Cacheable`).
- Cache key depends on route path, query string (order-independent) and the caller's scope: `public`, `user` or `tenant`. A response generated for user A must never be served to user B.
- Invalidate a whole group of entries (for example every `products` response) in one cheap operation, without scanning keys.
- Optional `ETag` / `If-None-Match` support so clients get `304 Not Modified` and skip the body.

Non-functional:

- p99 cache-hit overhead under 5 ms.
- Redis outage must not take the API down: the system degrades to "no cache".
- A cache stampede (many concurrent misses on a hot key) must not overload MongoDB/PostgreSQL.

### Architecture

```
            +--------+     +-------+      +----------------------------+
 Client --> | Nginx  | --> | Nest  | ---> | CacheInterceptor           |
            +--------+     | (xN)  |      |  1. build key              |
                           +-------+      |  2. GET version, GET entry |
                                          +-----+----------------+-----+
                                          hit   |                | miss
                                                v                v
                                          return cached     Controller -> DB
                                          (+304 if ETag)    then SET key EX ttl
                                                |                |
                                                +-------+--------+
                                                        v
                                                     [ Redis ]
 Write path:  ProductsService.update() --> cache.invalidate('products')
              --> SET shop:cache:products:ver <timestamp>   (old keys die by TTL)
```

### Redis data structures

| Purpose | Structure | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Cached response | String (JSON `{body, etag}`) | Opaque blob, atomic `SET ... EX` |
| Namespace version | String (timestamp) | One write invalidates every entry of the namespace |
| Stampede lock | String with `NX PX` | Cheap mutual exclusion across instances |

### Key design

```
shop:cache:<namespace>:v<version>:<scope>:<sha1(path + sorted query)>
shop:cache:products:v1731999999000:pub:3f2a...       (public list)
shop:cache:orders:v1731999999000:u42:91bc...         (user 42 only)
shop:cache:products:ver                              (version string)
shop:cache:lock:<hash>                               (stampede lock)
```

Versioned invalidation is the key idea. Instead of `SCAN` + `DEL` (slow, O(N) over the whole keyspace, not atomic), you change the version embedded in every key. Old entries become unreachable and expire through their own TTL. The cost is wasted memory until TTLs pass, so keep TTLs short (seconds to minutes).

Pitfall: if the version key is evicted or lost, the version resets and very old entries could match again. Use a timestamp as the version (never reused), and make sure entry TTLs are shorter than the lifetime you expect for the version key. Do not put the version key on an `allkeys-lru` instance without protection; a dedicated "cache" Redis with `maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru` plus timestamp versions is acceptable because a lost version only causes a miss path (`'0'`), never reuse of a recent version.

### TTL strategy

- Per-route TTL from the decorator (for example 30 s for product lists, 5 min for static catalog data).
- Add jitter (±10%) so keys created together do not all expire together.
- Version key: no TTL (or very long).
- Lock key: short `PX 10000`, always expires even if the holder crashes.

### Data flow

1. Interceptor reads `@Cacheable` metadata. If none, or method is not `GET`, pass through.
2. Build scope (`pub`, `u<id>`). If scope is `user` and there is no authenticated user, bypass the cache.
3. `GET shop:cache:<ns>:ver` then `GET` the entry key.
4. Hit: set `X-Cache: HIT`, honor `If-None-Match`, return body.
5. Miss: try `SET lock NX PX`. Winner executes the handler and stores the result. Losers poll the cache briefly (3 x 50 ms), then fall through to the handler if still empty.
6. Store only `200` responses with a defined body.

### Code implementation

```ts
// src/cache/cacheable.decorator.ts
import { SetMetadata } from '@nestjs/common';

export const CACHEABLE_KEY = 'cacheable:options';

export interface CacheableOptions {
  /** Invalidation group, e.g. 'products' */
  namespace: string;
  /** Seconds */
  ttl: number;
  /** Who may share an entry. Default 'public'. */
  scope?: 'public' | 'user' | 'tenant';
  /** Emit ETag and honor If-None-Match */
  etag?: boolean;
}

export const Cacheable = (options: CacheableOptions) =>
  SetMetadata(CACHEABLE_KEY, options);
```

```ts
// src/cache/response-cache.service.ts
import { Inject, Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { RedisKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

export interface CachedEntry {
  body: unknown;
  etag?: string;
}

const RELEASE_LOCK_LUA = `
if redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]) == ARGV[1] then
  return redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1])
end
return 0`;

@Injectable()
export class ResponseCacheService {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(ResponseCacheService.name);

  constructor(@Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis) {}

  async version(ns: string): Promise<string> {
    return (await this.redis.get(RedisKeys.cacheVersion(ns))) ?? '0';
  }

  async get(key: string): Promise<CachedEntry | null> {
    const raw = await this.redis.get(key);
    return raw ? (JSON.parse(raw) as CachedEntry) : null;
  }

  async set(key: string, entry: CachedEntry, ttlSeconds: number): Promise<void> {
    const jitter = 1 + (Math.random() * 0.2 - 0.1); // +/-10%
    const ttl = Math.max(1, Math.round(ttlSeconds * jitter));
    await this.redis.set(key, JSON.stringify(entry), 'EX', ttl);
  }

  /** Invalidate every entry of a namespace in O(1). Call after writes. */
  async invalidate(ns: string): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await this.redis.set(RedisKeys.cacheVersion(ns), Date.now().toString());
    } catch (err) {
      // If we cannot invalidate, stale data may be served until TTL. Log loudly.
      this.logger.error(`Cache invalidate failed for ${ns}: ${(err as Error).message}`);
      throw err;
    }
  }

  /** Returns a lock token or null. */
  async tryLock(hash: string, ttlMs = 10_000): Promise<string | null> {
    const token = `${process.pid}:${Date.now()}:${Math.random()}`;
    const ok = await this.redis.set(RedisKeys.cacheLock(hash), token, 'PX', ttlMs, 'NX');
    return ok === 'OK' ? token : null;
  }

  async unlock(hash: string, token: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.redis.eval(RELEASE_LOCK_LUA, 1, RedisKeys.cacheLock(hash), token);
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/cache/response-cache.interceptor.ts
import {
  CallHandler, ExecutionContext, Injectable, Logger, NestInterceptor,
} from '@nestjs/common';
import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import type { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { Observable, of } from 'rxjs';
import { tap } from 'rxjs/operators';
import { CACHEABLE_KEY, CacheableOptions } from './cacheable.decorator';
import { ResponseCacheService } from './response-cache.service';
import { RedisKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

@Injectable()
export class ResponseCacheInterceptor implements NestInterceptor {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(ResponseCacheInterceptor.name);

  constructor(
    private readonly reflector: Reflector,
    private readonly cache: ResponseCacheService,
  ) {}

  async intercept(ctx: ExecutionContext, next: CallHandler): Promise<Observable<unknown>> {
    const opts = this.reflector.get<CacheableOptions | undefined>(
      CACHEABLE_KEY,
      ctx.getHandler(),
    );
    const http = ctx.switchToHttp();
    const req = http.getRequest<Request & { user?: { id: string; tenantId?: string } }>();
    const res = http.getResponse<Response>();

    if (!opts || req.method !== 'GET') return next.handle();

    const scope = this.resolveScope(opts, req);
    if (!scope) return next.handle(); // user-scoped route but anonymous: never cache

    const hash = this.hashRequest(req);
    let key: string;
    try {
      const ver = await this.cache.version(opts.namespace);
      key = RedisKeys.cache(opts.namespace, ver, scope, hash);
      const hit = await this.cache.get(key);
      if (hit) return this.serveHit(hit, req, res, opts);

      // Miss: single-flight across instances
      const token = await this.cache.tryLock(hash);
      if (!token) {
        for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
          await sleep(50);
          const again = await this.cache.get(key);
          if (again) return this.serveHit(again, req, res, opts);
        }
        // Still empty: fall through to origin rather than block the user
      }

      res.setHeader('X-Cache', 'MISS');
      return next.handle().pipe(
        tap({
          next: (body) => void this.store(key, body, res, opts),
          finalize: () => {
            if (token) void this.cache.unlock(hash, token).catch(() => undefined);
          },
        }),
      );
    } catch (err) {
      // Redis down or slow: degrade to no cache
      this.logger.warn(`Cache bypassed: ${(err as Error).message}`);
      res.setHeader('X-Cache', 'BYPASS');
      return next.handle();
    }
  }

  private resolveScope(
    opts: CacheableOptions,
    req: Request & { user?: { id: string; tenantId?: string } },
  ): string | null {
    switch (opts.scope ?? 'public') {
      case 'public': return 'pub';
      case 'user': return req.user ? `u${req.user.id}` : null;
      case 'tenant': return req.user?.tenantId ? `t${req.user.tenantId}` : null;
    }
  }

  /** Order-independent: ?a=1&b=2 and ?b=2&a=1 share one entry. */
  private hashRequest(req: Request): string {
    const q = new URLSearchParams(req.query as Record<string, string>);
    q.sort();
    return createHash('sha1').update(`${req.path}?${q.toString()}`).digest('hex');
  }

  private serveHit(
    hit: { body: unknown; etag?: string },
    req: Request,
    res: Response,
    opts: CacheableOptions,
  ): Observable<unknown> {
    res.setHeader('X-Cache', 'HIT');
    if (opts.etag && hit.etag) {
      res.setHeader('ETag', hit.etag);
      if (req.headers['if-none-match'] === hit.etag) {
        res.status(304);
        return of(undefined);
      }
    }
    return of(hit.body);
  }

  private async store(
    key: string,
    body: unknown,
    res: Response,
    opts: CacheableOptions,
  ): Promise<void> {
    if (body === undefined || res.statusCode !== 200) return;
    try {
      const etag = opts.etag
        ? `"${createHash('sha1').update(JSON.stringify(body)).digest('base64url')}"`
        : undefined;
      if (etag) res.setHeader('ETag', etag);
      await this.cache.set(key, { body, etag }, opts.ttl);
    } catch (err) {
      this.logger.warn(`Cache store failed: ${(err as Error).message}`);
    }
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/products/products.controller.ts  (usage)
import { Controller, Get, Param, Patch, Body, UseInterceptors } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Cacheable } from '../cache/cacheable.decorator';
import { ResponseCacheInterceptor } from '../cache/response-cache.interceptor';
import { ResponseCacheService } from '../cache/response-cache.service';
import { ProductsService } from './products.service';

@Controller('products')
@UseInterceptors(ResponseCacheInterceptor)
export class ProductsController {
  constructor(
    private readonly products: ProductsService,
    private readonly cache: ResponseCacheService,
  ) {}

  @Get()
  @Cacheable({ namespace: 'products', ttl: 60, etag: true })
  list() {
    return this.products.findAll();
  }

  @Patch(':id')
  async update(@Param('id') id: string, @Body() dto: Record<string, unknown>) {
    const updated = await this.products.update(id, dto);
    await this.cache.invalidate('products'); // after the DB commit
    return updated;
  }
}
```

A note on the interceptor: Nest serializes the return value after interceptors run, so caching the controller's return value (a plain object) is correct only if no later serialization step changes it (for example class-transformer `ClassSerializerInterceptor`). Register the cache interceptor so it sees the same shape you want to store, and test it.

### Failure handling

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Redis down / timeout | `catch` in interceptor, header `X-Cache: BYPASS`, request served from DB. Set `maxRetriesPerRequest` low (Module 1 uses 3) so requests do not hang. |
| Redis down during `invalidate` | Throw (or enqueue a retry job in BullMQ). Silent failure means stale data until TTL. |
| Store fails after handler succeeded | Logged, response still returned. |
| Lock holder crashes | Lock expires in 10 s; waiters fall through to origin after 150 ms anyway. |
| DB spike on Redis restart | Cold cache causes a thundering herd; lock + short fall-through limits it. Consider warm-up for top routes. |

### Security considerations

- Scope is part of the key. Never cache authenticated responses under `pub`. Default to `scope: 'user'` for anything behind a guard and review each `@Cacheable('public')` in code review.
- Include any header that changes the output in the hash (`Accept-Language`, tenant header) or you leak variants between callers.
- Do not cache responses that set cookies or contain per-request secrets.
- Do not trust the raw query string size: cap URL length at Nginx to prevent cache-key flooding (each unique query creates a key).

### Performance considerations

- Two round trips on a hit (`GET ver`, `GET entry`). Reduce to one by caching the version in process memory for 1 to 2 seconds (accepting that staleness window), or by using a Lua script that reads both.
- Store compressed JSON for large payloads (`zlib.gzipSync`, store base64 or use `ioredis` `Buffer` methods) if values exceed ~10 KB.
- Monitor hit ratio from `INFO stats` (`keyspace_hits`, `keyspace_misses`) plus an app counter on `X-Cache`.
- Keep entries bounded (limit page size) to avoid big keys.

### Testing strategy

- Unit: scope resolution, key hash order independence, ETag 304 path (mock `ResponseCacheService`).
- Integration (Testcontainers Redis or docker-compose): MISS then HIT; user A vs user B isolation; `invalidate` makes the next call MISS; TTL expiry using a short TTL.
- Chaos: stop Redis container mid-test and assert 200 with `X-Cache: BYPASS`.
- Load: k6 against a hot key to verify only one origin call per TTL window (lock works).

### Production deployment notes

- Use a separate Redis instance (or logical split) for cache with `maxmemory` set and `maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru` or `allkeys-lfu`. Never share an eviction-enabled instance with BullMQ or sessions.
- Namespace names are part of your invalidation contract; document them next to the services that call `invalidate`.
- Add `Cache-Control` / `Vary` headers appropriate for the CDN or Nginx `proxy_cache` in front, so layers do not contradict each other.
- Alert on hit ratio drop, eviction count, and bypass rate.

## 14.2 Login session management

### Requirements

- Server-side sessions with an opaque, unguessable session id in an `HttpOnly` cookie. No user data in the cookie.
- A user can have several sessions (laptop, phone). List them and revoke one.
- Sliding expiration: active users stay logged in; idle sessions expire. Also an absolute maximum lifetime (for example 30 days).
- "Logout all devices" (also used after password change).
- Defend against session fixation: a new id is issued at login and on privilege change.

### Architecture

```
 Browser --cookie: sid=<random 256-bit>-->  Nginx --> NestJS
                                                       |
                                  SessionGuard: sha256(sid) -> HGETALL + EXPIRE
                                                       |
                                                    [ Redis ]
   shop:session:<sha256(sid)>        HASH  userId, createdAt, lastSeen, ip, ua   (TTL = idle timeout)
   shop:user:<userId>:sessions       SET   of sha256(sid) values                 (index for logout-all)
```

### Redis data structures

| Key | Type | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `shop:session:<hash>` | Hash | `userId`, `createdAt`, `lastSeen`, `ip`, `ua`, `roles` (optional) |
| `shop:user:<id>:sessions` | Set | Session hashes that belong to the user |

A hash lets you update `lastSeen` without rewriting the whole value. If you prefer storing sessions as one JSON string, `GETEX key EX 1800` `[6.2+]` reads and refreshes the TTL in a single command. For a hash there is no `GETEX` equivalent, so you use `HGETALL` plus `EXPIRE` in a pipeline.

### Key design

The cookie holds the raw random id. Redis stores only `sha256(rawId)` in the key name. If someone reads Redis (backup leak, `KEYS` access, a debugging dump), they cannot replay the cookies. This is the same idea as hashing password-reset tokens.

### TTL strategy

- Idle timeout: 30 minutes to 7 days depending on risk (`SESSION_IDLE_SECONDS`).
- Absolute lifetime: store `createdAt`; the guard rejects sessions older than `SESSION_MAX_SECONDS` even if still in Redis.
- Throttled sliding: calling `EXPIRE` on every request is cheap but adds a write per request. Only refresh when the remaining TTL is under half of the idle timeout (needs `TTL`, so do it in the same pipeline and decide after). The code below refreshes at most once per `touchIntervalSeconds` using `lastSeen`.
- User index set: TTL set to the absolute lifetime and refreshed on login. Stale members (sessions that already expired) are removed lazily.

### Data flow

```
Login:   verify password -> rotate: delete any presented old sid
         -> raw = randomBytes(32).base64url -> h = sha256(raw)
         -> MULTI: HSET session:h ... ; EXPIRE session:h idle ; SADD user:id:sessions h ; EXPIRE index max
         -> Set-Cookie sid=raw (HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/)
Request: cookie -> h -> pipeline(HGETALL session:h) -> empty? 401
         -> absolute age check -> maybe EXPIRE (sliding) -> attach req.session
Logout:  DEL session:h ; SREM index h ; clear cookie
Logout-all: SMEMBERS index -> DEL each session -> DEL index
```

### Code implementation

```ts
// src/session/session.service.ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { createHash, randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { RedisKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

export interface SessionData {
  userId: string;
  createdAt: number; // epoch ms
  lastSeen: number;
  ip: string;
  ua: string;
}

export interface ActiveSession extends SessionData {
  id: string; // hash, safe to expose to the owner as an opaque handle
}

@Injectable()
export class SessionService {
  private readonly idleSeconds: number;
  private readonly maxSeconds: number;
  private readonly touchIntervalMs = 60_000;

  constructor(
    @Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis,
    config: ConfigService,
  ) {
    this.idleSeconds = config.get<number>('SESSION_IDLE_SECONDS', 60 * 60 * 24 * 7);
    this.maxSeconds = config.get<number>('SESSION_MAX_SECONDS', 60 * 60 * 24 * 30);
  }

  static hash(raw: string): string {
    return createHash('sha256').update(raw).digest('hex');
  }

  /** Creates a brand-new session. Always call at login (fixation defense). */
  async create(userId: string, ip: string, ua: string): Promise<{ raw: string; ttl: number }> {
    const raw = randomBytes(32).toString('base64url'); // 256 bits of CSPRNG output
    const h = SessionService.hash(raw);
    const now = Date.now();
    const key = RedisKeys.session(h);
    const idx = RedisKeys.userSessions(userId);

    await this.redis
      .multi()
      .hset(key, { userId, createdAt: now, lastSeen: now, ip, ua: ua.slice(0, 200) })
      .expire(key, this.idleSeconds)
      .sadd(idx, h)
      .expire(idx, this.maxSeconds)
      .exec();

    return { raw, ttl: this.idleSeconds };
  }

  /** Validates, applies sliding expiration, returns null if invalid. */
  async validate(raw: string | undefined): Promise<(SessionData & { id: string }) | null> {
    if (!raw || raw.length < 32 || raw.length > 128) return null;
    const h = SessionService.hash(raw);
    const key = RedisKeys.session(h);

    const data = await this.redis.hgetall(key);
    if (!data.userId) return null;

    const s: SessionData = {
      userId: data.userId,
      createdAt: Number(data.createdAt),
      lastSeen: Number(data.lastSeen),
      ip: data.ip,
      ua: data.ua,
    };
    const now = Date.now();

    // Absolute lifetime
    if (now - s.createdAt > this.maxSeconds * 1000) {
      await this.destroyByHash(h, s.userId);
      return null;
    }

    // Sliding expiration, throttled to one write per interval
    if (now - s.lastSeen > this.touchIntervalMs) {
      await this.redis
        .multi()
        .hset(key, 'lastSeen', now)
        .expire(key, this.idleSeconds)
        .exec();
      s.lastSeen = now;
    }
    return { ...s, id: h };
  }

  async destroyByHash(h: string, userId: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.redis.multi().del(RedisKeys.session(h)).srem(RedisKeys.userSessions(userId), h).exec();
  }

  /** Logout all devices; optionally keep the current one. */
  async destroyAll(userId: string, exceptHash?: string): Promise<number> {
    const idx = RedisKeys.userSessions(userId);
    const hashes = (await this.redis.smembers(idx)).filter((h) => h !== exceptHash);
    if (hashes.length === 0) return 0;
    const pipe = this.redis.pipeline();
    for (const h of hashes) pipe.del(RedisKeys.session(h));
    pipe.srem(idx, ...hashes);
    await pipe.exec();
    return hashes.length;
  }

  /** Lists live sessions; removes dangling index entries (expired sessions). */
  async list(userId: string): Promise<ActiveSession[]> {
    const idx = RedisKeys.userSessions(userId);
    const hashes = await this.redis.smembers(idx);
    if (hashes.length === 0) return [];
    const pipe = this.redis.pipeline();
    hashes.forEach((h) => pipe.hgetall(RedisKeys.session(h)));
    const results = (await pipe.exec()) ?? [];

    const live: ActiveSession[] = [];
    const dead: string[] = [];
    results.forEach(([err, val], i) => {
      const d = val as Record<string, string>;
      if (err || !d?.userId) dead.push(hashes[i]);
      else live.push({ id: hashes[i], userId: d.userId, createdAt: +d.createdAt,
        lastSeen: +d.lastSeen, ip: d.ip, ua: d.ua });
    });
    if (dead.length) await this.redis.srem(idx, ...dead);
    return live;
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/session/session.guard.ts
import {
  CanActivate, ExecutionContext, Injectable, UnauthorizedException,
} from '@nestjs/common';
import type { Request } from 'express';
import { SessionService } from './session.service';

export const SESSION_COOKIE = 'sid';

@Injectable()
export class SessionGuard implements CanActivate {
  constructor(private readonly sessions: SessionService) {}

  async canActivate(ctx: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean> {
    const req = ctx.switchToHttp().getRequest<Request & { session?: unknown; user?: unknown }>();
    // requires cookie-parser: app.use(cookieParser())
    const raw = (req.cookies as Record<string, string> | undefined)?.[SESSION_COOKIE];
    let session;
    try {
      session = await this.sessions.validate(raw);
    } catch {
      // Redis unavailable: fail closed for authentication.
      throw new UnauthorizedException('Session store unavailable');
    }
    if (!session) throw new UnauthorizedException();
    req.session = session;
    req.user = { id: session.userId };
    return true;
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/session/auth.controller.ts
import {
  Body, Controller, Delete, Get, HttpCode, Param, Post, Req, Res, UseGuards,
} from '@nestjs/common';
import type { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { SESSION_COOKIE, SessionGuard } from './session.guard';
import { SessionService } from './session.service';

// Replace with your real credential check (argon2/bcrypt against PostgreSQL)
export abstract class CredentialsService {
  abstract verify(email: string, password: string): Promise<{ id: string } | null>;
}

interface AuthedRequest extends Request {
  session: { id: string; userId: string };
}

@Controller('auth')
export class AuthController {
  constructor(
    private readonly sessions: SessionService,
    private readonly creds: CredentialsService,
  ) {}

  @Post('login')
  @HttpCode(200)
  async login(
    @Body() dto: { email: string; password: string },
    @Req() req: Request,
    @Res({ passthrough: true }) res: Response,
  ) {
    const user = await this.creds.verify(dto.email, dto.password);
    if (!user) return { ok: false }; // use 401 + generic message in real code

    // Fixation defense: invalidate any presented session, always mint a new id.
    const oldRaw = (req.cookies as Record<string, string> | undefined)?.[SESSION_COOKIE];
    if (oldRaw) {
      const old = await this.sessions.validate(oldRaw).catch(() => null);
      if (old) await this.sessions.destroyByHash(old.id, old.userId);
    }

    const { raw, ttl } = await this.sessions.create(user.id, req.ip ?? '', req.get('user-agent') ?? '');
    res.cookie(SESSION_COOKIE, raw, {
      httpOnly: true,
      secure: true,
      sameSite: 'lax',
      path: '/',
      maxAge: ttl * 1000,
    });
    return { ok: true };
  }

  @Post('logout')
  @UseGuards(SessionGuard)
  @HttpCode(204)
  async logout(@Req() req: AuthedRequest, @Res({ passthrough: true }) res: Response) {
    await this.sessions.destroyByHash(req.session.id, req.session.userId);
    res.clearCookie(SESSION_COOKIE, { path: '/' });
  }

  @Post('logout-all')
  @UseGuards(SessionGuard)
  async logoutAll(@Req() req: AuthedRequest, @Res({ passthrough: true }) res: Response) {
    const count = await this.sessions.destroyAll(req.session.userId);
    res.clearCookie(SESSION_COOKIE, { path: '/' });
    return { revoked: count };
  }

  @Get('sessions')
  @UseGuards(SessionGuard)
  list(@Req() req: AuthedRequest) {
    return this.sessions.list(req.session.userId);
  }

  @Delete('sessions/:id')
  @UseGuards(SessionGuard)
  @HttpCode(204)
  async revoke(@Req() req: AuthedRequest, @Param('id') id: string) {
```
