```ts
    // Only revoke ids that are in the caller's own index
    const mine = await this.sessions.list(req.session.userId);
    if (mine.some((s) => s.id === id)) {
      await this.sessions.destroyByHash(id, req.session.userId);
    }
  }
}
```

### Failure handling

- Redis down: authentication fails closed (401/503). Do not fall back to "trust the cookie". Run Redis with replication and Sentinel (or a managed failover) because a Redis outage logs everybody out of protected routes.
- Failover with async replication can lose the last few writes: a just-created session may vanish (user must log in again) and a just-revoked session may reappear for a moment. For high-risk revocation (password change), also keep a short "revoked-before" timestamp per user in PostgreSQL or use `WAIT` after the revocation write.
- Partial failure in `destroyAll`: the pipeline is not atomic across keys; a retry is idempotent (deleting missing keys is fine).
- Dangling index entries are harmless and removed in `list`.

### Security considerations

- 256-bit CSPRNG ids (`crypto.randomBytes`), never `Math.random`, UUIDv1, or user-derived values.
- Cookie flags: `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` (or `Strict`), `Path=/`. Use the `__Host-` prefix if you can (requires `Secure`, `Path=/`, no `Domain`).
- Rotate the id at login, at privilege elevation, and after password/MFA change.
- Add CSRF protection for state-changing routes if you use cookies (SameSite helps but is not a complete defense).
- Optionally bind to coarse device info (UA family), but avoid hard IP binding because mobile networks change IPs.
- Rate limit `/auth/login` with project 14.4.
- Redis ACL user for the app with only the needed commands; `requirepass`/TLS on the network path.

### Performance considerations

- One `HGETALL` per request (O(fields)). Keep fields small. With `touchIntervalMs` at 60 s, only ~1 write per minute per active user.
- If session lookups dominate, add a short in-process LRU (5 to 10 s) keyed by session hash, accepting that revocation takes up to that long to propagate.
- Index sets stay small (a handful per user). Cap sessions per user (for example 10) by evicting the oldest on login.

### Testing strategy

- Unit: `hash` determinism, absolute lifetime rejection (mock `Date.now`).
- Integration: login sets cookie; protected route 200; after `logout` same cookie gets 401; `logout-all` kills a second session created with another client; TTL slides (use short `SESSION_IDLE_SECONDS`, assert `TTL` increases).
- Security tests: presented old sid is destroyed on login; tampered cookie returns 401; cookie flags present.

### Production deployment notes

- Behind Nginx, set `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme` and in Nest `app.set('trust proxy', 1)` so `req.ip` and `Secure` cookies behave.
- Sessions are durable-ish state: enable AOF (`appendfsync everysec`) or accept that a Redis crash logs users out. Do not run sessions on an `allkeys-lru` cache instance; use `volatile-lru` or `noeviction` with memory alerts.
- With PM2 cluster or multiple containers, sessions need no stickiness because state lives in Redis.

---

## 14.3 OTP generation and verification

### Requirements

- Generate a 6-digit one-time code for login/verification, valid for 5 minutes.
- Store a hash, never the plaintext code.
- Limit wrong guesses (max 5 attempts), enforce a resend cooldown (60 s), and cap sends per hour.
- Single use: after a successful verification the code cannot be reused, even by two concurrent requests.
- Do not reveal whether an identifier (email/phone) exists.

### Architecture

```
 Client --POST /otp/send--> OtpController --> OtpService.issue()
                                              |  Lua: cooldown + hourly cap + SET hash (atomic)
                                              +--> BullMQ queue "otp-delivery" --> SMS/email provider
 Client --POST /otp/verify-> OtpController --> OtpService.verify()
                                              |  Lua: attempts++ ; compare ; DEL on success (atomic)
                                           [ Redis ]
```

### Redis data structures

| Key | Type | Content | TTL |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shop:otp:<purpose>:<idHash>` | Hash | `h` (HMAC of code), `attempts` | 300 s |
| `shop:otp:cd:<purpose>:<idHash>` | String | `1` (cooldown marker) | 60 s |
| `shop:otp:sends:<purpose>:<idHash>` | String counter | sends in the current hour | 3600 s from first send |

### Key design

`idHash` is `sha256(normalizedEmailOrPhone)` truncated or full, so raw PII does not sit in key names (visible in `MONITOR`, `SLOWLOG`, `--bigkeys`). `purpose` (`login`, `reset`, `phone-verify`) prevents a code issued for one flow being used in another.

### TTL strategy

- Code: 5 minutes. Short TTL limits brute force window and storage.
- Cooldown: 60 s (`SET NX EX`-style inside Lua).
- Send counter: fixed 1-hour window, TTL set on first increment.
- All three keys always have a TTL; nothing is permanent.

### Data flow

1. `issue(purpose, identifier)`: generate code with `crypto.randomInt`, compute `HMAC-SHA256(secret, purpose|idHash|code)`.
2. Lua script atomically: if cooldown key exists, return remaining cooldown; increment hourly counter, reject if over cap; `HSET` hash with `attempts=0`, `EXPIRE` 300; set cooldown key.
3. Enqueue delivery job (BullMQ) with the plaintext code. The plaintext exists only in memory and the job payload; use `removeOnComplete: true` and consider encrypting the payload, since BullMQ jobs are stored in Redis.
4. `verify(purpose, identifier, code)`: Lua script atomically: load hash; if missing return expired; `HINCRBY attempts`; if attempts exceed max, delete and return locked; compare hashes; on success `DEL` and return OK.

Why HMAC with a server secret rather than a plain SHA-256: there are only one million six-digit codes. An unsalted hash can be reversed in microseconds if the data leaks. A keyed HMAC means a Redis dump alone is not enough.

### Code implementation

```ts
// src/otp/otp.service.ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
import { InjectQueue } from '@nestjs/bullmq';
import { Queue } from 'bullmq';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { createHash, createHmac, randomInt } from 'node:crypto';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { RedisKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

export type OtpPurpose = 'login' | 'reset' | 'phone-verify';

export type IssueResult =
  | { status: 'sent' }
  | { status: 'cooldown'; retryAfterSeconds: number }
  | { status: 'limited' };

export type VerifyResult = 'ok' | 'invalid' | 'expired' | 'locked';

// KEYS: 1 otp, 2 cooldown, 3 sends
// ARGV: 1 hmac, 2 codeTtl, 3 cooldownTtl, 4 maxSends, 5 sendsWindow
// returns: {0,'sent'} | {1,secondsLeft} cooldown | {2,0} limited
const ISSUE_LUA = `
local cd = redis.call('TTL', KEYS[2])
if cd > 0 then
  return {1, cd}
end
local sends = redis.call('INCR', KEYS[3])
if sends == 1 then
  redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[3], tonumber(ARGV[5]))
end
if sends > tonumber(ARGV[4]) then
  return {2, 0}
end
redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1])
redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], 'h', ARGV[1], 'attempts', 0)
redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], tonumber(ARGV[2]))
redis.call('SET', KEYS[2], '1', 'EX', tonumber(ARGV[3]))
return {0, 0}
`;

// KEYS: 1 otp ; ARGV: 1 hmac, 2 maxAttempts
// returns: 1 ok | 0 invalid | -1 expired/missing | -2 locked
const VERIFY_LUA = `
local stored = redis.call('HGET', KEYS[1], 'h')
if not stored then
  return -1
end
local attempts = redis.call('HINCRBY', KEYS[1], 'attempts', 1)
if attempts > tonumber(ARGV[2]) then
  redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1])
  return -2
end
if stored == ARGV[1] then
  redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1])
  return 1
end
return 0
`;

@Injectable()
export class OtpService {
  private readonly secret: string;
  private readonly codeTtl = 300;
  private readonly cooldown = 60;
  private readonly maxSends = 5;
  private readonly sendsWindow = 3600;
  private readonly maxAttempts = 5;

  constructor(
    @Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis,
    @InjectQueue('otp-delivery') private readonly deliveryQueue: Queue,
    config: ConfigService,
  ) {
    this.secret = config.getOrThrow<string>('OTP_HMAC_SECRET');
  }

  private idHash(identifier: string): string {
    return createHash('sha256').update(identifier.trim().toLowerCase()).digest('hex');
  }

  private mac(purpose: string, idHash: string, code: string): string {
    return createHmac('sha256', this.secret).update(`${purpose}|${idHash}|${code}`).digest('hex');
  }

  async issue(purpose: OtpPurpose, identifier: string): Promise<IssueResult> {
    const idHash = this.idHash(identifier);
    const code = randomInt(0, 1_000_000).toString().padStart(6, '0'); // CSPRNG, uniform

    const [state, extra] = (await this.redis.eval(
      ISSUE_LUA,
      3,
      RedisKeys.otp(purpose, idHash),
      RedisKeys.otpCooldown(purpose, idHash),
      RedisKeys.otpSends(purpose, idHash),
      this.mac(purpose, idHash, code),
      this.codeTtl,
      this.cooldown,
      this.maxSends,
      this.sendsWindow,
    )) as [number, number];

    if (state === 1) return { status: 'cooldown', retryAfterSeconds: extra };
    if (state === 2) return { status: 'limited' };

    await this.deliveryQueue.add(
      'send',
      { purpose, identifier, code },
      { attempts: 3, backoff: { type: 'exponential', delay: 2000 }, removeOnComplete: true, removeOnFail: 100 },
    );
    return { status: 'sent' };
  }

  async verify(purpose: OtpPurpose, identifier: string, code: string): Promise<VerifyResult> {
    if (!/^\d{6}$/.test(code)) return 'invalid';
    const idHash = this.idHash(identifier);
    const res = (await this.redis.eval(
      VERIFY_LUA,
      1,
      RedisKeys.otp(purpose, idHash),
      this.mac(purpose, idHash, code),
      this.maxAttempts,
    )) as number;
    return res === 1 ? 'ok' : res === 0 ? 'invalid' : res === -2 ? 'locked' : 'expired';
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/otp/otp.controller.ts
import { Body, Controller, HttpCode, HttpException, HttpStatus, Post } from '@nestjs/common';
import { OtpPurpose, OtpService } from './otp.service';

@Controller('otp')
export class OtpController {
  constructor(private readonly otp: OtpService) {}

  @Post('send')
  @HttpCode(202)
  async send(@Body() dto: { purpose: OtpPurpose; identifier: string }) {
    const r = await this.otp.issue(dto.purpose, dto.identifier);
    if (r.status === 'cooldown') {
      throw new HttpException(
        { message: 'Please wait before requesting another code', retryAfter: r.retryAfterSeconds },
        HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
      );
    }
    if (r.status === 'limited') {
      throw new HttpException('Too many requests', HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS);
    }
    // Same response whether or not the account exists (decide delivery elsewhere)
    return { message: 'If the account exists, a code has been sent' };
  }

  @Post('verify')
  @HttpCode(200)
  async verify(@Body() dto: { purpose: OtpPurpose; identifier: string; code: string }) {
    const r = await this.otp.verify(dto.purpose, dto.identifier, dto.code);
    if (r === 'ok') return { verified: true };
    if (r === 'locked') throw new HttpException('Too many attempts', HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS);
    // 'invalid' and 'expired' share one message to avoid oracle behaviour
    throw new HttpException('Invalid or expired code', HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST);
  }
}
```

If your OTP is really a long random token (magic link, email-confirm link), you do not need attempt counting. Store `SET token:<sha256(token)> userId EX 900` and consume it with `GETDEL` `[6.2+]`, which returns and deletes in one atomic step. For 6-digit codes the Lua script above is needed because you must compare, count attempts and delete as one unit.

### Failure handling

- Redis down on `issue`: return 503; do not send an SMS you cannot later verify. On `verify`: fail closed.
- Redis up but queue/provider fails after the code is stored: the user can request again after the 60 s cooldown. BullMQ retries delivery with backoff; if all retries fail, alert (this costs money and trust).
- Race: two concurrent correct `verify` calls. The Lua script serializes them: the first deletes the hash and returns 1, the second sees no hash and returns expired. Single use holds.
- Issue Lua increments the send counter even when over the cap. That is intentional (attackers cannot probe below the cap) but note the counter expires with the window.

### Security considerations

- `crypto.randomInt`, not `Math.random`.
- HMAC with a secret kept in a secrets manager, rotated with a versioned `kid` if needed (accept previous secret during rotation window).
- Attempt cap is per code, not per identifier alone. Also add an IP-based limit (14.4) on both endpoints so one attacker cannot spray many identifiers.
- Identical responses for existing and non-existing accounts; avoid timing differences by always doing the Redis work.
- SMS pumping / toll fraud: rate limit by IP, by country prefix and by overall send volume; this is a real cost attack.
- The Lua string comparison is not constant time, but the compared values are HMAC outputs and attempts are capped, so timing leakage is not practically exploitable.
- Never log the code, even at debug level. Mask in BullMQ job logs.

### Performance considerations

- Two small Lua scripts, O(1). Load them once with `SCRIPT LOAD`/`defineCommand` for fewer bytes on the wire (ioredis `redis.defineCommand` uses EVALSHA with fallback).
- The hot cost is the external SMS/email provider, which is why delivery goes through a queue and the HTTP request returns 202 immediately.

### Testing strategy

- Unit: HMAC determinism, 6-digit padding (`randomInt` result `5` becomes `000005`).
- Integration: issue then verify OK; reuse returns expired; 5 wrong guesses then correct code returns locked; second `issue` within 60 s returns cooldown; sixth send in an hour returns limited; TTL expiry with a shortened TTL config.
- Concurrency: fire 20 parallel verifies with the correct code and assert exactly one `ok`.

### Production deployment notes

- Keep OTP on a Redis with persistence not strictly required: losing codes only forces a resend. But isolate from eviction-enabled caches (an evicted code is a confusing user bug).
- Provider webhooks for delivery status can update a "delivery failed" metric; do not store them in the OTP keys.
- Dashboards: send rate per purpose, verification success ratio, lock rate, cooldown hits, per-provider failure rate.

---

## 14.4 Distributed API rate limiter

### Requirements

- Limit requests per IP, per authenticated user, or per route, configured with a decorator.
- Limits must hold across all Nest instances (PM2 workers, containers).
- Return standard headers (`RateLimit-*`, `Retry-After`) and HTTP 429.
- Support bursts (token bucket) and smooth windows (sliding window counter).
- Configurable fail-open or fail-closed when Redis is unavailable.

### Architecture

```
 Client --> Nginx (limit_req: coarse flood protection) --> NestJS
                                                            |
                                  RateLimitGuard (reads @RateLimit metadata)
                                                            |
                          EVALSHA token_bucket(key, capacity, refillPerSec, cost)
                                                            |
                                                         [ Redis ]  key: shop:rl:{route:subject}
 allowed=1 -> set headers, continue          allowed=0 -> 429 + Retry-After
```

Layering matters: Nginx `limit_req` absorbs raw floods cheaply, the Redis limiter enforces business rules (per user, per plan, per endpoint).

### Redis data structures

| Algorithm | Structure | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed window | String + `INCR` + `EXPIRE` | Simplest | 2x burst at window boundary |
| Sliding window log | ZSET of timestamps | Exact | O(requests) memory per subject |
| **Sliding window counter** | 2 counters (current, previous) weighted | Cheap, near-exact | Approximation |
| **Token bucket** | Hash `{tokens, ts}` | Bursts + steady rate, O(1) | Slightly harder to explain in headers |

This project implements token bucket (default) and sliding window counter (strict mode).

### Key design

```
shop:rl:{<routeName>:<subject>}          e.g. shop:rl:{login:ip:203.0.113.9}
subject = ip:<addr> | user:<id> | ip+route combos
```

The braces are a Redis Cluster hash tag: everything inside `{}` determines the slot. The sliding window script touches a derived second key (previous window); sharing the tag keeps both in one slot so the script works on Cluster. Keep the tag around a single subject to avoid creating a hot slot for all traffic.

### TTL strategy

- Token bucket: TTL of about `2 x capacity / refillRate`. After that long without requests the bucket would be full anyway, so deleting it loses no information.
- Sliding window counter: each window key expires after `2 x window`.
- No immortal keys: an attacker rotating IPs would otherwise grow memory forever.

### Data flow

1. Guard reads `@RateLimit({...})` from the handler (or class).
2. Resolve the subject: user id if authenticated and `by: 'user'`, else IP.
3. One `EVALSHA` call computes refill, decides, updates, sets TTL. Time comes from Redis `TIME`, so instance clock drift does not matter.
4. Set `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset` (IETF draft headers); on deny set `Retry-After` and throw 429.

### Code implementation

```ts
// src/rate-limit/rate-limit.decorator.ts
import { SetMetadata } from '@nestjs/common';

export const RATE_LIMIT_KEY = 'rate-limit:options';

export interface RateLimitOptions {
  /** Logical name; part of the Redis key, e.g. 'login' */
  name: string;
  /** Bucket size (max burst) or max requests per window */
  limit: number;
  /** Window in seconds. Token bucket refills `limit` tokens over this window. */
  windowSeconds: number;
  /** Who is limited. Default 'ip'. */
  by?: 'ip' | 'user' | 'user-or-ip';
  /** 'bucket' (default) or 'window' (sliding window counter) */
  algorithm?: 'bucket' | 'window';
  /** Behaviour when Redis is down. Default 'open'. Use 'closed' for login/OTP. */
  onRedisError?: 'open' | 'closed';
  /** Request cost, default 1 (bucket only) */
  cost?: number;
}

export const RateLimit = (options: RateLimitOptions) => SetMetadata(RATE_LIMIT_KEY, options);
```

```ts
// src/rate-limit/rate-limiter.service.ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { RedisKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

export interface LimitDecision {
  allowed: boolean;
  limit: number;
  remaining: number;
  retryAfterMs: number;
  resetMs: number; // time until bucket full / window end
}

// Token bucket. KEYS[1]=bucket. ARGV: capacity, refillPerSecond, cost
// Returns {allowed, remainingTokens(floor), retryAfterMs, resetMs}
const TOKEN_BUCKET_LUA = `
local capacity = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local refill   = tonumber(ARGV[2])
local cost     = tonumber(ARGV[3])
local t   = redis.call('TIME')
local now = t[1] * 1000 + math.floor(t[2] / 1000)

local data   = redis.call('HMGET', KEYS[1], 'tokens', 'ts')
local tokens = tonumber(data[1])
local ts     = tonumber(data[2])
if tokens == nil then
  tokens = capacity
  ts = now
end

local delta = math.max(0, now - ts)
tokens = math.min(capacity, tokens + delta * refill / 1000)

local allowed = 0
local retry = 0
if tokens >= cost then
  tokens = tokens - cost
  allowed = 1
else
  retry = math.ceil((cost - tokens) / refill * 1000)
end

redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], 'tokens', tokens, 'ts', now)
redis.call('PEXPIRE', KEYS[1], math.ceil(capacity / refill * 1000) * 2)
local reset = math.ceil((capacity - tokens) / refill * 1000)
return {allowed, math.floor(tokens), retry, reset}
`;

// Sliding window counter. KEYS[1]=base key (hash tag inside). ARGV: limit, windowMs
// Estimated count = current + previous * (1 - elapsedFractionOfCurrentWindow)
const SLIDING_WINDOW_LUA = `
local limit  = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local window = tonumber(ARGV[2])
local t   = redis.call('TIME')
local now = t[1] * 1000 + math.floor(t[2] / 1000)
local idx = math.floor(now / window)
local curKey  = KEYS[1] .. ':' .. idx
local prevKey = KEYS[1] .. ':' .. (idx - 1)

local cur  = tonumber(redis.call('GET', curKey) or '0')
local prev = tonumber(redis.call('GET', prevKey) or '0')
local elapsed = (now % window) / window
local estimated = cur + prev * (1 - elapsed)

local resetMs = window - (now % window)
if estimated + 1 > limit then
  return {0, 0, resetMs, resetMs}
end
cur = redis.call('INCR', curKey)
if cur == 1 then
  redis.call('PEXPIRE', curKey, window * 2)
end
local remaining = math.max(0, math.floor(limit - (cur + prev * (1 - elapsed))))
return {1, remaining, 0, resetMs}
`;

@Injectable()
export class RateLimiterService {
  constructor(@Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis) {}

  async consume(
    name: string,
    subject: string,
    limit: number,
    windowSeconds: number,
    algorithm: 'bucket' | 'window',
    cost = 1,
  ): Promise<LimitDecision> {
    const key = RedisKeys.rateLimit(name, subject);
    let r: number[];
    if (algorithm === 'bucket') {
      const refillPerSecond = limit / windowSeconds;
      r = (await this.redis.eval(TOKEN_BUCKET_LUA, 1, key, limit, refillPerSecond, cost)) as number[];
    } else {
      r = (await this.redis.eval(SLIDING_WINDOW_LUA, 1, key, limit, windowSeconds * 1000)) as number[];
    }
    return { allowed: r[0] === 1, limit, remaining: r[1], retryAfterMs: r[2], resetMs: r[3] };
  }
}
```

The sliding-window script builds its two key names inside Lua. That is fine on a single node and on Cluster only because of the shared `{...}` hash tag, but strictly speaking it violates the "declare all keys in KEYS" rule. State this trade-off if asked in an interview.

```ts
// src/rate-limit/rate-limit.guard.ts
import {
  CanActivate, ExecutionContext, HttpException, HttpStatus, Injectable, Logger,
} from '@nestjs/common';
import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core';
import type { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { RATE_LIMIT_KEY, RateLimitOptions } from './rate-limit.decorator';
import { RateLimiterService } from './rate-limiter.service';

@Injectable()
export class RateLimitGuard implements CanActivate {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(RateLimitGuard.name);

  constructor(
    private readonly reflector: Reflector,
    private readonly limiter: RateLimiterService,
  ) {}

  async canActivate(ctx: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean> {
    const opts = this.reflector.getAllAndOverride<RateLimitOptions | undefined>(
      RATE_LIMIT_KEY,
      [ctx.getHandler(), ctx.getClass()],
    );
    if (!opts) return true;

    const http = ctx.switchToHttp();
    const req = http.getRequest<Request & { user?: { id: string } }>();
    const res = http.getResponse<Response>();

    const subject = this.subject(opts, req);
    let decision;
    try {
      decision = await this.limiter.consume(
        opts.name, subject, opts.limit, opts.windowSeconds,
        opts.algorithm ?? 'bucket', opts.cost ?? 1,
      );
    } catch (err) {
      this.logger.error(`Rate limiter unavailable: ${(err as Error).message}`);
      if ((opts.onRedisError ?? 'open') === 'closed') {
        throw new HttpException('Service temporarily unavailable', HttpStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE);
      }
      return true; // fail open: availability over strictness
    }

    res.setHeader('RateLimit-Limit', decision.limit);
    res.setHeader('RateLimit-Remaining', decision.remaining);
    res.setHeader('RateLimit-Reset', Math.ceil(decision.resetMs / 1000));

    if (!decision.allowed) {
      res.setHeader('Retry-After', Math.max(1, Math.ceil(decision.retryAfterMs / 1000)));
      throw new HttpException(
        { statusCode: 429, message: 'Too many requests' },
        HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
      );
    }
    return true;
  }

  private subject(opts: RateLimitOptions, req: Request & { user?: { id: string } }): string {
    const ip = `ip:${req.ip}`; // needs app.set('trust proxy', 1) behind Nginx
    switch (opts.by ?? 'ip') {
      case 'user': return req.user ? `user:${req.user.id}` : ip;
      case 'user-or-ip': return req.user ? `user:${req.user.id}` : ip;
      default: return ip;
    }
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/rate-limit/rate-limit.module.ts
import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { RateLimitGuard } from './rate-limit.guard';
import { RateLimiterService } from './rate-limiter.service';

@Module({
  providers: [RateLimiterService, RateLimitGuard],
  exports: [RateLimiterService, RateLimitGuard],
})
export class RateLimitModule {}
```

```ts
// usage
@Post('login')
@UseGuards(RateLimitGuard)
@RateLimit({ name: 'login', limit: 5, windowSeconds: 60, by: 'ip', onRedisError: 'closed' })
login(/* ... */) { /* ... */ }

@Get('search')
@UseGuards(SessionGuard, RateLimitGuard) // SessionGuard first so req.user exists
@RateLimit({ name: 'search', limit: 30, windowSeconds: 60, by: 'user-or-ip' })
search(/* ... */) { /* ... */ }
```

Guard order matters: for per-user limits the authentication guard must run before the rate limit guard. For login (unauthenticated) rate limit by IP, and consider a second limit keyed by the submitted email to stop distributed credential stuffing.

### Failure handling

- Redis down: per-route policy. Public read endpoints fail open (do not turn a cache outage into a full API outage). Login, OTP, password reset fail closed or fall back to a small per-process in-memory limiter.
- Slow Redis: set a command timeout (`commandTimeout` in ioredis options) so the limiter does not add seconds to every request.
- Failover: the bucket state may be lost; users briefly get fresh burst capacity. Acceptable for rate limiting.
- Script atomicity: because everything happens inside one Lua call, there is no read-modify-write race between instances.

### Security considerations

- `req.ip` is only trustworthy with `trust proxy` configured for exactly your proxy hop count. Otherwise attackers spoof `X-Forwarded-For` and get unlimited buckets.
- IPv6: limit by /64, not by full address, or a single host can rotate through trillions of addresses.
- Prevent memory growth from key flooding: every key has a TTL; keep subjects bounded (do not use raw user-supplied strings as subjects).
- Do not leak exact internal limits for sensitive endpoints; `RateLimit-*` headers are a trade-off (helpful for API clients, informative for attackers).

### Performance considerations

- One round trip per limited request, O(1) work. Typical overhead is under 1 ms on the same network.
- `redis.eval` sends the script body each call; ioredis `defineCommand` or `evalsha` with caching reduces bandwidth. Redis caches scripts, so even `EVAL` is not recompiled.
- For extremely hot endpoints, combine with a local pre-check (per-process counters that sync periodically), accepting small overshoot.
- Limiter keys can be many (one per IP). Watch `used_memory`; with TTLs, memory tracks the number of recently active subjects.
- On Redis 7+ scripts replicate by effects, so calling `TIME` inside a script is allowed; on older versions you needed `redis.replicate_commands()`.

### Testing strategy

- Unit with a fake clock is hard because time is in Redis. Instead run integration tests against real Redis with small windows (limit 3 per 2 s): 3 requests pass, the fourth returns 429 with `Retry-After`; wait and verify recovery.
- Concurrency: 100 parallel requests with limit 10 must produce exactly 10 successes (proves atomicity).
- Boundary test for sliding window: send a burst at the end of a window and another at the start of the next; the estimate must block the second burst (fixed window would allow it).
- Redis stop test per policy: `open` route returns 200, `closed` route returns 503.

### Production deployment notes

- Keep Nginx `limit_req_zone` as a first layer (for example 20 r/s per IP with burst) and Redis limits for application rules.
- Return the same 429 JSON shape everywhere and log denies with route name and subject type (not raw PII) for abuse analysis.
- Roll out in "log only" mode first: compute the decision, log it, but allow the request. Enable enforcement after reviewing the numbers.
- Use a dedicated Redis (or DB index with no eviction pressure) so cache evictions cannot erase limiter state and vice versa.


---

## 14.5 Real-time notification system

### Requirements

- Deliver a notification to a user in real time through Socket.IO, no matter which Nest instance holds that user's socket.
- Persist notifications so offline users (and users who reconnect after a network blip) can fetch them later.
- Maintain an unread counter, cheap to read on every page load.
- Pagination of history, bounded storage per user.
- Authenticate the socket with the same session cookie used by REST (project 14.2).

### Architecture

```
  Producers (any service / BullMQ worker)
        |  NotificationService.send(userId, payload)
        v
  +-------------------------- Lua (atomic) -----------------------------+
  | XADD shop:notif:inbox:<uid> MAXLEN ~ 200 * p <json>   (durable)     |
  | INCR shop:notif:unread:<uid>                                         |
  | PUBLISH shop:notif:ch:<uid> "<id> <json>"             (live, 0..N)   |
  +----------------------------------------------------------------------+
        |                                   |
     [ Redis ] ---- Pub/Sub message ---> Nest instance A (user has socket here)
                  \-- (no subscriber) -> instance B does nothing
                                            |
                                   Socket.IO room user:<uid> --> browser

  Offline / reconnect:  client connects with auth.lastEventId
        -> server: XRANGE inbox (lastEventId + ... -> replays the gap
```

### Redis data structures

| Need | Structure | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Live fan-out to instances | Pub/Sub, one channel per user | At-most-once, no storage. Fast. |
| Per-user history | Stream `inbox` (`XADD`, `XREVRANGE`) | Entry ids are time-ordered cursors; `MAXLEN ~` caps size |
| Unread count | String counter | O(1) read |
| Durable async delivery (email/push for offline users) | Global stream + consumer group | `XREADGROUP`, `XACK`, retry via pending list |

Pub/Sub vs Streams, the decision you must be able to explain:

| | Pub/Sub | Streams |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery | At-most-once; subscriber offline = message lost | Persisted; consumers read from any id |
| Fan-out | Every subscriber gets a copy | Each consumer group gets a copy; within a group, work is shared |
| Backpressure | None (slow subscriber's buffer grows, may be disconnected by `client-output-buffer-limit pubsub`) | Consumers pull at their pace |
| Best for | Ephemeral "poke the socket" signals | Inbox history, replay, work queues |

This design uses both: the stream is the source of truth, and Pub/Sub is only the low-latency doorbell. Losing a Pub/Sub message is harmless because the client can replay from the stream.

Library note: `@socket.io/redis-adapter` is a Socket.IO library feature that also uses Redis Pub/Sub to broadcast between instances. It is a fine alternative for `io.to(room).emit()` across nodes. This project hand-rolls per-user channels so you can see the Redis mechanics and combine delivery with persistence in one atomic script.

### Key design

```
shop:notif:inbox:<userId>     STREAM   entries: p=<json payload>        TTL 30 days (refreshed on write)
shop:notif:unread:<userId>    STRING   integer                          TTL 30 days
shop:notif:ch:<userId>        CHANNEL  message "<streamId> <json>"
shop:notif:stream             STREAM   global event feed for workers    MAXLEN ~ 10000
```

On Redis Cluster, `inbox` and `unread` must be in one slot for the Lua script. Pass the user id wrapped in a hash tag, for example `RedisKeys.notifInbox(`{${userId}}`)`, and do the same for `unread`. Pub/Sub channels are not slot-bound for classic `PUBLISH` (it is broadcast across the cluster); that is why the channel name is passed as an `ARGV` rather than a `KEYS` entry. Sharded Pub/Sub `SPUBLISH`/`SSUBSCRIBE` `[7.0+]` is slot-aware and scales better on large clusters.

### TTL strategy

- Inbox and unread: 30 days after the last write (`EXPIRE` refreshed by the script). Inactive users cost nothing after that.
- Inbox length also capped at about 200 entries with `MAXLEN ~ 200` (approximate trimming, cheaper because it trims whole macro nodes).
- Pub/Sub has no TTL: it stores nothing.
- Long term history (audit, "all notifications ever") belongs in MongoDB/PostgreSQL; Redis is the hot window.

### Data flow

1. A producer calls `send(userId, payload)`.
2. The Lua script appends to the inbox stream, increments unread, publishes `"<id> <json>"` to the user's channel, returns the stream id.
3. Each Nest instance holds one dedicated subscriber connection. It subscribes to `notif:ch:<uid>` when the first socket for that user connects on that instance, and unsubscribes when the last one leaves.
4. On a message the instance emits to the Socket.IO room `user:<uid>`.
5. On (re)connect, the client sends `auth: { lastEventId }`; the server first subscribes, then replays `XRANGE inbox (lastEventId +`. Subscribing before replaying avoids a gap; the client dedupes by `id`.
6. REST: `GET /notifications` (history), `GET /notifications/unread-count`, `POST /notifications/read-all`.

### Code implementation

```ts
// src/notifications/notification.service.ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { RedisKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

export interface NotificationPayload {
  type: string;
  title: string;
  body?: string;
  data?: Record<string, unknown>;
  createdAt?: number;
}

export interface StoredNotification extends NotificationPayload {
  id: string; // stream id, e.g. 1731999999000-0
}

// KEYS: 1 inbox, 2 unread. ARGV: 1 json, 2 maxlen, 3 ttlSeconds, 4 channel
const NOTIFY_LUA = `
local id = redis.call('XADD', KEYS[1], 'MAXLEN', '~', ARGV[2], '*', 'p', ARGV[1])
redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], tonumber(ARGV[3]))
redis.call('INCR', KEYS[2])
redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[2], tonumber(ARGV[3]))
redis.call('PUBLISH', ARGV[4], id .. ' ' .. ARGV[1])
return id
`;

@Injectable()
export class NotificationService {
  private readonly maxLen = 200;
  private readonly ttl = 60 * 60 * 24 * 30;

  constructor(@Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis) {}

  async send(userId: string, payload: NotificationPayload): Promise<string> {
    const json = JSON.stringify({ ...payload, createdAt: payload.createdAt ?? Date.now() });
    const id = (await this.redis.eval(
      NOTIFY_LUA,
      2,
      RedisKeys.notifInbox(userId),
      RedisKeys.notifUnread(userId),
      json,
      this.maxLen,
      this.ttl,
      RedisKeys.notifChannel(userId),
    )) as string;

    // Durable feed for offline channels (email/push workers). Separate command: on
    // Cluster it lives in another slot, so it cannot join the Lua script above.
    await this.redis.xadd(RedisKeys.notifStream, 'MAXLEN', '~', 10_000, '*', 'userId', userId, 'inboxId', id);
    return id;
  }

  /** Newest first. Pass the oldest id you have as `beforeId` for the next page. */
  async list(userId: string, beforeId?: string, count = 20): Promise<StoredNotification[]> {
    const end = beforeId ? `(${beforeId}` : '+'; // exclusive range [6.2+]
    const rows = await this.redis.xrevrange(RedisKeys.notifInbox(userId), end, '-', 'COUNT', count);
    return rows.map(([id, fields]) => ({ id, ...(JSON.parse(fields[1]) as NotificationPayload) }));
  }

  /** Oldest first: everything after lastId, used for reconnect replay. */
  async since(userId: string, lastId: string, count = 100): Promise<StoredNotification[]> {
    const rows = await this.redis.xrange(RedisKeys.notifInbox(userId), `(${lastId}`, '+', 'COUNT', count);
    return rows.map(([id, fields]) => ({ id, ...(JSON.parse(fields[1]) as NotificationPayload) }));
  }

  async unreadCount(userId: string): Promise<number> {
    return Number((await this.redis.get(RedisKeys.notifUnread(userId))) ?? 0);
  }

  async markAllRead(userId: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.redis.set(RedisKeys.notifUnread(userId), 0, 'EX', this.ttl);
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/notifications/notifications.gateway.ts
import { Inject, Logger, OnModuleDestroy, OnModuleInit } from '@nestjs/common';
import {
  OnGatewayConnection, OnGatewayDisconnect, WebSocketGateway, WebSocketServer,
} from '@nestjs/websockets';
import { parse as parseCookie } from 'cookie';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { Server, Socket } from 'socket.io';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { RedisKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';
import { SessionService } from '../session/session.service';
import { SESSION_COOKIE } from '../session/session.guard';
import { NotificationService } from './notification.service';

@WebSocketGateway({
  namespace: '/notifications',
  cors: { origin: process.env.WEB_ORIGIN, credentials: true },
})
export class NotificationsGateway
  implements OnGatewayConnection, OnGatewayDisconnect, OnModuleInit, OnModuleDestroy
{
  @WebSocketServer() server!: Server;

  private readonly logger = new Logger(NotificationsGateway.name);
  private sub!: Redis;
  /** userId -> number of local sockets */
  private readonly local = new Map<string, number>();
  private readonly channelPrefix = RedisKeys.notifChannel('');

  constructor(
    @Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis,
    private readonly sessions: SessionService,
    private readonly notifications: NotificationService,
  ) {}

  onModuleInit(): void {
    // A connection in subscriber mode cannot run normal commands: use a dedicated one.
    this.sub = this.redis.duplicate();
    this.sub.on('error', (e) => this.logger.error(`sub error: ${e.message}`));
    this.sub.on('message', (channel: string, message: string) => {
      const userId = channel.slice(this.channelPrefix.length);
      const i = message.indexOf(' ');
      const id = message.slice(0, i);
      const payload = JSON.parse(message.slice(i + 1)) as Record<string, unknown>;
      this.server.to(`user:${userId}`).emit('notification', { id, ...payload });
    });
    // ioredis re-subscribes automatically after a reconnect (autoResubscribe defaults to true).
  }

  async onModuleDestroy(): Promise<void> {
    await this.sub.quit();
  }

  async handleConnection(client: Socket): Promise<void> {
    try {
      const raw = parseCookie(client.handshake.headers.cookie ?? '')[SESSION_COOKIE];
      const session = await this.sessions.validate(raw);
      if (!session) throw new Error('unauthenticated');

      const userId = session.userId;
      client.data.userId = userId;
      await client.join(`user:${userId}`);

      const n = (this.local.get(userId) ?? 0) + 1;
      this.local.set(userId, n);
      if (n === 1) await this.sub.subscribe(RedisKeys.notifChannel(userId));

      // Replay AFTER subscribing so no message falls in the gap.
      const lastId = client.handshake.auth?.lastEventId as string | undefined;
      if (lastId && /^\d+-\d+$/.test(lastId)) {
        const missed = await this.notifications.since(userId, lastId);
        for (const m of missed) client.emit('notification', m);
      }
    } catch {
      client.disconnect(true);
    }
  }

  async handleDisconnect(client: Socket): Promise<void> {
    const userId = client.data.userId as string | undefined;
    if (!userId) return;
    const n = (this.local.get(userId) ?? 1) - 1;
    if (n <= 0) {
      this.local.delete(userId);
      await this.sub.unsubscribe(RedisKeys.notifChannel(userId)).catch(() => undefined);
    } else {
      this.local.set(userId, n);
    }
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/notifications/notifications.controller.ts
import { Controller, Get, HttpCode, Post, Query, Req, UseGuards } from '@nestjs/common';
import type { Request } from 'express';
import { SessionGuard } from '../session/session.guard';
import { NotificationService } from './notification.service';

type Authed = Request & { session: { userId: string } };

@Controller('notifications')
@UseGuards(SessionGuard)
export class NotificationsController {
  constructor(private readonly notifications: NotificationService) {}

  @Get()
  list(@Req() req: Authed, @Query('before') before?: string, @Query('limit') limit = '20') {
    return this.notifications.list(req.session.userId, before, Math.min(Number(limit) || 20, 100));
  }

  @Get('unread-count')
  async unread(@Req() req: Authed) {
    return { count: await this.notifications.unreadCount(req.session.userId) };
  }

  @Post('read-all')
  @HttpCode(204)
  async readAll(@Req() req: Authed) {
    await this.notifications.markAllRead(req.session.userId);
  }
}
```

Durable fan-out for offline channels (email/push) is a standard consumer-group worker over `notif:stream`: `XGROUP CREATE shop:notif:stream push-workers $ MKSTREAM`, workers call `XREADGROUP GROUP push-workers <consumer> COUNT 50 BLOCK 5000 STREAMS shop:notif:stream >`, send, then `XACK`. A periodic `XAUTOCLAIM` `[6.2+]` takes over entries stuck with a crashed consumer. BullMQ is the simpler choice if you only need retries and delays; use raw Streams when you need replay and several independent consumers.

### Failure handling

| Failure | Result |
|---|---|
| Redis down during `send` | Throw; caller retries through a BullMQ job (the Lua script is not idempotent, so use a business-level dedupe id if retries can overlap). |
| Pub/Sub message lost (subscriber reconnecting) | Inbox still has it. Client calls replay on reconnect (`lastEventId`) and refreshes unread count. |
| Subscriber connection drops | ioredis reconnects and resubscribes automatically; messages published during the gap are recovered via replay. |
| Instance crashes | Sockets drop; clients reconnect to another instance and replay. |
| Partial failure: stream write ok, global `xadd` fails | User still gets the in-app notification; only the email/push worker misses it. Log and alert, or write both in one Lua on a single-node deployment. |
| Slow browser | Socket.IO buffers per socket; set limits and disconnect abusers. |

### Security considerations

- Authenticate during the handshake; never accept a `userId` from the client. Room and channel names are derived on the server from the session.
- Validate `lastEventId` format (as above) before using it in a Redis range query.
- Restrict CORS origin and require `credentials`. Reject WebSocket upgrades from unknown `Origin` headers.
- Payloads are rendered in a browser: treat `title`/`body` as untrusted text and escape them on the client.
- Limit the producer API (who may send to whom) at the service layer; Redis itself has no per-user authorization.
- Pub/Sub messages are visible to anyone with Redis access (`SUBSCRIBE`/`MONITOR`): use ACLs and network isolation, and keep sensitive content out of payloads (send ids, fetch details over REST).

### Performance considerations

- `PUBLISH` cost is proportional to the number of subscribers of that channel, which is tiny with per-user channels. Redis handles very large numbers of channels, but watch `PUBSUB NUMSUB` and the memory of the channel dictionary; for massive fan-out (broadcast to everyone) use one shared channel instead of millions of per-user publishes.
- The script is O(1) apart from approximate trimming.
- One subscriber connection per Nest process, not per socket.
- `client-output-buffer-limit pubsub` protects Redis from a slow subscriber; a disconnected subscriber is recovered by replay.
- Avoid sending the full history on connect; replay is capped at 100 and the REST endpoint pages the rest.

### Testing strategy

- Unit: payload encoding/decoding (`"<id> <json>"` split), `lastEventId` validation.
- Integration with two Nest app instances against one Redis (Testcontainers): connect a socket to instance A, call `send` from instance B, assert the event arrives on A.
- Offline: send while the user is disconnected, connect with `lastEventId`, assert replay and unread count.
- Trimming: send 300 notifications and assert `XLEN` stays near 200.
- Chaos: `CLIENT KILL TYPE pubsub`, confirm automatic resubscription and gap recovery.

### Production deployment notes

- Nginx must forward WebSocket upgrades: `proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade"; proxy_read_timeout 75s;` (longer than the Socket.IO ping interval).
- With PM2 cluster or several containers, enable sticky routing for the Socket.IO HTTP long-polling transport (for example `ip_hash` in Nginx) or force `transports: ['websocket']`.
- Persistence: the inbox is user-visible data, so enable AOF `everysec`, or accept losing up to the last second after a crash.
- Metrics: sockets per instance, publish rate, replay count, stream lengths, unread counter distribution, `pubsub_channels` from `INFO stats`.

---

## 14.6 Online user presence tracking

### Requirements

- Know whether a user is online (any device active in the last N seconds).
- Support multiple devices per user (web + mobile).
- Count online users and list them with pagination.
- Bulk lookup ("which of my 50 friends are online?") in one call.
- Cleanup of crashed clients (no clean disconnect), and optionally emit online/offline events.

### Architecture

```
 Clients (heartbeat every 25 s over Socket.IO, timeout 60 s)
      |
 NestJS: PresenceGateway --> PresenceService
      |                             |
      |   Lua heartbeat (atomic)    |            Sweeper (@Interval, every instance, safe)
      v                             v                  |
  [ Redis ]  shop:presence:z           ZSET user -> lastSeen(ms), max over devices
             shop:presence:devs:<uid>  ZSET device -> lastSeen
             shop:presence:d:<uid>:<dev>  STRING device metadata, TTL
                                                       v
                                  Lua sweep: ZRANGEBYSCORE -inf cutoff + ZREM (atomic)
                                           -> PUBLISH presence events ("offline")
```

### Redis data structures: comparing approaches

| | A. Key per user with TTL | B. Sorted set, score = lastSeen |
|---|---|---|
| Heartbeat | `SET presence:u:42 1 EX 60` | `ZADD presence:z <now> 42` |
| Is user online? | `EXISTS` (O(1)) | `ZSCORE` then compare with cutoff (O(1)) |
| Online count | Needs `SCAN` over `presence:u:*`, or a separate counter that can drift | `ZCOUNT z (now-60s) +inf`, O(log N) |
| List online users | `SCAN` (slow, unordered) | `ZRANGEBYSCORE` with `LIMIT`, paginated |
| Bulk status | `MGET`/many `EXISTS` | `ZMSCORE` `[6.2+]`, one command |
| Expiry | Automatic, no cleanup job | Entries stay until swept; the score check makes stale entries harmless, the sweeper only reclaims memory |
| Offline event | Keyspace notifications (`Ex`), at-most-once, off by default | Sweeper detects exactly which members crossed the cutoff |
| Memory | One key + overhead per user | ~tens of bytes per member in one key |
| Weakness | No cheap aggregate queries | One large key; cluster needs sharding by bucket |

Recommended: **B (sorted set)** for the global view, because counts, listings and bulk checks are the real product requirements. Use per-device state (keys with TTL) only for metadata. Approach A is the right answer when you only ever ask "is user X online?" and never count or list.

### Key design

```
shop:presence:z                  ZSET    member=<userId>   score=<lastSeen ms>  (max across devices)
shop:presence:devs:<userId>      ZSET    member=<deviceId> score=<lastSeen ms>
shop:presence:d:<userId>:<dev>   STRING  JSON metadata ({"platform":"ios"}), TTL
shop:presence:events             CHANNEL "online <uid>" / "offline <uid>"
```

Multi-device rule: a user is online if at least one device heartbeat is newer than the cutoff. The global score stores the newest device timestamp. On a clean disconnect of one device, the script recalculates the score from the remaining devices.

### TTL strategy

- Timeout (online window): 60 s, heartbeat every 20 to 25 s (about 2 to 3 missed beats tolerated).
- `devs:<uid>` and device metadata keys: TTL 120 s refreshed on heartbeat, so abandoned devices vanish without a sweeper.
- Global ZSET members: removed by the sweeper (cutoff = now - timeout) and by clean disconnects; the ZSET key itself has no TTL.
- Optional "last seen" feature: before removing an offline user, copy `lastSeen` into PostgreSQL/MongoDB (batch in the sweeper).

### Data flow

```
connect    -> heartbeat(user, device)      -> script returns 1 if user just came online -> publish "online"
every 25 s -> heartbeat(user, device)
disconnect -> disconnect(user, device)     -> script returns 1 if it was the last device -> publish "offline"
crash      -> no message; after 60 s the score is stale
sweeper    -> sweep(cutoff)                -> ZREM stale members atomically -> publish "offline" for each
read       -> ZMSCORE / ZCOUNT / ZRANGEBYSCORE compare against (now - 60 s)
```

### Code implementation

```ts
// src/presence/presence.service.ts
import { Inject, Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Interval } from '@nestjs/schedule';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { RedisKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

// KEYS: 1 global zset, 2 user's devices zset, 3 device meta
// ARGV: 1 userId, 2 deviceId, 3 now(ms), 4 cutoff(ms), 5 meta json, 6 ttl(s)
// returns 1 if the user just came online, else 0
const HEARTBEAT_LUA = `
local was = redis.call('ZSCORE', KEYS[1], ARGV[1])
redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', KEYS[2], '-inf', ARGV[4])
redis.call('ZADD', KEYS[2], ARGV[3], ARGV[2])
redis.call('ZADD', KEYS[1], ARGV[3], ARGV[1])
redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[2], tonumber(ARGV[6]))
redis.call('SET', KEYS[3], ARGV[5], 'EX', tonumber(ARGV[6]))
if was and tonumber(was) >= tonumber(ARGV[4]) then
  return 0
end
return 1
`;

// KEYS: 1 global, 2 devices, 3 device meta. ARGV: 1 userId, 2 deviceId
// returns 1 if the user went offline (no devices left)
const DISCONNECT_LUA = `
redis.call('ZREM', KEYS[2], ARGV[2])
redis.call('DEL', KEYS[3])
local newest = redis.call('ZREVRANGE', KEYS[2], 0, 0, 'WITHSCORES')
if #newest == 0 then
  redis.call('ZREM', KEYS[1], ARGV[1])
  return 1
end
redis.call('ZADD', KEYS[1], newest[2], ARGV[1])
return 0
`;

// KEYS: 1 global. ARGV: 1 cutoff, 2 batch size. Returns removed members.
const SWEEP_LUA = `
local stale = redis.call('ZRANGEBYSCORE', KEYS[1], '-inf', ARGV[1], 'LIMIT', 0, tonumber(ARGV[2]))
if #stale > 0 then
  redis.call('ZREM', KEYS[1], unpack(stale))
end
return stale
`;

@Injectable()
export class PresenceService {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(PresenceService.name);
  readonly timeoutMs = 60_000;
  private readonly ttlSeconds = 120;

  constructor(@Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis) {}

  async heartbeat(userId: string, deviceId: string, meta: Record<string, string> = {}): Promise<boolean> {
    const now = Date.now();
    const cameOnline = (await this.redis.eval(
      HEARTBEAT_LUA, 3,
      RedisKeys.presenceZ,
      RedisKeys.presenceDevices(userId),
      RedisKeys.presenceDevice(userId, deviceId),
      userId, deviceId, now, now - this.timeoutMs, JSON.stringify(meta), this.ttlSeconds,
    )) as number;
    if (cameOnline === 1) await this.publish('online', userId);
    return cameOnline === 1;
  }

  async disconnect(userId: string, deviceId: string): Promise<void> {
    const wentOffline = (await this.redis.eval(
      DISCONNECT_LUA, 3,
      RedisKeys.presenceZ,
      RedisKeys.presenceDevices(userId),
      RedisKeys.presenceDevice(userId, deviceId),
      userId, deviceId,
    )) as number;
    if (wentOffline === 1) await this.publish('offline', userId);
  }

  async isOnline(userId: string): Promise<boolean> {
    const score = await this.redis.zscore(RedisKeys.presenceZ, userId);
    return score !== null && Number(score) >= Date.now() - this.timeoutMs;
  }

  /** One round trip for many users. ZMSCORE [6.2+] */
  async statusOf(userIds: string[]): Promise<Record<string, boolean>> {
    if (userIds.length === 0) return {};
    const scores = await this.redis.zmscore(RedisKeys.presenceZ, ...userIds);
    const cutoff = Date.now() - this.timeoutMs;
    return Object.fromEntries(userIds.map((id, i) => [id, scores[i] !== null && Number(scores[i]) >= cutoff]));
  }

  async onlineCount(): Promise<number> {
    return this.redis.zcount(RedisKeys.presenceZ, Date.now() - this.timeoutMs, '+inf');
  }

  /** Most recently active first, paginated. ZRANGE ... BYSCORE REV LIMIT [6.2+] */
  async listOnline(offset = 0, limit = 50): Promise<string[]> {
    return this.redis.zrange(
      RedisKeys.presenceZ, '+inf', Date.now() - this.timeoutMs, 'BYSCORE', 'REV', 'LIMIT', offset, limit,
    );
  }

  async devicesOf(userId: string): Promise<string[]> {
    return this.redis.zrangebyscore(RedisKeys.presenceDevices(userId), Date.now() - this.timeoutMs, '+inf');
  }

  /** Runs on every instance; the Lua script makes each stale member be returned once. */
  @Interval(15_000)
  async sweep(): Promise<void> {
    try {
      const stale = (await this.redis.eval(
        SWEEP_LUA, 1, RedisKeys.presenceZ, Date.now() - this.timeoutMs, 500,
      )) as string[];
      for (const userId of stale) await this.publish('offline', userId);
      if (stale.length) this.logger.debug(`swept ${stale.length} stale users`);
    } catch (err) {
      this.logger.warn(`presence sweep failed: ${(err as Error).message}`);
    }
  }

  private publish(event: 'online' | 'offline', userId: string): Promise<number> {
    return this.redis.publish(RedisKeys.presenceEvents, `${event} ${userId}`);
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/presence/presence.gateway.ts
import { Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import {
  ConnectedSocket, OnGatewayConnection, OnGatewayDisconnect, SubscribeMessage,
  WebSocketGateway,
} from '@nestjs/websockets';
import { parse as parseCookie } from 'cookie';
import { Socket } from 'socket.io';
import { SessionService } from '../session/session.service';
import { SESSION_COOKIE } from '../session/session.guard';
import { PresenceService } from './presence.service';

@WebSocketGateway({ namespace: '/presence', cors: { origin: process.env.WEB_ORIGIN, credentials: true } })
export class PresenceGateway implements OnGatewayConnection, OnGatewayDisconnect {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(PresenceGateway.name);

  constructor(
    private readonly sessions: SessionService,
    private readonly presence: PresenceService,
  ) {}

  async handleConnection(client: Socket): Promise<void> {
    const raw = parseCookie(client.handshake.headers.cookie ?? '')[SESSION_COOKIE];
    const session = await this.sessions.validate(raw).catch(() => null);
    if (!session) return void client.disconnect(true);

    client.data.userId = session.userId;
    // Server-assigned socket id is the device id: a client cannot forge other users' devices.
    // For "stable device" semantics, sign a device cookie and use that instead.
    client.data.deviceId = client.id;
    await this.presence
      .heartbeat(session.userId, client.id, { ua: String(client.handshake.headers['user-agent'] ?? '').slice(0, 100) })
      .catch((e) => this.logger.warn(`heartbeat failed: ${e.message}`));
  }

  @SubscribeMessage('heartbeat')
  async onHeartbeat(@ConnectedSocket() client: Socket): Promise<void> {
    const { userId, deviceId } = client.data as { userId?: string; deviceId?: string };
    if (!userId || !deviceId) return;
    await this.presence.heartbeat(userId, deviceId).catch(() => undefined);
  }

  async handleDisconnect(client: Socket): Promise<void> {
    const { userId, deviceId } = client.data as { userId?: string; deviceId?: string };
    if (userId && deviceId) await this.presence.disconnect(userId, deviceId).catch(() => undefined);
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/presence/presence.controller.ts
import { BadRequestException, Controller, Get, Query, UseGuards } from '@nestjs/common';
import { SessionGuard } from '../session/session.guard';
import { PresenceService } from './presence.service';

@Controller('presence')
@UseGuards(SessionGuard)
export class PresenceController {
  constructor(private readonly presence: PresenceService) {}

  /** GET /presence/status?ids=1,2,3  (max 100 ids) */
  @Get('status')
  status(@Query('ids') ids = '') {
    const list = ids.split(',').filter(Boolean);
    if (list.length > 100) throw new BadRequestException('max 100 ids');
    return this.presence.statusOf(list);
  }

  @Get('count')
  async count() {
    return { online: await this.presence.onlineCount() };
  }
}
```

A note on the clock: the cutoff comes from the Nest process clock. The window is tens of seconds, so millisecond NTP skew is irrelevant here (unlike the rate limiter, which takes time from Redis `TIME`). If you want zero dependence on instance clocks, read `TIME` inside the scripts.

### Failure handling

- Redis down: presence calls fail; the gateway swallows errors (`catch`) so sockets keep working. Treat unknown as "offline/unknown" in the UI, never block chat or core flows on presence.
- After a Redis restart without persistence, the ZSET is empty and everyone re-appears at their next heartbeat (within 25 s). That is acceptable; presence is soft state, so disable persistence for this instance or keep it on a cache node.
- Instance crash: its sockets disconnect abruptly; their devices time out and the sweeper marks users offline after at most about 60 s plus the sweep interval.
- Sweeper running on many instances: the Lua script is atomic, so each stale member is returned to exactly one caller and the offline event is published once.
- Race between sweeper and a fresh heartbeat: both are Lua scripts and cannot interleave; if the heartbeat wins, the score is newer than the cutoff and the member is not swept.
- Flapping network: debounce "offline" notifications to other users (for example 10 s) at the UI/consumer side to avoid online/offline spam.

### Security considerations

- Privacy: presence reveals behavior. Check authorization before returning status (friends only, same tenant, user's "appear offline" setting). The `status` endpoint above must be filtered by a relationship check in real code.
- The user id and device id come from the validated session and the server-side socket id, never from client payloads.
- Cap bulk lookups (100 ids) and rate limit them (14.4) to prevent scraping the whole user base.
- Metadata (user agent) is truncated and not trusted.

### Performance considerations

- Heartbeat is one Lua call with O(log N) operations. At 100k concurrent users with a 25 s heartbeat that is about 4k calls per second, easy for a single Redis. Reduce load by lengthening the interval, or sending heartbeats only on activity.
- `ZCOUNT`, `ZMSCORE`, `ZRANGE ... BYSCORE` are O(log N) plus the returned items.
- One big ZSET of millions of members is fine on a single node (about tens of MB per million members). On Cluster, shard by `bucket = hash(userId) % 16` into `presence:z:{bucket}`; the multi-key Lua script then cannot update the global and per-user keys together, so split it into pipelined commands.
- Sweep in batches (500) to keep script run time short; Redis is single-threaded and a long script blocks everyone.

### Testing strategy

- Unit: `statusOf` cutoff logic with mocked `ZMSCORE` results.
- Integration: heartbeat then `isOnline` true; wait beyond a shortened timeout, false; two devices, disconnect one, user still online; disconnect the last device, offline event published.
- Sweeper: insert a stale member, run `sweep()` from two service instances concurrently, assert exactly one `offline` event.
- Soak: simulate 10k sockets with `socket.io-client` and verify CPU and `ZCARD` stability.

### Production deployment notes

- Put presence on a separate Redis (or at least separate from durable data): high write rate, disposable data, `appendonly no` is acceptable.
- Give the sweeper `@Interval` jitter if you run dozens of instances; correctness does not depend on it.
- Alert on `ZCARD` growth without matching connection growth (sweeper stuck) and on heartbeat error rate.
- For web-only products where users close tabs without a clean disconnect, rely on the timeout, not on `disconnect`.

---

## 14.7 Leaderboard and ranking system

### Requirements

- Increment a player's score from game events; show top N, a player's rank, and the players around them.
- All-time, daily and weekly boards.
- Deterministic ties (earlier achiever ranks higher).
- Pagination of large boards.
- Safe retries: a replayed score event must not be counted twice.

### Architecture

```
 Game/Order service --event{id, userId, points}--> LeaderboardService.record()
                                                        |
                                      Lua (atomic, idempotent via event id)
                                                        v
    [ Redis ]  lb:<game>:all            ZSET  (forever)
               lb:<game>:d:YYYYMMDD     ZSET  (TTL 8 days)
               lb:<game>:w:YYYY-Www     ZSET  (TTL 15 days)
               lb:<game>:ev:<eventId>   STRING dedupe marker (TTL 1 day)
                                                        ^
   GET /top, /me, /around  <---- ZRANGE REV / ZREVRANK -+       Source of truth: PostgreSQL score events
   rolling 7 days = ZUNIONSTORE of 7 daily boards (cached, rebuilt by a job)
```

### Redis data structures

| Need | Command(s) |
|---|---|
| Add points | `ZINCRBY key delta member` |
| Keep best score only | `ZADD key GT score member` `[6.2+]` (updates only if the new score is greater) |
| Top N | `ZRANGE key 0 N-1 REV WITHSCORES` `[6.2+]` |
| Rank of a user (0-based, 0 = top) | `ZREVRANK key member` |
| Neighbors | `ZRANGE key (rank-k) (rank+k) REV WITHSCORES` |
| Total players | `ZCARD` |
| Combine boards | `ZUNIONSTORE dest numkeys k1 k2 ... [WEIGHTS ...] [AGGREGATE SUM]` |
| Competition rank (1,2,2,4) | `ZCOUNT key (score +inf` + 1 |

### Key design

```
shop:lb:<game>:all
shop:lb:<game>:d:20261119            (UTC day)
shop:lb:<game>:w:2026-W47            (ISO week, UTC)
shop:lb:<game>:ev:<eventId>          idempotency marker (added to RedisKeys below)
```

Add one key builder to `RedisKeys` (Module 1 style): `lbEvent: (game: string, id: string) => `${APP}:lb:${game}:ev:${id}``. User display names are read from the Module 1 `RedisKeys.user(id)` string keys with one `MGET`, exactly like `DemoService.getMany`.

### TTL strategy

- All-time: no TTL.
- Daily: 8 days (keeps yesterday and a week of daily boards for rolling unions).
- Weekly: 15 days. Set with `EXPIRE key ttl NX` `[7.0+]`, which only sets a TTL if none exists, so later increments do not extend the board's life.
- Dedupe marker: 24 hours, longer than your producer's maximum retry window.
- Derived rolling board: 60 s TTL (acts as a cache, rebuilt on demand or by schedule).

### Data flow

1. The producer calls `record({ eventId, game, userId, points })` (normally from a BullMQ worker after the DB commit).
2. The Lua script: `SET dedupe NX EX`; if the marker already existed return `-1` (duplicate); else `ZINCRBY` all-time, daily and weekly boards, set TTLs with `NX`, return the new all-time score.
3. Reads: `top` uses `ZRANGE REV`; `me` uses a pipeline of `ZREVRANK` + `ZSCORE`, then fetches neighbors with a range around the rank; `ZCARD` gives the total.
4. Names are hydrated with `MGET` on `RedisKeys.user(id)`.

### Code implementation

```ts
// src/leaderboard/leaderboard.service.ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { RedisKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

export type Period = 'all' | 'daily' | 'weekly' | 'rolling7';

export interface Entry {
  rank: number;       // 1-based position (ties broken by member name in plain ZSET)
  userId: string;
  name: string | null;
  score: number;
}

export interface RecordInput {
  eventId: string;
  game: string;
  userId: string;
  points: number;
}

const DAILY_TTL = 60 * 60 * 24 * 8;
const WEEKLY_TTL = 60 * 60 * 24 * 15;
const DEDUPE_TTL = 60 * 60 * 24;

// KEYS: 1 dedupe, 2 all, 3 daily, 4 weekly
// ARGV: 1 member, 2 delta, 3 dedupeTtl, 4 dailyTtl, 5 weeklyTtl
// Returns the new all-time score (string) or -1 when the event was already applied.
const RECORD_LUA = `
if not redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], '1', 'NX', 'EX', tonumber(ARGV[3])) then
  return '-1'
end
local total = redis.call('ZINCRBY', KEYS[2], ARGV[2], ARGV[1])
redis.call('ZINCRBY', KEYS[3], ARGV[2], ARGV[1])
redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[3], tonumber(ARGV[4]), 'NX')
redis.call('ZINCRBY', KEYS[4], ARGV[2], ARGV[1])
redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[4], tonumber(ARGV[5]), 'NX')
return total
`;

export function utcDay(d = new Date()): string {
  return d.toISOString().slice(0, 10).replace(/-/g, '');
}

export function isoWeek(d = new Date()): string {
  const t = new Date(Date.UTC(d.getUTCFullYear(), d.getUTCMonth(), d.getUTCDate()));
  const day = t.getUTCDay() || 7;
  t.setUTCDate(t.getUTCDate() + 4 - day); // Thursday decides the ISO year
  const yearStart = new Date(Date.UTC(t.getUTCFullYear(), 0, 1));
  const week = Math.ceil(((t.getTime() - yearStart.getTime()) / 86_400_000 + 1) / 7);
  return `${t.getUTCFullYear()}-W${String(week).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

@Injectable()
export class LeaderboardService {
  constructor(@Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis) {}

  /** Idempotent: calling twice with the same eventId counts once. Returns null if duplicate. */
  async record(input: RecordInput, at = new Date()): Promise<number | null> {
    const res = (await this.redis.eval(
      RECORD_LUA,
      4,
      RedisKeys.lbEvent(input.game, input.eventId),
      RedisKeys.lbAllTime(input.game),
      RedisKeys.lbDaily(input.game, utcDay(at)),
      RedisKeys.lbWeekly(input.game, isoWeek(at)),
      input.userId,
      input.points,
      DEDUPE_TTL,
      DAILY_TTL,
      WEEKLY_TTL,
    )) as string;
    return res === '-1' ? null : Number(res);
  }

  /** Best-score-wins variant (e.g. "highest run"): ZADD GT only raises the score [6.2+]. */
  async submitBest(game: string, userId: string, score: number): Promise<void> {
    await this.redis.zadd(RedisKeys.lbAllTime(game), 'GT', score, userId);
  }

  private boardKey(game: string, period: Period, at = new Date()): string {
    switch (period) {
      case 'all': return RedisKeys.lbAllTime(game);
      case 'daily': return RedisKeys.lbDaily(game, utcDay(at));
      case 'weekly': return RedisKeys.lbWeekly(game, isoWeek(at));
      case 'rolling7': return `${RedisKeys.lbAllTime(game)}:rolling7`;
    }
  }

  /** Paginated top list: page is 1-based. */
  async top(game: string, period: Period, page = 1, pageSize = 20) {
    const key = this.boardKey(game, period);
    const start = (page - 1) * pageSize;
    const stop = start + pageSize - 1;
    const [flat, total] = await Promise.all([
      this.redis.zrange(key, start, stop, 'REV', 'WITHSCORES'),
      this.redis.zcard(key),
    ]);
    const entries = await this.hydrate(flat, start + 1);
    return { page, pageSize, total, entries };
  }

  /** Caller's rank and the k players above and below. */
  async around(game: string, period: Period, userId: string, k = 3) {
    const key = this.boardKey(game, period);
    const [[, rank], [, score]] = (await this.redis
      .pipeline()
      .zrevrank(key, userId)
      .zscore(key, userId)
      .exec()) as [[Error | null, number | null], [Error | null, string | null]];

    if (rank === null || score === null) return { rank: null, score: null, neighbors: [] };

    const from = Math.max(0, rank - k);
    const flat = await this.redis.zrange(key, from, rank + k, 'REV', 'WITHSCORES');
    return { rank: rank + 1, score: Number(score), neighbors: await this.hydrate(flat, from + 1) };
  }

  /**
   * Rebuild the rolling 7-day board from the last 7 daily boards.
   * ZUNIONSTORE is O(N) + O(M log M): run from a scheduled job, never per request.
   */
  async rebuildRolling7(game: string, now = new Date()): Promise<number> {
    const keys: string[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) {
      keys.push(RedisKeys.lbDaily(game, utcDay(new Date(now.getTime() - i * 86_400_000))));
    }
    const dest = this.boardKey(game, 'rolling7');
    const pipe = this.redis.pipeline();
    pipe.zunionstore(dest, keys.length, ...keys); // missing keys count as empty sets
    pipe.expire(dest, 120);
    const res = await pipe.exec();
    return Number(res?.[0]?.[1] ?? 0);
  }

  private async hydrate(flat: string[], firstRank: number): Promise<Entry[]> {
    const ids: string[] = [];
    const scores: number[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < flat.length; i += 2) {
      ids.push(flat[i]);
      scores.push(Number(flat[i + 1]));
    }
    const names = ids.length ? await this.redis.mget(ids.map((id) => RedisKeys.user(id))) : [];
    return ids.map((userId, i) => ({ rank: firstRank + i, userId, name: names[i], score: scores[i] }));
  }
}
```

Tie-breaking. In a sorted set, equal scores are ordered lexicographically by member, which is arbitrary from a game point of view. To rank "whoever reached the score first" higher, encode the time into the score. A double holds 53 bits of integer precision. Reserve 23 bits for a tie-breaker (about 97 days of seconds, enough for a season) and up to 30 bits for points:

```ts
// src/leaderboard/tiebreak.ts
export const SHIFT = 2 ** 23; // 8,388,608 seconds ~ 97 days per season

/** Higher is better. Earlier achievement => larger tie component => ranks higher. */
export const encode = (points: number, secondsSinceSeasonStart: number): number =>
  points * SHIFT + (SHIFT - 1 - Math.min(secondsSinceSeasonStart, SHIFT - 1));

export const decodePoints = (composite: number): number => Math.floor(composite / SHIFT);
```

Because the tie component must be recomputed on each update (a plain `ZINCRBY` would add the delta to the composite and corrupt it), the update becomes a read-decode-encode-write that must be atomic:

```lua
-- KEYS[1]=board  ARGV: member, delta, secondsSinceSeasonStart, SHIFT
local shift = tonumber(ARGV[4])
local cur = redis.call('ZSCORE', KEYS[1], ARGV[1])
local points = 0
if cur then points = math.floor(tonumber(cur) / shift) end
points = points + tonumber(ARGV[2])
local tie = shift - 1 - math.min(tonumber(ARGV[3]), shift - 1)
redis.call('ZADD', KEYS[1], points * shift + tie, ARGV[1])
return points
```

Keep `points * SHIFT` under 2^53 (so points below 2^30, about one billion) or the low bits are lost. Readers use `decodePoints` to display real scores. For a plain ZSET without this trick, say explicitly in interviews that ties are broken by member name.

Rank display options for ties: ZSET rank is always unique (1,2,3,4). "Competition ranking" (1,2,2,4) is `ZCOUNT key (score +inf` plus one, which counts only strictly higher scores and costs O(log N).

```ts
// src/leaderboard/leaderboard.controller.ts
import {
  Body, Controller, Get, Param, ParseEnumPipe, Post, Query, Req, UseGuards,
} from '@nestjs/common';
import type { Request } from 'express';
import { SessionGuard } from '../session/session.guard';
import { RateLimit } from '../rate-limit/rate-limit.decorator';
import { RateLimitGuard } from '../rate-limit/rate-limit.guard';
import { LeaderboardService, Period } from './leaderboard.service';

type Authed = Request & { session: { userId: string } };
const PERIODS: Period[] = ['all', 'daily', 'weekly', 'rolling7'];

@Controller('leaderboards/:game')
@UseGuards(SessionGuard, RateLimitGuard)
export class LeaderboardController {
  constructor(private readonly lb: LeaderboardService) {}

  @Get(':period')
  @RateLimit({ name: 'lb-top', limit: 60, windowSeconds: 60, by: 'user' })
  top(
    @Param('game') game: string,
    @Param('period', new ParseEnumPipe(PERIODS)) period: Period,
    @Query('page') page = '1',
    @Query('pageSize') pageSize = '20',
  ) {
    return this.lb.top(game, period, Math.max(1, +page || 1), Math.min(100, +pageSize || 20));
  }

  @Get(':period/me')
  around(
    @Req() req: Authed,
    @Param('game') game: string,
    @Param('period', new ParseEnumPipe(PERIODS)) period: Period,
  ) {
    return this.lb.around(game, period, req.session.userId, 3);
  }
}

// Internal write API: called by trusted services/workers only (service token, not the browser).
@Controller('internal/leaderboards/:game')
export class LeaderboardInternalController {
  constructor(private readonly lb: LeaderboardService) {}

  @Post('score')
  async score(
    @Param('game') game: string,
    @Body() dto: { eventId: string; userId: string; points: number },
  ) {
    const total = await this.lb.record({ game, ...dto });
    return { applied: total !== null, total };
  }
}
```

The internal controller must sit behind a service-to-service guard (mTLS or a shared secret on a private network); it is intentionally not covered by `SessionGuard`. Browsers must never call a score-writing endpoint.

### Failure handling

- Redis is a derived view. The source of truth is the score-event table in PostgreSQL (or MongoDB). Write the event to the database first, then call `record` (directly or via BullMQ with retries). Because `record` is idempotent by `eventId`, retries are safe even if the first attempt actually succeeded but the response was lost.
- Redis data loss or failover: rebuild a board by streaming events or aggregated sums from the DB in batches with `ZADD` (pipelines of a few thousand). Keep a rebuild job and test it.
- Partial failure between boards: not possible within the script (atomic). On Redis Cluster the three boards plus marker live in different slots, so use a hash tag on the game name (for example `shop:lb:{game}:...`) or perform separate idempotent commands.
- Redis down on reads: serve a stale snapshot from an application cache or return 503 for the leaderboard only; never fail the whole API.
- Daily rollover: new day keys are created lazily by the first `ZINCRBY`; there is no cron dependency for correctness.

### Security considerations

- Scores are an integrity target (cheating). Only trusted backend code writes scores, derived from server-validated events, never from client-submitted totals.
- Validate `points` (finite number, within bounds) before calling Redis; reject `NaN`/`Infinity` (`ZINCRBY` rejects them but fail early).
- Validate `game` against an allow-list so users cannot create unbounded keys.
- Cap `pageSize` and page depth, and rate limit reads.
- Privacy: showing names/ranks of other users may require opt-in; return display names, not emails or internal ids if ids are guessable.

### Performance considerations

- `ZINCRBY`, `ZADD`, `ZREVRANK`, `ZSCORE` are O(log N). `ZRANGE` is O(log N + M) for M returned items, so deep offsets stay cheap (it does not scan from the beginning like SQL `OFFSET` does). Offset pagination is only unstable if the board changes between page requests; for infinite scroll use score-cursor pagination with `ZRANGE ... BYSCORE REV LIMIT` and exclusive bounds.
- A ZSET with tens of millions of members is feasible but large (roughly 60 to 100 bytes per member). Plan memory, or split by season/region.
- `ZUNIONSTORE` over big daily boards is expensive and blocks Redis while running; keep it off the request path, schedule it, and cache the result for a short period.
- Hydrating names with `MGET` is one round trip for a page.
- Hot board writes: all increments hit one key, which on Cluster means one shard. Writes are cheap, so this is rarely a bottleneck; if it is, shard by region and merge on read.

### Testing strategy

- Unit: `isoWeek` and `utcDay` around year boundaries (2026-12-31, 2027-01-01 with 53-week years), `encode/decodePoints` round trips, rejection of precision overflow.
- Integration against real Redis: record events and assert top order; same `eventId` twice counts once; `around` for first, last and missing users; page boundaries; TTL present on daily and weekly boards but absent on all-time (`TTL` returns -1); `rebuildRolling7` sums days correctly.
- Concurrency: 1,000 parallel `record` calls for one user sum exactly.
- Tie test: two users reach the same points at different times with the tie-break script; the earlier user ranks first.
- Rebuild test: flush Redis, rebuild from fixture DB rows, compare against the previous top 100.

### Production deployment notes

- Use persistence (AOF `everysec` plus periodic RDB) on the leaderboard instance, but keep the rebuild-from-database job as the real safety net.
- Do not use an eviction policy that can evict leaderboard keys; use `noeviction` or `volatile-*` (daily and weekly keys carry TTLs, all-time does not).
- Monitor `ZCARD` per board, memory per key (`MEMORY USAGE key`), command latency for `zunionstore` (via `SLOWLOG`), and the duplicate-event rate (a spike means a producer retry storm).
- Season resets: do not `DEL` a huge ZSET inline in production; use `UNLINK` (non-blocking free) after renaming the key (`RENAME` to an archive name) so reads switch instantly.
- Document the board key conventions and TTLs next to the `RedisKeys` file so other teams do not invent parallel formats.
