## 14.8 Shopping cart storage

A cart is a classic Redis workload: short-lived, write-heavy, per-user, and tolerant of small data loss. The interesting parts are the guest-to-user merge, TTL policy, and the rule that **Redis never decides what something costs**.

### Requirements

| Type | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Functional | Add, update quantity, remove item, clear cart, read cart |
| Functional | Guest (anonymous) carts keyed by a cookie id; logged-in carts keyed by user id |
| Functional | On login, merge the guest cart into the user cart atomically |
| Functional | At checkout, persist the cart as an order in PostgreSQL |
| Non-functional | p99 < 10 ms for cart operations; 5k cart writes/s |
| Non-functional | Guest carts expire after 7 days idle; user carts after 30 days idle |
| Safety | Prices must come from the catalog at checkout, never from the cart |

### Architecture

```
 Browser (cookie: guest_id)         Browser (JWT: user id)
        |                                   |
        v                                   v
   +-----------+   NestJS CartController   +-----------+
   | Nginx     |-------------------------->| CartService|
   +-----------+                           +-----+-----+
                                                 |
                  +------------------------------+----------------+
                  |                                               |
                  v                                               v
        +------------------+                            +------------------+
        | Redis            |                            | PostgreSQL       |
        |  cart:{id} HASH  |                            |  products (price)|
        |  (productId->qty)|                            |  orders/items    |
        +------------------+                            +------------------+
                  ^
                  |  merge Lua (guest -> user)
```

### Redis data structures

| Key | Type | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `shop:cart:guest:{guestId}` | HASH | field = productId, value = quantity |
| `shop:cart:user:{userId}` | HASH | same shape |
| `shop:cart:merged:{guestId}` | STRING | marker, short TTL, makes merge idempotent |

Why a hash: `HINCRBY` adds quantity atomically, `HDEL` removes one line, `HGETALL` reads the whole cart in one round trip, and memory is compact for small hashes (listpack encoding). Only `productId -> qty` is stored. Name, image, and price are looked up from the catalog when the cart is displayed. Storing a price snapshot in the cart is the most common cart bug: it goes stale and it can be tampered with.

### Key design

Extend `RedisKeys` from section 1.12:

```ts
// src/redis/redis-keys.ts (additions)
export const CartKeys = {
  guest: (guestId: string) => `shop:cart:guest:${guestId}`,
  user: (userId: string | number) => `shop:cart:user:${userId}`,
  merged: (guestId: string) => `shop:cart:merged:${guestId}`,
} as const;
```

Guest ids must be unguessable (UUIDv4 or 128-bit random) because the cookie is the only credential for that cart.

### TTL strategy

| Cart | TTL | Refresh policy |
|---|---|---|
| Guest | 7 days | Sliding: `EXPIRE` after every write |
| User | 30 days | Sliding: `EXPIRE` after every write |
| Merge marker | 10 minutes | Fixed |

Sliding TTL on write only (not on read) so that bots reading carts do not keep them alive. Put `HINCRBY` and `EXPIRE` in the same Lua script or a `MULTI` so a crash cannot leave a cart without a TTL.

### Data flow

```
ADD ITEM
  client -> POST /cart/items {productId, qty}
         -> validate productId exists + qty in 1..99 (Postgres/cache)
         -> HINCRBY cart:<id> productId qty ; EXPIRE cart:<id> ttl   (atomic)

LOGIN MERGE
  client -> POST /auth/login (carries guest cookie)
         -> Lua: read guest hash, HINCRBY each field into user hash,
                 DEL guest hash, SET marker, EXPIRE user hash
         -> clear guest cookie

CHECKOUT
  client -> POST /checkout
         -> HGETALL cart:user:<id>
         -> SELECT price, stock FROM products WHERE id = ANY($1)   (source of truth)
         -> BEGIN; INSERT order + items with DB prices; COMMIT
         -> DEL cart:user:<id>
```

### Code implementation

```ts
// src/cart/cart.service.ts
import { BadRequestException, Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { DataSource } from 'typeorm';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { CartKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

const GUEST_TTL = 7 * 24 * 3600;
const USER_TTL = 30 * 24 * 3600;
const MAX_LINES = 100;
const MAX_QTY = 99;

// KEYS[1]=cart  ARGV[1]=productId ARGV[2]=delta ARGV[3]=ttl ARGV[4]=maxLines ARGV[5]=maxQty
// Returns the new quantity, or -1 (too many lines) / -2 (qty over limit)
const ADD_ITEM_LUA = `
local exists = redis.call('HEXISTS', KEYS[1], ARGV[1])
if exists == 0 and redis.call('HLEN', KEYS[1]) >= tonumber(ARGV[4]) then
  return -1
end
local q = redis.call('HINCRBY', KEYS[1], ARGV[1], tonumber(ARGV[2]))
if q > tonumber(ARGV[5]) then
  redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], ARGV[1], ARGV[5])
  q = -2
elseif q <= 0 then
  redis.call('HDEL', KEYS[1], ARGV[1])
  q = 0
end
redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], ARGV[3])
return q
`;

// KEYS[1]=guest cart KEYS[2]=user cart KEYS[3]=merge marker
// ARGV[1]=user ttl ARGV[2]=marker ttl ARGV[3]=maxQty
const MERGE_LUA = `
if redis.call('EXISTS', KEYS[3]) == 1 then return 0 end
local items = redis.call('HGETALL', KEYS[1])
if #items == 0 then return 0 end
local cap = tonumber(ARGV[3])
for i = 1, #items, 2 do
  local q = redis.call('HINCRBY', KEYS[2], items[i], tonumber(items[i + 1]))
  if q > cap then redis.call('HSET', KEYS[2], items[i], cap) end
end
redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1])
redis.call('SET', KEYS[3], '1', 'EX', tonumber(ARGV[2]))
redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[2], tonumber(ARGV[1]))
return #items / 2
`;

export interface CartOwner { kind: 'guest' | 'user'; id: string }

@Injectable()
export class CartService {
  constructor(
    @Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis,
    private readonly db: DataSource,
  ) {
    this.redis.defineCommand('cartAdd', { numberOfKeys: 1, lua: ADD_ITEM_LUA });
    this.redis.defineCommand('cartMerge', { numberOfKeys: 3, lua: MERGE_LUA });
  }

  private key(o: CartOwner): string {
    return o.kind === 'guest' ? CartKeys.guest(o.id) : CartKeys.user(o.id);
  }

  async addItem(o: CartOwner, productId: string, delta: number): Promise<number> {
    const ttl = o.kind === 'guest' ? GUEST_TTL : USER_TTL;
    const res = await (this.redis as any).cartAdd(
      this.key(o), productId, delta, ttl, MAX_LINES, MAX_QTY,
    ) as number;
    if (res === -1) throw new BadRequestException('Cart is full');
    if (res === -2) throw new BadRequestException(`Max quantity is ${MAX_QTY}`);
    return res;
  }

  async removeItem(o: CartOwner, productId: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.redis.hdel(this.key(o), productId);
  }

  async raw(o: CartOwner): Promise<Record<string, number>> {
    const h = await this.redis.hgetall(this.key(o));
    return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(h).map(([k, v]) => [k, Number(v)]));
  }

  /** Call from the login handler. Safe to call twice (marker makes it idempotent). */
  async mergeGuestIntoUser(guestId: string, userId: string): Promise<number> {
    return (this.redis as any).cartMerge(
      CartKeys.guest(guestId), CartKeys.user(userId), CartKeys.merged(guestId),
      USER_TTL, 600, MAX_QTY,
    ) as Promise<number>;
  }

  /** Display view: quantities from Redis, prices from the catalog. */
  async view(o: CartOwner) {
    const cart = await this.raw(o);
    const ids = Object.keys(cart);
    if (!ids.length) return { lines: [], total: 0 };
    const rows: { id: string; name: string; price_cents: number }[] =
      await this.db.query('SELECT id, name, price_cents FROM products WHERE id = ANY($1)', [ids]);
    const lines = rows.map((r) => ({
      productId: r.id, name: r.name, qty: cart[r.id],
      unitCents: r.price_cents, lineCents: r.price_cents * cart[r.id],
    }));
    return { lines, total: lines.reduce((s, l) => s + l.lineCents, 0) };
  }

  /** Checkout: re-read prices and stock inside the DB transaction. */
  async checkout(userId: string): Promise<{ orderId: string }> {
    const o: CartOwner = { kind: 'user', id: userId };
    const cart = await this.raw(o);
    const ids = Object.keys(cart);
    if (!ids.length) throw new BadRequestException('Cart is empty');

    const orderId = await this.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
      const rows: { id: string; price_cents: number; stock: number }[] = await tx.query(
        'SELECT id, price_cents, stock FROM products WHERE id = ANY($1) FOR UPDATE', [ids],
      );
      if (rows.length !== ids.length) throw new BadRequestException('Unknown product in cart');
      for (const r of rows) {
        if (r.stock < cart[r.id]) throw new BadRequestException(`Out of stock: ${r.id}`);
      }
      const total = rows.reduce((s, r) => s + r.price_cents * cart[r.id], 0);
      const [{ id }] = await tx.query(
        'INSERT INTO orders(user_id, total_cents) VALUES ($1, $2) RETURNING id', [userId, total],
      );
      for (const r of rows) {
        await tx.query(
          'INSERT INTO order_items(order_id, product_id, qty, unit_cents) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4)',
          [id, r.id, cart[r.id], r.price_cents],
        );
        await tx.query('UPDATE products SET stock = stock - $1 WHERE id = $2', [cart[r.id], r.id]);
      }
      return id as string;
    });
    await this.redis.del(CartKeys.user(userId)); // after commit; failure here is harmless
    return { orderId };
  }
}
```

### Failure handling

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Redis down on add/read | Return 503 for cart endpoints; browsing and the rest of the site keep working. Optionally fall back to a client-side cart in localStorage and re-sync later. |
| Redis down at checkout | Checkout depends on the cart, so it fails with 503. Nothing was written to Postgres, so retrying is safe. |
| Crash after DB commit, before `DEL` | The cart remains. The next checkout would create a duplicate order. Mitigation: add a unique `cart_snapshot_hash` or an idempotency key to the order (see 14.11). |
| Merge called twice (retry) | The marker key makes the second call a no-op. |
| Redis restart without persistence | Carts lost. Acceptable for guest carts; for user carts enable AOF `everysec` or accept the loss. |

### Security considerations

- Never trust `price`, `name`, or `discount` from the client. The add-item endpoint accepts only `productId` and `qty`.
- Cap lines (100) and quantity (99) inside Lua so a script cannot bloat memory with one huge hash.
- Guest ids: 128-bit random, `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie. Validate format (`/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/`) before building a key, which also prevents key injection.
- Rate limit cart writes per IP and per guest id (see 14.2 rate limiter).

### Performance considerations

- Everything is O(1) per item, and `HGETALL` is O(n) with n at most 100.
- Small hashes use listpack encoding (`hash-max-listpack-entries`, default 128), which is memory-compact; the 100-line cap keeps carts in that encoding.
- Use `defineCommand` so scripts are sent as `EVALSHA` after first use.
- In Redis Cluster, the merge script touches a guest key and a user key, which hash to different slots and would fail with `CROSSSLOT`. Options: run on a single primary (typical for carts), or do the merge in the application with two steps and rely on the marker for idempotency.

### Testing strategy

| Test | How |
|---|---|
| Add/remove/clamp | Integration test against a real Redis (Testcontainers) |
| Merge semantics | Guest {A:2,B:1}, user {A:1} gives user {A:3,B:1}; guest key gone |
| Merge idempotency | Call twice, quantities unchanged on second call |
| Concurrency | 50 parallel `addItem` for the same product, expect exact sum (or the cap) |
| TTL | After add, `TTL` is within 1 s of the expected value; after `HDEL` of the last line, the key is gone |
| Price tamper | Send a `price` field in the body, assert it is ignored and checkout total matches the DB |

### Production deployment notes

- Cart data is derived and low value: a single primary with replica and AOF `everysec` is enough.
- Memory estimate: about 100 to 200 bytes per line, so an average cart of 5 lines is under 1.5 KB including the key; 1M active carts is around 1.5 GB.
- Set `maxmemory-policy` to `volatile-lru` if the instance also holds non-expiring data; every cart key has a TTL so it is eligible for eviction.
- Optional: an abandoned-cart job scanning with `SCAN MATCH shop:cart:user:*` is possible, but prefer emitting an event on first add, and let a BullMQ delayed job (see 14.10) check the cart 1 hour later.

## 14.9 Distributed lock service

When several app instances (PM2 cluster, multiple containers) might run the same critical section, you need mutual exclusion that lives outside any single process. Redis can provide an **efficiency lock** (avoid duplicate work) reliably. It cannot provide a perfect **correctness lock** on its own, which is why this project includes fencing tokens.

### Requirements

| Type | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Functional | `acquire(resource, ttl)` returns a token or fails; `release(resource, token)` only releases if the caller still owns it |
| Functional | Long jobs can renew (extend) the lock |
| Functional | `withLock(resource, ttl, fn)` helper that always releases |
| Functional | Fencing token (monotonic) for downstream stores that can reject stale writers |
| Non-functional | Lock expiry guarantees liveness if the holder crashes |
| Non-functional | Overhead of one lock < 2 ms |

### Architecture

```
  App instance A            App instance B            App instance C
       |                         |                         |
       |  SET lock:payout <tokA> NX PX 30000               |
       |------------------------>|                         |
       |        OK               |  SET ... NX -> nil      |
       |                         |------------------------>|
       |                         |      (blocked: retry/skip)
       |   run critical section (renew every ttl/3)        |
       |                                                   |
       |  Lua: if GET==tokA then DEL                       |
       v                                                   v
                       +------------------+
                       |      Redis       |
                       | lock:payout      |  token + PX
                       | fence:payout     |  INCR counter
                       +------------------+
```

### Redis data structures

| Key | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `shop:lock:{resource}` | STRING | Value = random owner token, `PX` = lease |
| `shop:fence:{resource}` | STRING (integer) | `INCR` on every successful acquire; never expires (or very long TTL) |

### Key design

```ts
// src/redis/redis-keys.ts (additions)
export const LockKeys = {
  lock: (resource: string) => `shop:lock:${resource}`,
  fence: (resource: string) => `shop:fence:${resource}`,
} as const;
```

Name resources at the right granularity: `payout:2026-11-19` (one run per day) versus `order:{id}` (one per order). Coarse locks are simple but serialize more work.

### TTL strategy

- The lease TTL is a **failure detector**, not a work estimate. Choose about 3 to 10 times the typical critical-section duration, and renew.
- Renew every `ttl / 3` with a Lua script that checks the token first.
- If renewal fails (returns 0), the lock is lost. The job must abort or at least stop making side effects.
- The fence counter has no TTL. It is a tiny integer per resource.

### Data flow

```
acquire:   SET lock token NX PX ttl   -> OK?   then  INCR fence -> fenceToken
renew:     Lua: if GET(lock)==token then PEXPIRE(lock, ttl) return 1 else 0
release:   Lua: if GET(lock)==token then DEL(lock)        return 1 else 0
withLock:  acquire -> start renew timer -> await fn(ctx) -> stop timer -> release (finally)
```

Why a Lua script for release: `GET` then `DEL` as two commands has a race. If the lock expires between them and another client acquires it, your `DEL` would delete their lock. The script makes check-and-delete atomic.

### Code implementation

```ts
// src/lock/lock.service.ts
import { Inject, Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { LockKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

const RELEASE_LUA = `
if redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]) == ARGV[1] then
  return redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1])
end
return 0
`;

const RENEW_LUA = `
if redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]) == ARGV[1] then
  return redis.call('PEXPIRE', KEYS[1], ARGV[2])
end
return 0
`;

export interface LockHandle {
  resource: string;
  token: string;
  fence: number;
}

export class LockLostError extends Error {
  constructor(resource: string) { super(`Lock lost: ${resource}`); }
}
export class LockNotAcquiredError extends Error {
  constructor(resource: string) { super(`Lock busy: ${resource}`); }
}

@Injectable()
export class LockService {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(LockService.name);

  constructor(@Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis) {
    this.redis.defineCommand('lockRelease', { numberOfKeys: 1, lua: RELEASE_LUA });
    this.redis.defineCommand('lockRenew', { numberOfKeys: 1, lua: RENEW_LUA });
  }

  async tryAcquire(resource: string, ttlMs: number): Promise<LockHandle | null> {
    const token = randomUUID();
    const ok = await this.redis.set(LockKeys.lock(resource), token, 'PX', ttlMs, 'NX');
    if (ok !== 'OK') return null;
    // Fencing token. Incremented only by the winner, so it is monotonic per resource.
    const fence = await this.redis.incr(LockKeys.fence(resource));
    return { resource, token, fence };
  }

  /** Retry with jitter until timeoutMs elapses. */
  async acquire(
    resource: string, ttlMs: number, waitMs = 0, retryMs = 100,
  ): Promise<LockHandle> {
    const deadline = Date.now() + waitMs;
    for (;;) {
      const h = await this.tryAcquire(resource, ttlMs);
      if (h) return h;
      if (Date.now() >= deadline) throw new LockNotAcquiredError(resource);
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, retryMs + Math.random() * retryMs));
    }
  }

  async renew(h: LockHandle, ttlMs: number): Promise<boolean> {
    const r = await (this.redis as any).lockRenew(LockKeys.lock(h.resource), h.token, ttlMs);
    return r === 1;
  }

  async release(h: LockHandle): Promise<boolean> {
    const r = await (this.redis as any).lockRelease(LockKeys.lock(h.resource), h.token);
    return r === 1;
  }

  /**
   * Runs fn while holding the lock; renews in the background.
   * fn receives an AbortSignal that fires if the lease is lost.
   */
  async withLock<T>(
    resource: string,
    opts: { ttlMs: number; waitMs?: number },
    fn: (ctx: { fence: number; signal: AbortSignal }) => Promise<T>,
  ): Promise<T> {
    const handle = await this.acquire(resource, opts.ttlMs, opts.waitMs ?? 0);
    const ac = new AbortController();
    const timer = setInterval(async () => {
      try {
        const ok = await this.renew(handle, opts.ttlMs);
        if (!ok) {
          this.logger.error(`Lease lost for ${resource}`);
          ac.abort(new LockLostError(resource));
        }
      } catch (e) {
        // Redis unreachable: we cannot prove we still hold the lock.
        this.logger.error(`Renew failed for ${resource}: ${(e as Error).message}`);
        ac.abort(new LockLostError(resource));
      }
    }, Math.floor(opts.ttlMs / 3));
    timer.unref();

    try {
      return await fn({ fence: handle.fence, signal: ac.signal });
    } finally {
      clearInterval(timer);
      await this.release(handle).catch((e) =>
        this.logger.warn(`Release failed for ${resource}: ${e.message}`),
      );
    }
  }
}
```

Usage in a daily payout job that runs on every instance but must execute once:

```ts
// src/payout/payout.cron.ts
import { Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Cron } from '@nestjs/schedule';
import { DataSource } from 'typeorm';
import { LockNotAcquiredError, LockService } from '../lock/lock.service';

@Injectable()
export class PayoutCron {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(PayoutCron.name);
  constructor(private readonly locks: LockService, private readonly db: DataSource) {}

  @Cron('0 2 * * *')
  async run(): Promise<void> {
    const day = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
    try {
      await this.locks.withLock(`payout:${day}`, { ttlMs: 60_000 }, async ({ fence, signal }) => {
        const batches = await this.db.query(
          `SELECT id FROM payout_batches WHERE day = $1 AND status = 'pending'`, [day],
        );
        for (const b of batches) {
          if (signal.aborted) throw signal.reason; // stop side effects if lease lost
          // Fenced write: reject if a newer lock holder already touched this row.
          const res = await this.db.query(
            `UPDATE payout_batches
                SET status = 'paid', fence = $2
              WHERE id = $1 AND fence < $2`,
            [b.id, fence],
          );
          // pg driver returns [rows, count] for UPDATE via TypeORM; check rows affected
          if (Array.isArray(res) && res[1] === 0) {
            throw new Error(`Stale fence ${fence} for batch ${b.id}`);
          }
        }
      });
    } catch (e) {
      if (e instanceof LockNotAcquiredError) {
        this.logger.debug('Another instance runs the payout');
        return;
      }
      throw e;
    }
  }
}
```

The `fence < $2` predicate is the point of fencing tokens. If instance A pauses (GC, VM freeze) past its TTL, B acquires with a larger fence and writes. When A wakes up and tries to write with its old, smaller fence, the database rejects it. The **database** enforces correctness; Redis only reduces how often conflicts happen.

### Failure handling

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Holder crashes | TTL expires, another instance acquires. Max stall equals the TTL. |
| Holder paused beyond TTL | Lock expires, second holder starts. Fencing token at the DB rejects the stale writer. |
| Redis down during `acquire` | Throws. Cron jobs should skip and alert; they must not run unlocked. |
| Redis down during renew | The job aborts via `AbortSignal` (it cannot prove ownership). |
| Failover loses the lock key | Async replication means a promoted replica may not have the lock. Two holders can overlap briefly. Again: fencing at the DB. Redlock across independent nodes reduces but does not eliminate this; for strict correctness use DB locks or consensus systems. |
| Release fails | Lock expires on its own after TTL. |

### Security considerations

- Token is `randomUUID()` (122 random bits), not a PID or hostname, so it cannot be guessed or collide.
- Resource names built from user input must be sanitized or hashed to avoid creating arbitrary keys.
- Use ACLs so only the worker role can write `shop:lock:*` and `shop:fence:*`.

### Performance considerations

- Acquire is `SET NX` + `INCR` (two round trips); you can fold both into one Lua script if you need to save one RTT. Keep them split here for clarity.
- Spin-wait with jitter instead of tight loops; high contention on one resource should be solved with a queue (BullMQ), not by spinning many instances.
- Avoid very short TTLs (< 1 s) in services with GC or event-loop stalls.

### Testing strategy

| Test | How |
|---|---|
| Mutual exclusion | 20 concurrent `tryAcquire`, exactly one non-null |
| Safe release | A acquires, key expires, B acquires, A calls `release`: B's lock is intact |
| Renewal | Hold 3x TTL with renewal active, no other client can acquire |
| Lost lease | Delete the key manually mid-job, `signal.aborted` becomes true |
| Fence monotonic | Acquire, release, acquire again: second fence is greater |
| Pause simulation | Test using fake timers to stall a holder; assert DB rejects its late write |

### Production deployment notes

- Run the cron on all instances (simplest) with the lock deciding the winner, or run it on one PM2 instance via `NODE_APP_INSTANCE === '0'` as an additional guard (the lock is still needed during rolling restarts).
- Expose metrics: lock acquire success/fail count, hold duration, renewal failures.
- Do not put locks in a Redis that uses `allkeys-*` eviction; an evicted lock key silently breaks mutual exclusion. Use `volatile-*` or `noeviction`.

---

## 14.10 Background email and SMS processing

Sending email or SMS inside an HTTP request couples your latency and availability to a third-party provider. Move it behind a queue. BullMQ stores jobs in Redis and gives you retries, delays, rate limiting, and concurrency control. Remember the split: Redis provides the data structures; **BullMQ** (a library) provides the queue semantics.

### Requirements

| Type | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Functional | API enqueues an email or SMS and returns immediately |
| Functional | Retries with exponential backoff on transient provider errors |
| Functional | Permanent failures (invalid address) go to a dead-letter queue, no retry |
| Functional | Respect provider rate limits (for example 50 emails/s, 10 SMS/s) |
| Functional | Deduplicate: the same logical notification must not be sent twice |
| Functional | Inspect and retry jobs through Bull Board |
| Non-functional | No job loss when workers restart (graceful shutdown) |

### Architecture

```
 +---------+  enqueue   +------------------------+  fetch  +----------------+
 | API     |----------->| Redis (BullMQ)         |-------->| Worker (email) |--> SES/SendGrid
 | (Nest)  |            |  bull:email:wait       |         |  limiter 50/s  |
 +---------+            |  bull:email:active     |         +-------+--------+
      |                 |  bull:email:delayed    |                 | final fail
      |                 |  bull:email:failed     |                 v
      |                 |  bull:sms:*            |         +----------------+
      |                 |  bull:dead-letter:*    |<--------| dead-letter Q  |
      |                 +------------------------+         +----------------+
      |                          ^
      +---> Bull Board (/admin/queues, behind auth)
```

### Redis data structures

BullMQ manages these itself (all under the `bull:<queue>:` prefix): lists/streams for waiting, sorted sets for delayed and prioritized, a hash per job, sets for completed and failed, and a lock key per active job. You do not write to them directly. You only choose queue names, job options, and connection settings.

| Concern | BullMQ feature |
|---|---|
| Retries | `attempts`, `backoff` in job options |
| Delay | `delay` job option |
| Rate limit | `limiter: { max, duration }` on the Worker |
| Concurrency | `concurrency` on the Worker |
| Dedup | Custom `jobId` (a job with an existing id is ignored while that job exists) |
| Cleanup | `removeOnComplete`, `removeOnFail` |

### Key design

- Queues: `email`, `sms`, `dead-letter`. One queue per provider so each has its own limiter and failure isolation.
- Job id for dedup: `email-{type}-{userId}-{businessKey}`, for example `email-order-confirmation-42-order-9001`. Avoid colons in custom ids; BullMQ uses `:` as its own key separator.
- Use a dedicated Redis instance for queues with `maxmemory-policy noeviction`; do not share it with an LRU cache.

### TTL strategy

| Data | Retention |
|---|---|
| Completed jobs | Keep last 1,000 or 24 h (`removeOnComplete: { count: 1000, age: 86400 }`) |
| Failed jobs | Keep 7 days (`removeOnFail: { age: 604800 }`) for debugging |
| Dead-letter jobs | Keep 30 days, then purge (job-level `removeOnComplete` when moved) |
| Dedup window | Tied to job retention: a completed job with the same id still blocks re-add until it is removed. For a time-boxed dedup window, add a separate `SET NX EX` key (see below). |

### Data flow

```
enqueue(email) -> Queue.add(name, data, {jobId, attempts:5, backoff})
worker picks job (respecting limiter) -> provider.send()
   success -> job completed
   transient error -> throw -> BullMQ schedules retry (delay grows)
   permanent error -> throw UnrecoverableError -> no more attempts -> failed
on 'failed' event with no attempts left -> copy payload to dead-letter queue + alert
SIGTERM -> worker.close() waits for active jobs to finish
```

### Code implementation

```ts
// src/notifications/notifications.module.ts
import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { BullModule } from '@nestjs/bullmq';
import { ConfigModule, ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
import { BullBoardModule } from '@bull-board/nestjs';
import { ExpressAdapter } from '@bull-board/express';
import { BullMQAdapter } from '@bull-board/api/bullMQAdapter';
import { NotificationsService } from './notifications.service';
import { EmailProcessor } from './email.processor';
import { SmsProcessor } from './sms.processor';
import { DeadLetterService } from './dead-letter.service';

export const QUEUES = { EMAIL: 'email', SMS: 'sms', DLQ: 'dead-letter' } as const;

@Module({
  imports: [
    ConfigModule,
    BullModule.forRootAsync({
      imports: [ConfigModule],
      inject: [ConfigService],
      useFactory: (c: ConfigService) => ({
        connection: {
          host: c.getOrThrow<string>('QUEUE_REDIS_HOST'),
          port: c.get<number>('QUEUE_REDIS_PORT', 6379),
          password: c.get<string>('QUEUE_REDIS_PASSWORD'),
        },
        defaultJobOptions: {
          removeOnComplete: { count: 1000, age: 86_400 },
          removeOnFail: { age: 604_800 },
        },
      }),
    }),
    BullModule.registerQueue(
      { name: QUEUES.EMAIL }, { name: QUEUES.SMS }, { name: QUEUES.DLQ },
    ),
    BullBoardModule.forRoot({ route: '/admin/queues', adapter: ExpressAdapter }),
    BullBoardModule.forFeature(
      { name: QUEUES.EMAIL, adapter: BullMQAdapter },
      { name: QUEUES.SMS, adapter: BullMQAdapter },
      { name: QUEUES.DLQ, adapter: BullMQAdapter },
    ),
  ],
  providers: [NotificationsService, EmailProcessor, SmsProcessor, DeadLetterService],
  exports: [NotificationsService],
})
export class NotificationsModule {}
```

Protect `/admin/queues` with a Nginx `auth_basic` or IP allow-list, or a Nest middleware that checks an admin role. Bull Board can retry, delete, and inspect job payloads, so treat it as an admin tool.

```ts
// src/notifications/notifications.service.ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { InjectQueue } from '@nestjs/bullmq';
import { JobsOptions, Queue } from 'bullmq';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { QUEUES } from './notifications.module';

export interface EmailJob { to: string; template: string; vars: Record<string, unknown> }
export interface SmsJob { to: string; body: string }

const RETRY: JobsOptions = {
  attempts: 5,
  backoff: { type: 'exponential', delay: 2_000 }, // 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s between attempts
};

@Injectable()
export class NotificationsService {
  constructor(
    @InjectQueue(QUEUES.EMAIL) private readonly emailQ: Queue<EmailJob>,
    @InjectQueue(QUEUES.SMS) private readonly smsQ: Queue<SmsJob>,
    @Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis, // app Redis, for the time-boxed dedup key
  ) {}

  /**
   * dedupKey identifies the logical notification, e.g. `order-confirmation-42-order-9001`.
   * Layer 1: SET NX with TTL = business dedup window (here 1 h).
   * Layer 2: custom jobId, so a duplicate add while the job still exists is ignored.
   */
  async sendEmail(dedupKey: string, data: EmailJob): Promise<'queued' | 'duplicate'> {
    const first = await this.redis.set(`shop:notif:dedup:${dedupKey}`, '1', 'EX', 3600, 'NX');
    if (first !== 'OK') return 'duplicate';
    await this.emailQ.add('send', data, { ...RETRY, jobId: `email-${dedupKey}` });
    return 'queued';
  }

  async sendSms(dedupKey: string, data: SmsJob): Promise<'queued' | 'duplicate'> {
    const first = await this.redis.set(`shop:notif:dedup:${dedupKey}`, '1', 'EX', 3600, 'NX');
    if (first !== 'OK') return 'duplicate';
    await this.smsQ.add('send', data, { ...RETRY, jobId: `sms-${dedupKey}` });
    return 'queued';
  }
}
```

If `emailQ.add` fails after the dedup key was set, the notification would be suppressed for one hour. Handle it by deleting the key in a `catch` block and rethrowing:

```ts
// inside sendEmail, wrapping add():
try {
  await this.emailQ.add('send', data, { ...RETRY, jobId: `email-${dedupKey}` });
} catch (e) {
  await this.redis.del(`shop:notif:dedup:${dedupKey}`).catch(() => undefined);
  throw e;
}
```

```ts
// src/notifications/email.processor.ts
import { Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { OnWorkerEvent, Processor, WorkerHost } from '@nestjs/bullmq';
import { Job, UnrecoverableError } from 'bullmq';
import { DeadLetterService } from './dead-letter.service';
import { EmailJob } from './notifications.service';
import { QUEUES } from './notifications.module';

class ProviderError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string, readonly status: number) { super(message); }
}

// Provider rate limit: at most 50 jobs per 1000 ms across ALL workers of this queue.
@Processor(QUEUES.EMAIL, {
  concurrency: 10,
  limiter: { max: 50, duration: 1_000 },
})
export class EmailProcessor extends WorkerHost {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(EmailProcessor.name);
  constructor(private readonly dlq: DeadLetterService) { super(); }

  async process(job: Job<EmailJob>): Promise<{ messageId: string }> {
    try {
      return await this.callProvider(job.data);
    } catch (e) {
      const err = e as ProviderError;
      // 4xx (except 429) means the request itself is bad. Retrying will not help.
      if (err.status >= 400 && err.status < 500 && err.status !== 429) {
        throw new UnrecoverableError(`Permanent failure: ${err.message}`);
      }
      throw e; // transient: BullMQ applies attempts/backoff
    }
  }

  private async callProvider(data: EmailJob): Promise<{ messageId: string }> {
    // Replace with SES / SendGrid SDK call. Use an idempotency token from job.id if supported.
    return { messageId: `msg-${Date.now()}-${data.to}` };
  }

  @OnWorkerEvent('failed')
  async onFailed(job: Job<EmailJob> | undefined, err: Error): Promise<void> {
    if (!job) return;
    const exhausted = job.attemptsMade >= (job.opts.attempts ?? 1);
    const permanent = err instanceof UnrecoverableError;
    if (exhausted || permanent) {
      this.logger.error(`Job ${job.id} dead: ${err.message}`);
      await this.dlq.park(QUEUES.EMAIL, job, err);
    }
  }
}
```

SMS is the same shape with a smaller limiter (for example `{ max: 10, duration: 1_000 }`) and its own provider client; copy `EmailProcessor` as `SmsProcessor` and change the queue name and limiter.

```ts
// src/notifications/dead-letter.service.ts
import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { InjectQueue } from '@nestjs/bullmq';
import { Job, Queue } from 'bullmq';
import { QUEUES } from './notifications.module';

@Injectable()
export class DeadLetterService {
  constructor(@InjectQueue(QUEUES.DLQ) private readonly dlq: Queue) {}

  /** BullMQ has no built-in DLQ; we copy the exhausted job into a queue nobody processes. */
  async park(source: string, job: Job, err: Error): Promise<void> {
    await this.dlq.add(
      `${source}-dead`,
      { source, originalId: job.id, data: job.data, reason: err.message, at: new Date().toISOString() },
      { removeOnComplete: false, removeOnFail: false },
    );
  }
}
```

Nobody registers a worker for `dead-letter`, so its jobs stay in `wait` where Bull Board shows them. An operator can inspect and re-enqueue them to the original queue after fixing the cause.

Graceful shutdown: with `app.enableShutdownHooks()` (see Module 1, `main.ts`), `@nestjs/bullmq` closes workers on `SIGTERM`, which waits for active jobs to finish. Make sure the orchestrator allows enough time:

```ts
// main.ts excerpt
app.enableShutdownHooks();
```

```
# docker-compose.yml excerpt
services:
  worker:
    stop_grace_period: 60s     # longer than your slowest job
# PM2: ecosystem.config.js -> kill_timeout: 60000
```

If you manage the worker manually: `await worker.close()` (waits for in-flight jobs), `worker.close(true)` forces.

### Failure handling

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Provider outage (5xx, timeout) | Job fails, retried with backoff for 5 attempts, then DLQ + alert. Consider a circuit breaker to pause the queue with `queue.pause()` during a long outage. |
| Provider throttles (429) | Treated as transient. The limiter should normally prevent it; if it still happens, backoff helps. |
| Worker crash mid-job | BullMQ detects the stalled job (lock not renewed) and moves it back to waiting. The job may run twice, so provider calls must tolerate repeats (see below). |
| Redis down | `queue.add` throws, so the API must decide: return 503, or write to an outbox table in Postgres and let a relay enqueue later. For critical emails (receipts) use the **outbox pattern**. |
| Redis restart without persistence | Queued jobs lost. Enable AOF `everysec` for the queue instance. |

BullMQ gives at-least-once delivery. A job that sent the email and then crashed before acknowledging will be retried. If the provider supports an idempotency key, pass `job.id`; otherwise accept rare duplicates for non-critical messages.

### Security considerations

- Do not put secrets or full PII in job data if avoidable; store a reference (`userId`, `templateId`) and load details in the worker. Job payloads are readable in Redis and in Bull Board.
- Put Bull Board behind authentication and TLS. Queue Redis requires `requirepass` or ACL users.
- Validate and rate limit the API that triggers sends (password-reset endpoints are an abuse vector for SMS pumping).
- Strip or encode template variables to prevent header injection in email.

### Performance considerations

- `concurrency` controls parallelism per worker process. Total throughput is bounded by `min(limiter, concurrency x latency)`.
- Limiter is global per queue across workers, because it is stored in Redis.
- Keep job data small (a few KB) and set `removeOnComplete`/`removeOnFail`; unbounded history is the number one cause of queue Redis memory growth.
- BullMQ requires `maxRetriesPerRequest: null` for its blocking worker connections. Passing connection options (as above) lets BullMQ create its own connections with the right settings; do not reuse the `REDIS_CLIENT` instance for Workers.

### Testing strategy

| Test | How |
|---|---|
| Processor unit test | Call `process(fakeJob)` with a mocked provider; assert 4xx throws `UnrecoverableError` |
| Retry behaviour | Integration test with a real Redis and a provider stub that fails twice, then succeeds; assert `attemptsMade` is 3 |
| DLQ | Stub always fails; after attempts exhausted, assert a job exists in `dead-letter` |
| Rate limit | Enqueue 200 jobs with limiter 50/s; assert at least 3 s elapsed |
| Dedup | Call `sendEmail` twice with the same key; assert one job |
| Shutdown | Start a slow job, call `worker.close()`, assert the job completed |

### Production deployment notes

- Separate Redis instance for queues with `maxmemory-policy noeviction` and AOF on; do not share with your cache.
- Run workers as a separate Docker service or PM2 app from the API, so you can scale and restart them independently.
- Monitor queue depth (`queue.getJobCounts()`), oldest waiting job age, failed count, and DLQ size; alert when the DLQ is not empty.
- Expose Bull Board only on an internal network or via Nginx `auth_basic` plus allow-list.

## 14.11 Idempotency management for payment APIs

Networks fail after the server has done the work. A mobile client times out on `POST /payments`, retries, and the customer is charged twice. An **idempotency key** lets the client retry safely: the server executes the operation once and replays the stored result for every repeat. Redis is a good fit for the fast path (claim, in-progress state, cached response). **PostgreSQL remains the source of truth.**

### Requirements

| Type | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Functional | Client sends `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` on `POST /payments` |
| Functional | First request executes; later requests with the same key and same body get the same status code and body |
| Functional | Same key with a different body returns `422` (key reuse with different payload) |
| Functional | A duplicate that arrives while the first is still running returns `409` with `Retry-After` |
| Functional | Keys are remembered for 24 hours |
| Safety | Even if Redis loses every key, a payment must never be created twice |
| Non-functional | Overhead < 3 ms on the happy path |

### Architecture

```
 Client --POST /payments (Idempotency-Key: K, body B)--> Nginx --> NestJS
                                                                    |
                                    1. fingerprint = sha256(method+path+canonical(B))
                                                                    |
                          +-----------------------------------------v------+
                          | Redis: Lua "begin"                             |
                          |   key idem:{merchant}:{K}                      |
                          |   absent  -> SET in_progress(owner,fp) EX 60   |
                          |   present -> return stored record              |
                          +---------+--------------------+-----------------+
                                    |                    |
                         new (we own it)         existing record
                                    |                    |
                                    v          fp differs? -> 422
                         +---------------------+  in_progress? -> 409
                         | Handler:            |  completed?   -> replay response
                         | INSERT payment      |
                         |  UNIQUE(merchant,K) |<-- source of truth (PostgreSQL)
                         | call PSP            |
                         +----------+----------+
                                    |
                                    v
                         Lua "complete": SET completed(response) EX 86400
                         (only if owner token still matches)
```

### Redis data structures

| Key | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `shop:idem:{merchantId}:{key}` | STRING (JSON) | `{ owner, fp, status: 'in_progress' or 'completed', code?, body?, createdAt }` |

One key per request. A single string keeps the claim and the stored response in one atomic unit.

### Key design

```ts
// src/redis/redis-keys.ts (additions)
export const IdemKeys = {
  record: (merchantId: string, key: string) => `shop:idem:${merchantId}:${key}`,
} as const;
```

- Scope by merchant or tenant (or authenticated user) so one customer's key can never collide with or read another's response.
- Validate the key: 16 to 64 characters, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` only. Reject anything else with `400`.
- The **fingerprint** hashes method, route, and the canonicalized body (stable key order). Do not include volatile headers such as `Date`.

### TTL strategy

| State | TTL | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `in_progress` | 60 s (above the p99 handler time) | If the process crashes, the claim expires and a retry can proceed instead of being blocked for 24 h |
| `completed` | 24 h | Standard retry window; matches what clients expect from payment APIs |

Because the `in_progress` TTL can expire while a slow handler is still running, a second request might begin. That is exactly why the database unique constraint exists: the second attempt's `INSERT` hits the constraint and the code returns the already-created payment.

### Data flow

```
 request 1                         request 2 (retry, 200 ms later)
 ---------                         --------------------------------
 begin  -> NEW                     begin -> EXISTING in_progress
 INSERT payment (unique)           -> 409 Conflict, Retry-After: 1
 call PSP
 complete(200, body)               request 3 (retry, 10 s later)
                                   begin -> EXISTING completed, same fp
                                   -> replay 200 + stored body
                                      + header Idempotent-Replayed: true

 request 4 (same key, different amount)
 begin -> EXISTING, fp mismatch -> 422
```

### Code implementation

```ts
// src/idempotency/idempotency.service.ts
import { Inject, Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { createHash, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { IdemKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

const IN_PROGRESS_TTL = 60;
const COMPLETED_TTL = 24 * 3600;

interface IdemRecord {
  owner: string;
  fp: string;
  status: 'in_progress' | 'completed';
  code?: number;
  body?: unknown;
  createdAt: number;
}

// KEYS[1]=record  ARGV[1]=new record JSON  ARGV[2]=in-progress ttl
// Returns { 1 } if we created it, or { 0, existingJson }
const BEGIN_LUA = `
local cur = redis.call('GET', KEYS[1])
if cur then return { 0, cur } end
redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], ARGV[1], 'EX', tonumber(ARGV[2]))
return { 1 }
`;

// KEYS[1]=record ARGV[1]=owner ARGV[2]=completed JSON ARGV[3]=ttl
// Only the owner may complete. Returns 1 on success, 0 if the claim was lost.
const COMPLETE_LUA = `
local cur = redis.call('GET', KEYS[1])
if not cur then return 0 end
local rec = cjson.decode(cur)
if rec.owner ~= ARGV[1] then return 0 end
redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], ARGV[2], 'EX', tonumber(ARGV[3]))
return 1
`;

// Owner-only delete, used when the handler failed with a retryable error.
const ABORT_LUA = `
local cur = redis.call('GET', KEYS[1])
if not cur then return 0 end
local rec = cjson.decode(cur)
if rec.owner == ARGV[1] then return redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1]) end
return 0
`;

export type BeginResult =
  | { kind: 'new'; owner: string }
  | { kind: 'in_progress' }
  | { kind: 'mismatch' }
  | { kind: 'replay'; code: number; body: unknown };

export function fingerprint(method: string, path: string, body: unknown): string {
  return createHash('sha256').update(`${method}\n${path}\n${canonical(body)}`).digest('hex');
}

function canonical(v: unknown): string {
  if (v === null || typeof v !== 'object') return JSON.stringify(v) ?? 'null';
  if (Array.isArray(v)) return `[${v.map(canonical).join(',')}]`;
  const o = v as Record<string, unknown>;
  return `{${Object.keys(o).sort().map((k) => `${JSON.stringify(k)}:${canonical(o[k])}`).join(',')}}`;
}

@Injectable()
export class IdempotencyService {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(IdempotencyService.name);

  constructor(@Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis) {
    this.redis.defineCommand('idemBegin', { numberOfKeys: 1, lua: BEGIN_LUA });
    this.redis.defineCommand('idemComplete', { numberOfKeys: 1, lua: COMPLETE_LUA });
    this.redis.defineCommand('idemAbort', { numberOfKeys: 1, lua: ABORT_LUA });
  }

  async begin(merchantId: string, key: string, fp: string): Promise<BeginResult> {
    const owner = randomUUID();
    const rec: IdemRecord = { owner, fp, status: 'in_progress', createdAt: Date.now() };
    const [created, existing] = (await (this.redis as any).idemBegin(
      IdemKeys.record(merchantId, key), JSON.stringify(rec), IN_PROGRESS_TTL,
    )) as [number, string?];

    if (created === 1) return { kind: 'new', owner };
    const cur = JSON.parse(existing as string) as IdemRecord;
    if (cur.fp !== fp) return { kind: 'mismatch' };
    if (cur.status === 'in_progress') return { kind: 'in_progress' };
    return { kind: 'replay', code: cur.code as number, body: cur.body };
  }

  async complete(
    merchantId: string, key: string, owner: string, fp: string, code: number, body: unknown,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const rec: IdemRecord = {
      owner, fp, status: 'completed', code, body, createdAt: Date.now(),
    };
    const ok = await (this.redis as any).idemComplete(
      IdemKeys.record(merchantId, key), owner, JSON.stringify(rec), COMPLETED_TTL,
    );
    if (ok !== 1) this.logger.warn(`Lost idempotency claim for ${merchantId}:${key}`);
  }

  async abort(merchantId: string, key: string, owner: string): Promise<void> {
    await (this.redis as any).idemAbort(IdemKeys.record(merchantId, key), owner);
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/payments/payments.controller.ts
import {
  BadRequestException, Body, ConflictException, Controller, Headers, HttpCode,
  HttpException, Post, Req, Res, ServiceUnavailableException,
} from '@nestjs/common';
import type { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { IdempotencyService, fingerprint } from '../idempotency/idempotency.service';
import { PaymentsService } from './payments.service';

class CreatePaymentDto { amountCents!: number; currency!: string; customerId!: string }

const KEY_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$/;

@Controller('payments')
export class PaymentsController {
  constructor(
    private readonly idem: IdempotencyService,
    private readonly payments: PaymentsService,
  ) {}

  @Post()
  @HttpCode(201)
  async create(
    @Headers('idempotency-key') key: string | undefined,
    @Body() dto: CreatePaymentDto,
    @Req() req: Request,
    @Res({ passthrough: true }) res: Response,
  ) {
    if (!key || !KEY_RE.test(key)) {
      throw new BadRequestException('Idempotency-Key header required (16-64 chars, [A-Za-z0-9_-])');
    }
    const merchantId = (req as any).user.merchantId as string; // from your auth guard
    const fp = fingerprint(req.method, req.path, dto);

    let state;
    try {
      state = await this.idem.begin(merchantId, key, fp);
    } catch {
      // Fail closed: without the fast-path guard we do not risk a double charge.
      throw new ServiceUnavailableException('Idempotency store unavailable, retry shortly');
    }

    switch (state.kind) {
      case 'mismatch':
        throw new HttpException('Idempotency-Key reused with a different request', 422);
      case 'in_progress':
        res.setHeader('Retry-After', '1');
        throw new ConflictException('A request with this Idempotency-Key is in progress');
      case 'replay':
        res.status(state.code).setHeader('Idempotent-Replayed', 'true');
        return state.body;
      case 'new':
        break;
    }

    try {
      // DB unique constraint (merchant_id, idempotency_key) is the real guarantee.
      const payment = await this.payments.createOnce(merchantId, key, fp, dto);
      await this.idem.complete(merchantId, key, state.owner, fp, 201, payment);
      return payment;
    } catch (e) {
      if (e instanceof HttpException && e.getStatus() >= 400 && e.getStatus() < 500) {
        // Deterministic client error: cache it so retries see the same answer.
        await this.idem.complete(
          merchantId, key, state.owner, fp, e.getStatus(), e.getResponse(),
        ).catch(() => undefined);
      } else {
        // 5xx or unknown: release the claim so the client can retry for real.
        await this.idem.abort(merchantId, key, state.owner).catch(() => undefined);
      }
      throw e;
    }
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/payments/payments.service.ts
import { Injectable, UnprocessableEntityException } from '@nestjs/common';
import { DataSource } from 'typeorm';

/*
 CREATE TABLE payments (
   id              uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
   merchant_id     text NOT NULL,
   idempotency_key text NOT NULL,
   request_fp      text NOT NULL,
   amount_cents    bigint NOT NULL,
   currency        char(3) NOT NULL,
   status          text NOT NULL,
   psp_ref         text,
   created_at      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
   UNIQUE (merchant_id, idempotency_key)
 );
*/
@Injectable()
export class PaymentsService {
  constructor(private readonly db: DataSource) {}

  async createOnce(
    merchantId: string, key: string, fp: string,
    dto: { amountCents: number; currency: string; customerId: string },
  ) {
    // 1) Claim the row first. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING returns no row if it already exists.
    const inserted = await this.db.query(
      `INSERT INTO payments (merchant_id, idempotency_key, request_fp, amount_cents, currency, status)
       VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,'pending')
       ON CONFLICT (merchant_id, idempotency_key) DO NOTHING
       RETURNING id, status, amount_cents, currency`,
      [merchantId, key, fp, dto.amountCents, dto.currency],
    );

    if (inserted.length === 0) {
      // Someone else already created it (Redis claim expired, or Redis was empty).
      const [row] = await this.db.query(
        `SELECT id, status, amount_cents, currency, request_fp
           FROM payments WHERE merchant_id = $1 AND idempotency_key = $2`,
        [merchantId, key],
      );
      if (row.request_fp !== fp) {
        throw new UnprocessableEntityException('Idempotency-Key reused with a different request');
      }
      return row; // same logical request: return the existing payment
    }

    // 2) Call the PSP with the same key so the PSP also dedups (most PSPs support this).
    const pspRef = await this.callPsp(key, dto);
    const [done] = await this.db.query(
      `UPDATE payments SET status = 'succeeded', psp_ref = $2 WHERE id = $1
       RETURNING id, status, amount_cents, currency`,
      [inserted[0].id, pspRef],
    );
    return done;
  }

  private async callPsp(idempotencyKey: string, dto: unknown): Promise<string> {
    return `psp_${idempotencyKey}`; // replace with real PSP SDK call passing idempotencyKey
  }
}
```

### Failure handling

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Redis down | `begin` throws, API returns 503 (fail closed). A looser option is to skip Redis and rely solely on the DB constraint plus PSP-side idempotency; choose per risk appetite. |
| Redis loses data (restart, eviction) | The DB unique constraint returns the existing payment for the same key. No double charge. |
| Crash after INSERT, before PSP call | Row stays `pending`. A retry finds the row, and a reconciliation job (or the retry path) resumes the PSP call using the same key. |
| Crash after PSP success, before DB update | PSP idempotency key makes the retry return the same charge; the retry then updates the row. Without PSP idempotency you need reconciliation against the PSP. |
| `complete` fails | Next retry sees `in_progress` until TTL (60 s) then goes through the DB path and returns the existing payment. |
| Handler 5xx | Claim is aborted, client retries and re-executes (safe because of the DB constraint). |

### Security considerations

- Scope keys per authenticated merchant or user to prevent cross-account replay or response leakage.
- The stored response may contain sensitive data. Store only what the client would see anyway (no card data, no secrets) and set a TTL; encrypt at rest on disk if required by policy.
- Strict key format validation prevents key injection and oversized keys.
- Enforce a body size limit before fingerprinting.

### Performance considerations

- The Lua `begin` is a single round trip and O(1).
- Canonicalizing and hashing a payment body costs microseconds; do not fingerprint multi-megabyte uploads (use idempotency on small JSON APIs).
- Memory: about 1 KB per record times requests per day, so 1M payments/day is around 1 GB retained for 24 h. Size accordingly or trim the stored body to essential fields.

### Testing strategy

| Test | How |
|---|---|
| Replay | Same key and body twice: identical status and body, second has `Idempotent-Replayed` |
| Mismatch | Same key, different amount: 422 |
| Concurrency | `Promise.all` of 20 identical requests: exactly one `INSERT`, one PSP call; others get 409 or replay |
| Redis flush | Run request, `FLUSHALL`, repeat: no second row, same payment returned |
| Failure cases | Handler throws 500: claim removed, retry executes |
| Claim ownership | Expire claim mid-flight, second request takes over, first request's `complete` does nothing |
| Key validation | Missing, too short, or invalid characters give 400 |

### Production deployment notes

- Prefer a Redis with persistence (AOF `everysec`) so the fast path survives restarts; correctness does not depend on it, but the UX does.
- Add a nightly job deleting old `payments` rows' key association only if your retention policy requires it; the unique constraint should live as long as clients might retry (at least the 24 h window, commonly forever for payments).
- Emit metrics: replay rate, 409 rate, 422 rate. A spike in 422 indicates a client bug generating keys badly.
- Document the contract for API consumers: header name, TTL, behaviours for 409/422, and that keys must be unique per logical operation (UUIDv4).

---

## 14.12 Real-time analytics counters

Dashboards need numbers such as page views per minute, unique visitors per hour, and daily active users. Writing every event to PostgreSQL does not scale well and does not need to. Redis absorbs the writes (INCR-style operations are cheap and atomic), and a periodic job flushes aggregates to the database for long-term storage and reporting.

### Requirements

| Type | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Functional | Count page views per page per minute |
| Functional | Approximate unique visitors per page per hour (1 to 2 percent error is acceptable) |
| Functional | Exact daily active users (DAU) for numeric user ids, plus weekly active via union |
| Functional | Flush minute aggregates to PostgreSQL every minute; no double counting |
| Functional | Live read of the last N minutes straight from Redis |
| Non-functional | 20k events/s sustained, writes batched to minimize round trips |

### Architecture

```
 Nest API instances (many)
   |  track(event)  -> in-memory buffer (100 ms or 500 events)
   |  flush buffer  -> ONE pipeline: HINCRBY, PFADD, SETBIT, EXPIRE
   v
 +------------------------------------------------------------+
 | Redis                                                      |
 |  an:views:{minute}      HASH   page -> count               |
 |  an:uv:{hour}:{page}    HLL    visitor ids                 |
 |  an:dau:{day}           BITMAP bit[userId] = 1             |
 |  an:flushing            SET    names of in-flight batches  |
 +------------------------+-----------------------------------+
                          ^
   every minute (under a distributed lock, see 14.9)
                          |
 +------------------------+------+   RENAMENX -> HGETALL ->
 | Flusher (@Cron)               |   PG upsert (+ batch log) -> DEL
 +---------------+---------------+
                 v
     PostgreSQL: page_views_minute, flush_log
```

### Redis data structures

| Key | Type | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `shop:an:views:{yyyyMMddHHmm}` | HASH (page -> count) | `HINCRBY` is atomic; one key per minute keeps each hash small and makes the flush a bounded operation |
| `shop:an:uv:{yyyyMMddHH}:{page}` | HyperLogLog | About 12 KB maximum per key for millions of uniques, ~0.81% standard error. `PFADD`, `PFCOUNT`, and `PFMERGE` to roll up hours into days |
| `shop:an:dau:{yyyyMMdd}` | Bitmap (STRING) | One bit per numeric user id. `BITCOUNT` gives exact DAU. 10M users is about 1.2 MB per day |
| `shop:an:flushing` | SET | Tracks batch keys that were renamed and are not yet confirmed in Postgres |

Bitmaps need dense, small integer ids. With UUID user ids, use an HLL instead (approximate) or maintain a separate id-to-integer mapping.

### Key design

```ts
// src/redis/redis-keys.ts (additions)
export const AnKeys = {
  views: (minute: string) => `shop:an:views:${minute}`,            // yyyyMMddHHmm
  viewsFlush: (minute: string, ts: number) => `shop:an:views:${minute}:flushing:${ts}`,
  uv: (hour: string, page: string) => `shop:an:uv:${hour}:${page}`,   // yyyyMMddHH
  dau: (day: string) => `shop:an:dau:${day}`,                       // yyyyMMdd
  flushing: 'shop:an:flushing',
} as const;
```

Bucketing by time in the key is the central idea. Old buckets stop receiving writes, so they can be flushed, expired, and queried independently. Normalize `page` (strip query strings, cap length, allow-list) to bound the field cardinality; otherwise attackers can create unlimited fields.

### TTL strategy

| Key | TTL | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `views:{minute}` | 2 hours after the last write (set on every write) | Safety net; the flusher deletes it earlier, and live reads cover recent minutes |
| `uv:{hour}:{page}` | 48 hours | Allows rollups and late reads |
| `dau:{day}` | 40 days | Weekly and monthly unions without the DB |
| `flushing` set | None (entries removed after commit) | Must survive until reconciled; alert if it grows |

### Data flow

```
write path:   event -> buffer -> pipeline[HINCRBY views, PFADD uv, SETBIT dau, EXPIRE...]
flush path:   for each closed minute m:
                1. SADD flushing <flushKey>      (record intent)
                2. RENAMENX views:m -> flushKey  (atomic snapshot; new writes start a fresh key)
                3. HGETALL flushKey
                4. BEGIN; INSERT flush_log(batch_key) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
                   if inserted: UPSERT views += delta;  COMMIT
                5. DEL flushKey ; SREM flushing flushKey
recovery:     on start of each flush, process leftovers listed in flushing first
read path:    last N minutes: pipeline of HGETALL on N keys + any flushing keys; older: Postgres
```

`RENAMENX` (not `RENAME`) matters: `RENAME` silently overwrites an existing destination and would destroy a batch that has not been committed. The flush log row, inserted in the same transaction as the upsert, makes the additive upsert idempotent: if the DB commit succeeded but the `DEL` failed, the retry finds the batch id in `flush_log` and skips the upsert.

For simple string counters, `GETDEL` [6.2+] reads and removes atomically in one command, which is the same idea without the staging key. Hashes do not have an equivalent single command in older versions, so renaming the key is the portable approach.

### Code implementation

```ts
// src/analytics/analytics.service.ts
import { Inject, Injectable, Logger, OnApplicationShutdown } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { AnKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';

export interface PageViewEvent {
  page: string;          // normalized path, e.g. /products/42
  visitorId: string;     // cookie id or user id
  userId?: number;       // numeric id when logged in (for DAU bitmap)
  at?: Date;
}

const pad = (n: number) => String(n).padStart(2, '0');
export const minuteOf = (d: Date) =>
  `${d.getUTCFullYear()}${pad(d.getUTCMonth() + 1)}${pad(d.getUTCDate())}${pad(d.getUTCHours())}${pad(d.getUTCMinutes())}`;
export const hourOf = (d: Date) => minuteOf(d).slice(0, 10);
export const dayOf = (d: Date) => minuteOf(d).slice(0, 8);

@Injectable()
export class AnalyticsService implements OnApplicationShutdown {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(AnalyticsService.name);
  private buffer: PageViewEvent[] = [];
  private timer: NodeJS.Timeout;

  constructor(@Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis) {
    this.timer = setInterval(() => void this.drain(), 100);
    this.timer.unref();
  }

  /** Non-blocking: never slows the request. May drop events if Redis is down and buffer is full. */
  track(e: PageViewEvent): void {
    if (this.buffer.length >= 50_000) return; // backpressure: drop rather than OOM
    this.buffer.push(e);
    if (this.buffer.length >= 500) void this.drain();
  }

  private async drain(): Promise<void> {
    if (this.buffer.length === 0) return;
    const batch = this.buffer;
    this.buffer = [];
    const p = this.redis.pipeline();
    for (const e of batch) {
      const at = e.at ?? new Date();
      const vKey = AnKeys.views(minuteOf(at));
      p.hincrby(vKey, e.page, 1);
      p.expire(vKey, 7_200);
      const uKey = AnKeys.uv(hourOf(at), e.page);
      p.pfadd(uKey, e.visitorId);
      p.expire(uKey, 172_800);
      if (e.userId !== undefined && e.userId >= 0) {
        const dKey = AnKeys.dau(dayOf(at));
        p.setbit(dKey, e.userId, 1);
        p.expire(dKey, 40 * 86_400);
      }
    }
    try {
      const res = await p.exec(); // pipeline: errors are per command, not thrown
      const failed = res?.filter(([err]) => err).length ?? 0;
      if (failed) this.logger.warn(`${failed} analytics commands failed`);
    } catch (err) {
      this.logger.error(`Analytics drain failed: ${(err as Error).message}`);
      // events in this batch are lost: acceptable for analytics, count it in a metric
    }
  }

  async uniqueVisitors(hour: string, page: string): Promise<number> {
    return this.redis.pfcount(AnKeys.uv(hour, page));
  }

  async dailyActive(day: string): Promise<number> {
    return this.redis.bitcount(AnKeys.dau(day));
  }

  /** Weekly active = OR of 7 daily bitmaps into a temp key, then BITCOUNT. */
  async weeklyActive(days: string[]): Promise<number> {
    const tmp = `shop:an:tmp:wau:${days[0]}`;
    await this.redis.bitop('OR', tmp, ...days.map(AnKeys.dau));
    await this.redis.expire(tmp, 300);
    return this.redis.bitcount(tmp);
  }

  /** Live counts for the last N minutes (unflushed data only exists here). */
  async liveViews(minutes: string[]): Promise<Record<string, Record<string, string>>> {
    const p = this.redis.pipeline();
    minutes.forEach((m) => p.hgetall(AnKeys.views(m)));
    const res = await p.exec();
    return Object.fromEntries(minutes.map((m, i) => [m, (res?.[i]?.[1] as Record<string, string>) ?? {}]));
  }

  async onApplicationShutdown(): Promise<void> {
    clearInterval(this.timer);
    await this.drain(); // best effort final flush of the in-memory buffer
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/analytics/analytics-flusher.ts
import { Inject, Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Cron } from '@nestjs/schedule';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { DataSource } from 'typeorm';
import { REDIS_CLIENT } from '../redis/redis.constants';
import { AnKeys } from '../redis/redis-keys';
import { LockNotAcquiredError, LockService } from '../lock/lock.service';
import { minuteOf } from './analytics.service';

/*
 CREATE TABLE page_views_minute (
   bucket timestamptz NOT NULL, page text NOT NULL, views bigint NOT NULL,
   PRIMARY KEY (bucket, page));
 CREATE TABLE flush_log (batch_key text PRIMARY KEY, flushed_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now());
*/
@Injectable()
export class AnalyticsFlusher {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(AnalyticsFlusher.name);

  constructor(
    @Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis,
    private readonly db: DataSource,
    private readonly locks: LockService,
  ) {}

  @Cron('5 * * * * *') // 5 seconds past every minute
  async run(): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await this.locks.withLock('analytics-flush', { ttlMs: 50_000 }, async ({ signal }) => {
        // 1) finish anything left over from a crashed run
        for (const flushKey of await this.redis.smembers(AnKeys.flushing)) {
          if (signal.aborted) return;
          await this.commit(flushKey);
        }
        // 2) snapshot closed minutes (previous 10 minutes, to catch late runs)
        const now = Date.now();
        for (let i = 1; i <= 10; i++) {
          if (signal.aborted) return;
          await this.snapshotAndCommit(minuteOf(new Date(now - i * 60_000)));
        }
      });
    } catch (e) {
      if (!(e instanceof LockNotAcquiredError)) throw e;
    }
  }

  private async snapshotAndCommit(minute: string): Promise<void> {
    const src = AnKeys.views(minute);
    const dst = AnKeys.viewsFlush(minute, Date.now());
    await this.redis.sadd(AnKeys.flushing, dst); // record intent first
    const ok = await this.redis.renamenx(src, dst).catch((e: Error) => {
      if (/no such key/i.test(e.message)) return 0; // nothing to flush
      throw e;
    });
    if (!ok) {
      await this.redis.srem(AnKeys.flushing, dst);
      return;
    }
    await this.commit(dst);
  }

  private async commit(flushKey: string): Promise<void> {
    const m = /views:(\d{12}):flushing:/.exec(flushKey);
    if (!m) { await this.redis.srem(AnKeys.flushing, flushKey); return; }
    const minute = m[1];
    const bucket = new Date(Date.UTC(
      +minute.slice(0, 4), +minute.slice(4, 6) - 1, +minute.slice(6, 8),
      +minute.slice(8, 10), +minute.slice(10, 12),
    ));
    const data = await this.redis.hgetall(flushKey);
    const pages = Object.keys(data);

    await this.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
      const log = await tx.query(
        'INSERT INTO flush_log(batch_key) VALUES ($1) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING 1', [flushKey],
      );
      if (log.length === 0 || pages.length === 0) return; // already applied earlier
      await tx.query(
        `INSERT INTO page_views_minute (bucket, page, views)
         SELECT $1, p, v FROM unnest($2::text[], $3::bigint[]) AS t(p, v)
         ON CONFLICT (bucket, page) DO UPDATE SET views = page_views_minute.views + EXCLUDED.views`,
        [bucket, pages, pages.map((p) => data[p])],
      );
    });
    await this.redis.multi().del(flushKey).srem(AnKeys.flushing, flushKey).exec();
    this.logger.debug(`Flushed ${pages.length} pages for ${minute}`);
  }
}
```

### Failure handling

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Redis down | `track()` buffers up to 50k events, then drops. Analytics loss is bounded and acceptable; surface a "dropped events" metric. |
| API instance crash | Up to ~100 ms of buffered events lost. |
| Flusher crash after `RENAMENX` | The key name is in `shop:an:flushing`; the next run commits it (recovery loop). |
| Crash after PG commit, before `DEL` | Next run re-reads the batch; `flush_log` conflict skips the upsert, then `DEL` runs. No double counting. |
| Postgres down | Flush fails, batch stays in Redis (renamed key, tracked in the set). Retried each minute. Watch the 2-hour TTL on live keys and the size of the `flushing` set. |
| Late events for an already flushed minute | They create `views:{minute}` again; the next run flushes it as another batch and the additive upsert merges. Correct. |

### Security considerations

- Normalize and allow-list `page` values; cap field length (for example 200 chars) to prevent unbounded hash growth or memory abuse.
- Do not accept arbitrary client-provided `userId`; take it from the authenticated session. A malicious large `userId` in `SETBIT` could allocate hundreds of MB (bit offset 2^32 is 512 MB). Enforce an upper bound.
- The tracking endpoint is public: rate limit it, and consider bot filtering.
- Visitor ids in HLLs are hashed, not stored, which is privacy-friendly. Document retention.

### Performance considerations

- Pipelining plus client-side batching turns 20k events/s into roughly 200 round trips/s.
- `HINCRBY` on a small per-minute hash is O(1); `PFADD` O(1); `SETBIT` O(1) (amortized when the string grows).
- HLL: reads with `PFCOUNT` on one key are fast; multi-key `PFCOUNT` merges on the fly and costs more. Prefer `PFMERGE` into a rollup key for daily numbers.
- In Redis Cluster, `BITOP` and multi-key `PFCOUNT` require keys in one slot; use a hash tag such as `shop:an:{dau}:20261119` for bitmaps you intend to combine.

### Testing strategy

| Test | How |
|---|---|
| Counting | Track 1,000 events concurrently, assert `HGET` equals 1,000 |
| HLL accuracy | Add 100k distinct ids, assert `PFCOUNT` within 2% |
| Bitmap | Set bits 1, 5, 1000; `BITCOUNT` is 3; weekly OR combines days correctly |
| Flush idempotency | Run flush, simulate crash after commit (skip `DEL`), run again, assert PG value unchanged |
| Late data | Track into a flushed minute, flush again, assert PG sum is correct |
| Recovery | Manually create a `flushing` batch, run flusher, assert it is committed |

### Production deployment notes

- Analytics Redis can be separate and use `maxmemory` with `volatile-ttl`; every key has a TTL.
- Keep the flusher single-run via the lock (14.9); the lock TTL (50 s) must be below the cron interval.
- Alert on: size of `shop:an:flushing`, age of oldest unflushed minute, dropped-event counter.
- For heavy workloads, consider Redis Streams or Kafka as a durable ingest log; this design trades durability for simplicity and speed.
